class AdditiveSchemaEvolution:
    """
    Handles adding new columns to existing schemas while maintaining 
    backward compatibility.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def create_v1_schema(self):
        """Original schema version 1"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("username", StringType(), False),
            StructField("email", StringType(), True),
            StructField("created_at", TimestampType(), False)
        ])
    
    def create_v2_schema(self):
        """Enhanced schema version 2 - Added new fields"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("username", StringType(), False),
            StructField("email", StringType(), True),
            StructField("created_at", TimestampType(), False),
            # New additive fields
            StructField("phone_number", StringType(), True),  # NEW
            StructField("last_login", TimestampType(), True),  # NEW
            StructField("is_premium", BooleanType(), True),    # NEW
            StructField("preferences", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)  # NEW
        ])
    
    def generate_v1_data(self):
        """Generate sample data with v1 schema"""
        data = [
            ("U001", "alice", "alice@example.com", datetime(2023, 1, 1)),
            ("U002", "bob", "bob@example.com", datetime(2023, 1, 2)),
            ("U003", "charlie", "charlie@example.com", datetime(2023, 1, 3))
        ]
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, self.create_v1_schema())
    
    def evolve_to_v2(self, df_v1):
        """
        Evolve v1 DataFrame to v2 schema by adding new columns with defaults
        """
        df_v2 = df_v1 \
            .withColumn("phone_number", lit(None).cast(StringType())) \
            .withColumn("last_login", lit(None).cast(TimestampType())) \
            .withColumn("is_premium", lit(False)) \
            .withColumn("preferences", lit(None).cast(MapType(StringType(), StringType())))
        
        return df_v2
    
    def generate_v2_data(self):
        """Generate sample data with v2 schema"""
        data = [
            ("U004", "david", "david@example.com", datetime(2023, 2, 1),
             "+1234567890", datetime(2023, 2, 15), True, {"theme": "dark", "lang": "en"}),
            ("U005", "eve", "eve@example.com", datetime(2023, 2, 2),
             "+0987654321", datetime(2023, 2, 16), False, {"theme": "light", "lang": "es"})
        ]
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, self.create_v2_schema())
    
    def merge_versions(self, df_v1, df_v2):
        """
        Merge data from different schema versions
        """
        # Evolve v1 to v2 schema
        df_v1_evolved = self.evolve_to_v2(df_v1)
        
        # Union both DataFrames
        merged_df = df_v1_evolved.union(df_v2)
        
        return merged_df
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate additive schema evolution"""
        print("\n--- Original V1 Data ---")
        df_v1 = self.generate_v1_data()
        df_v1.show(truncate=False)
        df_v1.printSchema()
        
        print("\n--- New V2 Data ---")
        df_v2 = self.generate_v2_data()
        df_v2.show(truncate=False)
        df_v2.printSchema()
        
        print("\n--- Merged Data (V1 evolved to V2) ---")
        merged = self.merge_versions(df_v1, df_v2)
        merged.show(truncate=False)
        merged.printSchema()
        
        return merged

# Execute Pattern 1

additive_result = additive_pattern.demonstrate()

class SubtractiveSchemaEvolution:
    """
    Handles removing columns from schemas with proper migration strategy
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def create_full_schema(self):
        """Original schema with all fields"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("transaction_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("currency", StringType(), False),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            # Fields to be removed
            StructField("credit_card_number", StringType(), True),  # DEPRECATED - Security
            StructField("cvv", StringType(), True),                 # DEPRECATED - Security
            StructField("legacy_field", StringType(), True)         # DEPRECATED - No longer used
        ])
    
    def create_reduced_schema(self):
        """Reduced schema after removing sensitive/deprecated fields"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("transaction_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("currency", StringType(), False),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False),
            # Replacement for removed fields
            StructField("payment_token", StringType(), True)  # Tokenized payment info
        ])
    
    def generate_full_data(self):
        """Generate data with full schema"""
        data = [
            ("T001", "U001", 100.0, "USD", datetime(2023, 1, 1), 
             "4532-1234-5678-9010", "123", "legacy_value_1"),
            ("T002", "U002", 200.0, "EUR", datetime(2023, 1, 2), 
             "5432-9876-5432-1098", "456", "legacy_value_2")
        ]
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, self.create_full_schema())
    
    def migrate_to_reduced_schema(self, df_full):
        """
        Migrate from full schema to reduced schema
        Strategy: Hash sensitive data before removal
        """
        from pyspark.sql.functions import sha2, concat_ws
        
        # Create payment token from sensitive data before removal
        df_migrated = df_full \
            .withColumn("payment_token", 
                       sha2(concat_ws("-", col("credit_card_number"), col("cvv")), 256)) \
            .drop("credit_card_number", "cvv", "legacy_field")
        
        return df_migrated
    
    def archive_removed_fields(self, df_full, archive_path="/tmp/archive"):
        """
        Archive removed fields separately for compliance/audit
        """
        # Extract only the fields being removed
        df_archive = df_full.select(
            "transaction_id",
            "credit_card_number",
            "cvv",
            "legacy_field",
            current_timestamp().alias("archived_at")
        )
        
        print(f"\n--- Archiving removed fields to: {archive_path} ---")
        # In production, write to secure storage
        # df_archive.write.mode("append").parquet(archive_path)
        df_archive.show(truncate=False)
        
        return df_archive
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate subtractive schema evolution"""
        print("\n--- Original Data (Full Schema) ---")
        df_full = self.generate_full_data()
        df_full.show(truncate=False)
        df_full.printSchema()
        
        print("\n--- Archive Removed Fields ---")
        self.archive_removed_fields(df_full)
        
        print("\n--- Migrated Data (Reduced Schema) ---")
        df_reduced = self.migrate_to_reduced_schema(df_full)
        df_reduced.show(truncate=False)
        df_reduced.printSchema()
        
        return df_reduced

# Execute Pattern 2

class ModificationSchemaEvolution:
    """
    Handles modifying existing field types and constraints
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def create_v1_schema(self):
        """Original schema with initial types"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("product_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("price", IntegerType(), False),        # Will change to Double
            StructField("quantity", StringType(), False),      # Will change to Integer
            StructField("active", StringType(), True),         # Will change to Boolean
            StructField("metadata", StringType(), True)        # Will change to Map
        ])
    
    def create_v2_schema(self):
        """Modified schema with updated types"""
        return StructType([
            StructField("product_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("price", DoubleType(), False),         # MODIFIED: Int -> Double
            StructField("quantity", IntegerType(), False),     # MODIFIED: String -> Int
            StructField("active", BooleanType(), True),        # MODIFIED: String -> Boolean
            StructField("metadata", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)  # MODIFIED
        ])
    
    def generate_v1_data(self):
        """Generate data with v1 schema"""
        data = [
            ("P001", "Laptop", 999, "10", "true", '{"brand": "Dell"}'),
            ("P002", "Mouse", 25, "50", "false", '{"brand": "Logitech"}'),
            ("P003", "Keyboard", 75, "30", "true", '{"brand": "Microsoft"}')
        ]
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, self.create_v1_schema())
    
    def transform_v1_to_v2(self, df_v1):
        """
        Transform v1 data to v2 schema with type conversions
        """
        df_v2 = df_v1 \
            .withColumn("price", col("price").cast(DoubleType())) \
            .withColumn("quantity", col("quantity").cast(IntegerType())) \
            .withColumn("active", 
                       when(col("active") == "true", True)
                       .when(col("active") == "false", False)
                       .otherwise(None)) \
            .withColumn("metadata", from_json(col("metadata"), 
                                             MapType(StringType(), StringType())))
        
        return df_v2
    
    def validate_transformation(self, df_v1, df_v2):
        """
        Validate that transformation was successful
        """
        print("\n--- Validation Results ---")
        
        # Check for null values introduced by failed conversions
        null_counts = df_v2.select([
            sum(col(c).isNull().cast("int")).alias(c) 
            for c in df_v2.columns
        ])
        
        print("Null counts after transformation:")
        null_counts.show()
        
        # Compare row counts
        v1_count = df_v1.count()
        v2_count = df_v2.count()
        print(f"V1 row count: {v1_count}, V2 row count: {v2_count}")
        print(f"Data integrity: {'✓ PASSED' if v1_count == v2_count else '✗ FAILED'}")
        
        return v1_count == v2_count
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate modification schema evolution"""
        print("\n--- Original V1 Data ---")
        df_v1 = self.generate_v1_data()
        df_v1.show(truncate=False)
        df_v1.printSchema()
        
        print("\n--- Transformed V2 Data ---")
        df_v2 = self.transform_v1_to_v2(df_v1)
        df_v2.show(truncate=False)
        df_v2.printSchema()
        
        self.validate_transformation(df_v1, df_v2)
        
        return df_v2

# Execute Pattern 3

modification_result = modification_pattern.demonstrate()

    def normalize_to_latest_schema(self, df, source_version, target_version):
        """
        Normalize any version to the latest schema
        """
        if source_version == "1.0" and target_version == "3.0":
            # Add all missing fields from v2 and v3
            df = df \
                .withColumn("session_id", lit(None).cast(StringType())) \
                .withColumn("device_info", lit(None).cast(
                    StructType([
                        StructField("device_type", StringType(), True),
                        StructField("os", StringType(), True),
                        StructField("browser", StringType(), True)
                    ]))) \
                .withColumn("geo_location", lit(None).cast(
                    StructType([
                        StructField("country", StringType(), True),
                        StructField("city", StringType(), True)
                    ])))
        
        elif source_version == "2.0" and target_version == "3.0":
            # Add browser to device_info and geo_location
            df = df \
                .withColumn("device_info", 
                           when(col("device_info").isNotNull(),
                                struct(
                                    col("device_info.device_type").alias("device_type"),
                                    col("device_info.os").alias("os"),
                                    lit(None).cast(StringType()).alias("browser")
                                ))
                           .otherwise(None)) \
                .withColumn("geo_location", lit(None).cast(
                    StructType([
                        StructField("country", StringType(), True),
                        StructField("city", StringType(), True)
                    ])))
        
        return df
    
    def merge_compatible_versions(self, dfs_with_versions):
        """
        Merge multiple DataFrames with different compatible schema versions
        """
        target_version = "3.0"
        normalized_dfs = []
        
        for df, version in dfs_with_versions:
            if version != target_version:
                df = self.normalize_to_latest_schema(df, version, target_version)
            normalized_dfs.append(df)
        
        # Union all normalized DataFrames
        result = normalized_dfs[0]
        for df in normalized_dfs[1:]:
            result = result.union(df)
        
        return result
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate compatible evolution pattern"""

        print("\n--- V3.0 Data (Further Compatible Addition) ---")
        df_v3 = self.generate_v3_data()
        df_v3.show(truncate=False)

        print("\n--- Merged Compatible Versions ---")

            (df_v1, "1.0"),

        ])

        print("\n--- Compatibility Check ---")

        print(f"V2.0 records: {merged.filter(col('schema_version') == '2.0').count()}")
        print(f"V3.0 records: {merged.filter(col('schema_version') == '3.0').count()}")
        
        return merged

    def migrate_legacy_to_new(self, df_legacy):

        import uuid
        
        # UDF to generate UUID from integer ID

    def create_migration_report(self, df_legacy, df_migrated):
        """
        Generate migration report to track the breaking changes
        """
        print("\n--- Migration Report ---")
        
        legacy_count = df_legacy.count()
        migrated_count = df_migrated.count()
        
        print(f"Legacy records: {legacy_count}")
        print(f"Migrated records: {migrated_count}")
        print(f"Migration success rate: {(migrated_count/legacy_count)*100:.2f}%")
        
        # Check for data quality issues
        print("\n--- Data Quality Checks ---")
        
        null_checks = df_migrated.select([
            sum(when(col("customer_uuid").isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("null_uuid"),
            sum(when(col("first_name").isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("null_first_name"),
            sum(when(col("last_name").isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("null_last_name"),
            sum(when(col("address").isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("null_address"),
            sum(when(col("contact_info").isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("null_contact")
        ])
        
        null_checks.show()
        
        # Create mapping table for ID conversion
        mapping_df = df_legacy.select("id") \
            .withColumn("customer_uuid", 
                       self.generate_uuid_for_mapping(col("id")))
        
        print("\n--- Legacy ID to UUID Mapping (Sample) ---")
        mapping_df.show(5)
        
        return mapping_df
    
    def generate_uuid_for_mapping(self, id_col):
        """Helper function for UUID generation in mapping"""
        from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
        from pyspark.sql.types import StringType
        import uuid
        
        @udf(StringType())
        def gen_uuid(old_id):
            return str(uuid.uuid5(uuid.NAMESPACE_DNS, f"customer_{old_id}"))
        
        return gen_uuid(id_col)
    
    def dual_write_strategy(self, df_legacy):
        """
        Demonstrate dual-write strategy during migration period
        Write to both legacy and new systems
        """
        print("\n--- Dual Write Strategy ---")
        print("Writing to both legacy and new schemas during transition...")
        
        # Write to legacy format
        print("\n1. Writing to legacy system...")
        # df_legacy.write.mode("append").parquet("/tmp/legacy_data")
        print("   ✓ Legacy write complete")
        
        # Migrate and write to new format
        print("\n2. Migrating and writing to new system...")
        df_new = self.migrate_legacy_to_new(df_legacy)
        # df_new.write.mode("append").parquet("/tmp/new_data")
        print("   ✓ New system write complete")
        
        print("\n3. Dual write completed successfully")
        
        return df_new
    
    def rollback_strategy(self, df_migrated):
        """
        Demonstrate rollback capability for breaking changes
        """
        print("\n--- Rollback Strategy ---")
        print("Converting new schema back to legacy format...")
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import concat_ws, monotonically_increasing_id
        
        # Attempt to reconstruct legacy format
        df_rollback = df_migrated \
            .withColumn("id", monotonically_increasing_id().cast(IntegerType())) \
            .withColumn("full_name", concat_ws(" ", col("first_name"), col("last_name"))) \
            .withColumn("address", 
                       concat_ws(", ",
                                col("address.street"),
                                col("address.city"),
                                concat_ws(" ", col("address.state"), col("address.zip_code")))) \
            .withColumn("contact", col("contact_info.email")) \
            .withColumn("account_balance", col("account_balance").cast(IntegerType())) \
            .withColumn("status", col("account_status.code")) \
            .select("id", "full_name", "address", "contact", "account_balance", "status")
        
        print("Rollback schema:")
        df_rollback.printSchema()
        df_rollback.show(truncate=False)
        
        return df_rollback
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate breaking evolution pattern"""
        print("\n--- Legacy Schema and Data ---")
        df_legacy = self.generate_legacy_data()

        # Demonstrate rollback capability

        return df_migrated

class SchemaEvolutionFramework:
    """
    Unified framework for managing all types of schema evolution
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        self.version_history = []
        self.migration_logs = []
        
    def detect_evolution_type(self, old_schema, new_schema):
        """
        Automatically detect the type of schema evolution
        """
        old_fields = {f.name: f for f in old_schema.fields}
        new_fields = {f.name: f for f in new_schema.fields}
        
        added_fields = set(new_fields.keys()) - set(old_fields.keys())
        removed_fields = set(old_fields.keys()) - set(new_fields.keys())
        common_fields = set(old_fields.keys()) & set(new_fields.keys())
        
        modified_fields = []
        for field_name in common_fields:
            if old_fields[field_name].dataType != new_fields[field_name].dataType:
                modified_fields.append(field_name)
        
        evolution_type = []
        
        if added_fields:
            evolution_type.append("ADDITIVE")
            print(f"\nAdded fields: {added_fields}")
        
        if removed_fields:
            evolution_type.append("SUBTRACTIVE")
            print(f"\nRemoved fields: {removed_fields}")
        
        if modified_fields:
            evolution_type.append("MODIFICATION")
            print(f"\nModified fields: {modified_fields}")
        
        # Determine if changes are compatible or breaking
        is_breaking = bool(removed_fields or modified_fields)
        
        if is_breaking:
            evolution_type.append("BREAKING")
        else:
            evolution_type.append("COMPATIBLE")
        
        return {
            "types": evolution_type,
            "added": list(added_fields),
            "removed": list(removed_fields),
            "modified": modified_fields,
            "is_breaking": is_breaking
        }
    
    def create_migration_plan(self, evolution_info):
        """
        Create an automated migration plan based on evolution type
        """
        plan = {
            "steps": [],
            "estimated_duration": "Unknown",
            "risk_level": "Low"
        }
        
        if "ADDITIVE" in evolution_info["types"]:
            plan["steps"].append({
                "step": 1,
                "action": "Add new columns with default values",
                "fields": evolution_info["added"],
                "risk": "Low"
            })
        
        if "SUBTRACTIVE" in evolution_info["types"]:
            plan["steps"].append({
                "step": 2,
                "action": "Archive removed fields before deletion",
                "fields": evolution_info["removed"],
                "risk": "Medium"
            })
            plan["risk_level"] = "Medium"
        
        if "MODIFICATION" in evolution_info["types"]:
            plan["steps"].append({
                "step": 3,
                "action": "Transform field types with validation",
                "fields": evolution_info["modified"],
                "risk": "High"
            })
            plan["risk_level"] = "High"
        
        if evolution_info["is_breaking"]:
            plan["steps"].append({
                "step": 4,
                "action": "Implement dual-write strategy",
                "description": "Write to both old and new schemas during transition",
                "risk": "High"
            })
            plan["steps"].append({
                "step": 5,
                "action": "Create rollback mechanism",
                "description": "Prepare rollback scripts for emergency recovery",
                "risk": "Critical"
            })
        
        return plan
    
    def execute_migration(self, df, old_schema, new_schema, migration_plan):
        """
        Execute the migration plan
        """
        print("\n--- Executing Migration Plan ---")
        
        for step in migration_plan["steps"]:
            print(f"\nStep {step['step']}: {step['action']}")
            print(f"Risk Level: {step['risk']}")
        
        # This is a simplified execution - in production, each step would be detailed
        evolution_info = self.detect_evolution_type(old_schema, new_schema)
        
        if "ADDITIVE" in evolution_info["types"]:
            # Add new fields
            for field in evolution_info["added"]:
                df = df.withColumn(field, lit(None))
        
        print("\n✓ Migration executed successfully")
        return df
    
    def log_migration(self, version_from, version_to, evolution_info, success):
        """
        Log migration for audit trail
        """
        log_entry = {
            "timestamp": datetime.now(),
            "version_from": version_from,
            "version_to": version_to,
            "evolution_type": evolution_info["types"],
            "changes": {
                "added": evolution_info["added"],
                "removed": evolution_info["removed"],
                "modified": evolution_info["modified"]
            },
            "success": success,
            "is_breaking": evolution_info["is_breaking"]
        }
        
        self.migration_logs.append(log_entry)
        
        print("\n--- Migration Log Entry ---")
        print(json.dumps({k: str(v) for k, v in log_entry.items()}, indent=2))
    
    def generate_schema_diff_report(self, old_schema, new_schema):
        """
        Generate a detailed diff report between schemas
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("SCHEMA DIFF REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        evolution_info = self.detect_evolution_type(old_schema, new_schema)
        
        print(f"\nEvolution Type: {', '.join(evolution_info['types'])}")
        print(f"Breaking Change: {'YES' if evolution_info['is_breaking'] else 'NO'}")
        
        if evolution_info["added"]:
            print(f"\n✓ Added Fields ({len(evolution_info['added'])}):")
            for field in evolution_info["added"]:
                print(f"  + {field}")
        
        if evolution_info["removed"]:
            print(f"\n✗ Removed Fields ({len(evolution_info['removed'])}):")
            for field in evolution_info["removed"]:
                print(f"  - {field}")
        
        if evolution_info["modified"]:
            print(f"\n⚠ Modified Fields ({len(evolution_info['modified'])}):")
            for field in evolution_info["modified"]:
                print(f"  ~ {field}")
        
        return evolution_info
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate the comprehensive framework"""
        print("\n--- Framework Demonstration ---")
        
        # Create sample schemas
        old_schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        
        new_schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), False),  # Modified
            StructField("description", StringType(), True),  # Added
            StructField("tags", ArrayType(StringType()), True)  # Added
        ])
        
        # Generate diff report
        evolution_info = self.generate_schema_diff_report(old_schema, new_schema)
        
        # Create migration plan
        print("\n--- Migration Plan ---")
        plan = self.create_migration_plan(evolution_info)
        print(json.dumps(plan, indent=2))
        
        # Create sample data
        data = [(1, "Item1", 100), (2, "Item2", 200)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, old_schema)
        
        # Execute migration
        df_migrated = self.execute_migration(df, old_schema, new_schema, plan)
        
        # Log the migration
        self.log_migration("1.0", "2.0", evolution_info, True)
        
        return df_migrated

# Execute Comprehensive Framework
framework = SchemaEvolutionFramework(spark)
framework_result = framework.demonstrate()

class PracticalUseCases:

    def use_case_1_gdpr_compliance(self):
        """
        Use Case 1: GDPR Compliance - Remove PII fields
        Pattern: Subtractive + Breaking Evolution
        """
        print("\n--- Use Case 1: GDPR Compliance ---")
        print("Scenario: Remove PII fields to comply with data retention policies")
        
        # Original schema with PII
        schema_with_pii = StructType([
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("email", StringType(), True),
            StructField("ip_address", StringType(), True),
            StructField("device_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("session_data", StringType(), True),
            StructField("anonymized_id", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        # Compliant schema without PII
        schema_compliant = StructType([
            StructField("anonymized_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("session_hash", StringType(), True),
            StructField("retention_date", TimestampType(), False)
        ])
        
        # Sample data
        data = [
            ("U001", "user1@example.com", "192.168.1.1", "DEV001", "session_xyz", "ANON001"),
            ("U002", "user2@example.com", "192.168.1.2", "DEV002", "session_abc", "ANON002")
        ]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema_with_pii)
        
        print("\nOriginal data with PII:")
        df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Anonymization process
        from pyspark.sql.functions import sha2, concat_ws, add_months, current_date
        
        df_compliant = df.select(
            col("anonymized_id"),
            sha2(col("session_data"), 256).alias("session_hash"),
            add_months(current_date(), 12).alias("retention_date")
        )
        
        print("\nGDPR compliant data:")
        df_compliant.show(truncate=False)
        df_compliant.printSchema()
        
        # Archive PII separately with encryption (simulated)
        df_pii_archive = df.select(
            col("user_id"),
            sha2(col("email"), 256).alias("email_hash"),
            sha2(col("ip_address"), 256).alias("ip_hash"),
            current_timestamp().alias("archived_at"),
            add_months(current_date(), 3).alias("delete_after")
        )
        
        print("\nArchived PII (hashed for security):")
        df_pii_archive.show(truncate=False)
        
        return df_compliant

class SchemaEvolutionTester:
    """
    Automated testing framework for schema evolution
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        self.test_results = []
    
    def test_backward_compatibility(self, old_schema, new_schema):
        """
        Test if new schema is backward compatible with old schema
        """
        print("\n--- Testing Backward Compatibility ---")
        
        old_fields = {f.name: f for f in old_schema.fields}
        new_fields = {f.name: f for f in new_schema.fields}
        
        issues = []
        
        # Check if any required fields were removed
        for field_name, field in old_fields.items():
            if not field.nullable and field_name not in new_fields:
                issues.append(f"Required field '{field_name}' was removed")
        
        # Check if any field types changed incompatibly
        for field_name in set(old_fields.keys()) & set(new_fields.keys()):
            old_type = old_fields[field_name].dataType
            new_type = new_fields[field_name].dataType
            
            if str(old_type) != str(new_type):
                if not self._is_compatible_type_change(old_type, new_type):
                    issues.append(
                        f"Incompatible type change for '{field_name}': "
                        f"{old_type} -> {new_type}"
                    )
        
        is_compatible = len(issues) == 0
        
        result = {
            "test": "backward_compatibility",
            "passed": is_compatible,
            "issues": issues
        }
        
        self.test_results.append(result)
        
        if is_compatible:
            print("✓ PASSED: Schema is backward compatible")
        else:
            print("✗ FAILED: Schema has backward compatibility issues:")
            for issue in issues:
                print(f"  - {issue}")
        
        return is_compatible
    
    def test_forward_compatibility(self, old_schema, new_schema):
        """
        Test if old schema can read data written with new schema
        """
        print("\n--- Testing Forward Compatibility ---")
        
        old_fields = {f.name: f for f in old_schema.fields}
        new_fields = {f.name: f for f in new_schema.fields}
        
        issues = []
        
        # Check if new required fields were added
        for field_name, field in new_fields.items():
            if not field.nullable and field_name not in old_fields:
                issues.append(
                    f"New required field '{field_name}' added - "
                    f"old readers cannot provide value"
                )
        
        is_compatible = len(issues) == 0
        
        result = {
            "test": "forward_compatibility",
            "passed": is_compatible,
            "issues": issues
        }
        
        self.test_results.append(result)
        
        if is_compatible:
            print("✓ PASSED: Schema is forward compatible")
        else:
            print("✗ FAILED: Schema has forward compatibility issues:")
            for issue in issues:
                print(f"  - {issue}")
        
        return is_compatible
    
    def _is_compatible_type_change(self, old_type, new_type):
        """
        Check if type change is compatible
        """
        compatible_changes = {
            "IntegerType": ["LongType", "DoubleType", "DecimalType"],
            "FloatType": ["DoubleType", "DecimalType"],
            "StringType": ["StringType"]  # String is always compatible with itself
        }
        
        old_type_name = type(old_type).__name__
        new_type_name = type(new_type).__name__
        
        if old_type_name == new_type_name:
            return True
        
        return new_type_name in compatible_changes.get(old_type_name, [])
    
    def test_data_integrity(self, df_old, df_new):
        """
        Test data integrity after schema evolution
        """
        print("\n--- Testing Data Integrity ---")
        
        issues = []
        
        # Test row count preservation
        old_count = df_old.count()
        new_count = df_new.count()
        
        if old_count != new_count:
            issues.append(f"Row count mismatch: {old_count} -> {new_count}")
        
        # Test for unexpected nulls in non-nullable fields
        for field in df_new.schema.fields:
            if not field.nullable:
                null_count = df_new.filter(col(field.name).isNull()).count()
                if null_count > 0:
                    issues.append(
                        f"Found {null_count} null values in "
                        f"non-nullable field '{field.name}'"
                    )
        
        is_valid = len(issues) == 0
        
        result = {
            "test": "data_integrity",
            "passed": is_valid,
            "issues": issues,
            "old_count": old_count,
            "new_count": new_count
        }
        
        self.test_results.append(result)
        
        if is_valid:
            print(f"✓ PASSED: Data integrity maintained ({old_count} rows)")
        else:
            print("✗ FAILED: Data integrity issues found:")
            for issue in issues:
                print(f"  - {issue}")
        
        return is_valid
    
    def test_performance_impact(self, df_old, df_new):
        """
        Test performance impact of schema evolution
        """
        print("\n--- Testing Performance Impact ---")
        
        import time
        
        # Test old schema query performance
        start = time.time()
        df_old.select("*").count()
        old_time = time.time() - start
        
        # Test new schema query performance
        start = time.time()
        df_new.select("*").count()
        new_time = time.time() - start
        
        performance_degradation = ((new_time - old_time) / old_time) * 100
        
        threshold = 20  # 20% degradation threshold
        is_acceptable = performance_degradation < threshold
        
        result = {
            "test": "performance_impact",
            "passed": is_acceptable,
            "old_time_ms": old_time * 1000,
            "new_time_ms": new_time * 1000,
            "degradation_percent": performance_degradation
        }
        
        self.test_results.append(result)
        
        if is_acceptable:
            print(f"✓ PASSED: Performance impact acceptable "
                  f"({performance_degradation:.2f}% change)")
        else:
            print(f"✗ FAILED: Performance degradation too high "
                  f"({performance_degradation:.2f}%)")
        
        return is_acceptable
    
    def generate_test_report(self):
        """
        Generate comprehensive test report
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("SCHEMA EVOLUTION TEST REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        total_tests = len(self.test_results)
        passed_tests = sum(1 for r in self.test_results if r['passed'])
        
        print(f"\nTotal Tests: {total_tests}")
        print(f"Passed: {passed_tests}")
        print(f"Failed: {total_tests - passed_tests}")
        print(f"Success Rate: {(passed_tests/total_tests)*100:.2f}%")
        
        print("\n--- Detailed Results ---")
        for result in self.test_results:
            status = "✓ PASS" if result['passed'] else "✗ FAIL"
            print(f"\n{status}: {result['test']}")
            
            if 'issues' in result and result['issues']:
                for issue in result['issues']:
                    print(f"  - {issue}")
        
        return self.test_results
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate testing framework"""
        # Create test schemas
        old_schema = StructType([
            StructField("
```python
id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", IntegerType(), False)
        ])
        
        new_schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), False),  # Type changed
            StructField("description", StringType(), True),  # Added field
            StructField("tags", ArrayType(StringType()), True)  # Added field
        ])
        
        # Create test data
        data = [(1, "Item1", 100), (2, "Item2", 200), (3, "Item3", 300)]
        df_old = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, old_schema)
        
        # Evolve to new schema
        df_new = df_old \
            .withColumn("value", col("value").cast(DoubleType())) \
            .withColumn("description", lit(None).cast(StringType())) \
            .withColumn("tags", lit(None).cast(ArrayType(StringType())))
        
        # Run all tests
        self.test_backward_compatibility(old_schema, new_schema)
        self.test_forward_compatibility(old_schema, new_schema)
        self.test_data_integrity(df_old, df_new)
        self.test_performance_impact(df_old, df_new)
        
        # Generate report
        return self.generate_test_report()

# Execute Testing Framework
tester = SchemaEvolutionTester(spark)

print("\n" + "=" * 80)
print("SCHEMA VERSIONING AND REGISTRY")
print("=" * 80)

class SchemaRegistry:
    """
    Schema registry for managing and versioning schemas
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        self.schemas = {}
        self.version_history = []
        self.compatibility_mode = "BACKWARD"  # BACKWARD, FORWARD, FULL, NONE
    
    def register_schema(self, subject, version, schema, description=""):
        """
        Register a new schema version
        """
        if subject not in self.schemas:
            self.schemas[subject] = {}
        
        # Check compatibility with previous version
        if version > 1:
            prev_version = version - 1
            if prev_version in self.schemas[subject]:
                prev_schema = self.schemas[subject][prev_version]['schema']
                is_compatible = self._check_compatibility(prev_schema, schema)
                
                if not is_compatible and self.compatibility_mode != "NONE":
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"Schema version {version} is not compatible with "
                        f"version {prev_version} under {self.compatibility_mode} mode"
                    )
        
        # Register schema
        self.schemas[subject][version] = {
            'schema': schema,
            'description': description,
            'registered_at': datetime.now(),
            'status': 'ACTIVE'
        }
        
        # Add to version history
        self.version_history.append({
            'subject': subject,
            'version': version,
            'timestamp': datetime.now(),
            'action': 'REGISTERED'
        })
        
        print(f"✓ Registered schema: {subject} v{version}")
        
        return True
    
    def get_schema(self, subject, version=None):
        """
        Retrieve a schema by subject and version
        """
        if subject not in self.schemas:
            raise ValueError(f"Subject '{subject}' not found")
        
        if version is None:
            # Get latest version
            version = max(self.schemas[subject].keys())
        
        if version not in self.schemas[subject]:
            raise ValueError(f"Version {version} not found for subject '{subject}'")
        
        return self.schemas[subject][version]['schema']
    
    def list_versions(self, subject):
        """
        List all versions for a subject
        """
        if subject not in self.schemas:
            return []
        
        versions = []
        for version, info in sorted(self.schemas[subject].items()):
            versions.append({
                'version': version,
                'description': info['description'],
                'registered_at': info['registered_at'],
                'status': info['status']
            })
        
        return versions
    
    def deprecate_version(self, subject, version):
        """
        Deprecate a schema version
        """
        if subject in self.schemas and version in self.schemas[subject]:
            self.schemas[subject][version]['status'] = 'DEPRECATED'
            
            self.version_history.append({
                'subject': subject,
                'version': version,
                'timestamp': datetime.now(),
                'action': 'DEPRECATED'
            })
            
            print(f"✓ Deprecated schema: {subject} v{version}")
            return True
        
        return False
    
    def _check_compatibility(self, old_schema, new_schema):
        """
        Check schema compatibility based on mode
        """
        if self.compatibility_mode == "NONE":
            return True
        
        tester = SchemaEvolutionTester(self.spark)
        
        if self.compatibility_mode == "BACKWARD":
            return tester.test_backward_compatibility(old_schema, new_schema)
        elif self.compatibility_mode == "FORWARD":
            return tester.test_forward_compatibility(old_schema, new_schema)
        elif self.compatibility_mode == "FULL":
            backward = tester.test_backward_compatibility(old_schema, new_schema)
            forward = tester.test_forward_compatibility(old_schema, new_schema)
            return backward and forward
        
        return False
    
    def export_schema_to_json(self, subject, version):
        """
        Export schema to JSON format
        """
        schema = self.get_schema(subject, version)
        
        def schema_to_dict(schema):
            """Convert StructType to dictionary"""
            if isinstance(schema, StructType):
                return {
                    "type": "struct",
                    "fields": [
                        {
                            "name": f.name,
                            "type": schema_to_dict(f.dataType) if isinstance(f.dataType, StructType) else str(f.dataType),
                            "nullable": f.nullable
                        }
                        for f in schema.fields
                    ]
                }
            return str(schema)
        
        schema_dict = schema_to_dict(schema)
        return json.dumps(schema_dict, indent=2)
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate schema registry"""
        print("\n--- Schema Registry Demonstration ---")
        
        # Register schemas
        schema_v1 = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False)
        ])
        
        schema_v2 = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("email", StringType(), True)  # Added field
        ])
        
        schema_v3 = StructType([
            StructField("id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("email", StringType(), True),
            StructField("phone", StringType(), True)  # Added field
        ])
        
        # Register versions
        self.register_schema("user", 1, schema_v1, "Initial user schema")
        self.register_schema("user", 2, schema_v2, "Added email field")
        self.register_schema("user", 3, schema_v3, "Added phone field")
        
        # List versions
        print("\n--- Schema Versions for 'user' ---")
        versions = self.list_versions("user")
        for v in versions:
            print(f"Version {v['version']}: {v['description']} "
                  f"({v['status']}) - {v['registered_at']}")
        
        # Export schema
        print("\n--- Exported Schema (JSON) ---")
        json_schema = self.export_schema_to_json("user", 3)
        print(json_schema)
        
        # Deprecate old version
        print("\n--- Deprecating Version 1 ---")
        self.deprecate_version("user", 1)
        
        # Show version history
        print("\n--- Version History ---")
        for entry in self.version_history:
            print(f"{entry['timestamp']}: {entry['action']} - "
                  f"{entry['subject']} v{entry['version']}")
        
        return self.schemas

# Execute Schema Registry
registry = SchemaRegistry(spark)
registry_result = registry.demonstrate()

class AdvancedSchemaUtilities:
    """
    Advanced utilities for schema evolution
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def schema_diff(self, schema1, schema2):
        """
        Generate detailed diff between two schemas
        """
        print("\n--- Schema Diff ---")
        
        fields1 = {f.name: f for f in schema1.fields}
        fields2 = {f.name: f for f in schema2.fields}
        
        diff = {
            'added': [],
            'removed': [],
            'modified': [],
            'unchanged': []
        }
        
        # Find added fields
        for name in set(fields2.keys()) - set(fields1.keys()):
            diff['added'].append({
                'name': name,
                'type': str(fields2[name].dataType),
                'nullable': fields2[name].nullable
            })
        
        # Find removed fields
        for name in set(fields1.keys()) - set(fields2.keys()):
            diff['removed'].append({
                'name': name,
                'type': str(fields1[name].dataType),
                'nullable': fields1[name].nullable
            })
        
        # Find modified fields
        for name in set(fields1.keys()) & set(fields2.keys()):
            f1 = fields1[name]
            f2 = fields2[name]
            
            if str(f1.dataType) != str(f2.dataType) or f1.nullable != f2.nullable:
                diff['modified'].append({
                    'name': name,
                    'old_type': str(f1.dataType),
                    'new_type': str(f2.dataType),
                    'old_nullable': f1.nullable,
                    'new_nullable': f2.nullable
                })
            else:
                diff['unchanged'].append(name)
        
        # Print diff
        if diff['added']:
            print(f"\n+ Added ({len(diff['added'])} fields):")
            for field in diff['added']:
                print(f"  + {field['name']}: {field['type']} "
                      f"({'nullable' if field['nullable'] else 'required'})")
        
        if diff['removed']:
            print(f"\n- Removed ({len(diff['removed'])} fields):")
            for field in diff['removed']:
                print(f"  - {field['name']}: {field['type']}")
        
        if diff['modified']:
            print(f"\n~ Modified ({len(diff['modified'])} fields):")
            for field in diff['modified']:
                print(f"  ~ {field['name']}: {field['old_type']} -> {field['new_type']}")
        
        print(f"\n= Unchanged: {len(diff['unchanged'])} fields")
        
        return diff
    
    def merge_schemas(self, *schemas):
        """
        Merge multiple schemas into a unified schema
        """
        print("\n--- Merging Schemas ---")
        
        all_fields = {}
        
        for schema in schemas:
            for field in schema.fields:
                if field.name not in all_fields:
                    all_fields[field.name] = field
                else:
                    # If field exists, make it nullable if any version is nullable
                    existing = all_fields[field.name]
                    if field.nullable or existing.nullable:
                        all_fields[field.name] = StructField(
                            field.name,
                            field.dataType,
                            True
                        )
        
        merged_schema = StructType(list(all_fields.values()))
        
        print(f"Merged {len(schemas)} schemas into {len(merged_schema.fields)} fields")
        merged_schema.printSchema()
        
        return merged_schema
    
    def validate_data_against_schema(self, df, expected_schema):
        """
        Validate DataFrame against expected schema
        """
        print("\n--- Validating Data Against Schema ---")
        
        issues = []
        
        # Check field names
        df_fields = set(df.columns)
        expected_fields = set(f.name for f in expected_schema.fields)
        
        missing_fields = expected_fields - df_fields
        extra_fields = df_fields - expected_fields
        
        if missing_fields:
            issues.append(f"Missing fields: {missing_fields}")
        
        if extra_fields:
            issues.append(f"Extra fields: {extra_fields}")
        
        # Check types for common fields
        for field in expected_schema.fields:
            if field.name in df.columns:
                df_type = str([f.dataType for f in df.schema.fields if f.name == field.name][0])
                expected_type = str(field.dataType)
                
                if df_type != expected_type:
                    issues.append(
                        f"Type mismatch for '{field.name}': "
                        f"expected {expected_type}, got {df_type}"
                    )
        
        is_valid = len(issues) == 0
        
        if is_valid:
            print("✓ Data validation PASSED")
        else:
            print("✗ Data validation FAILED:")
            for issue in issues:
                print(f"  - {issue}")
        
        return is_valid, issues
    
    def generate_migration_script(self, old_schema, new_schema, language="python"):
        """
        Auto-generate migration script
        """
        print(f"\n--- Generating {language.upper()} Migration Script ---")
        
        diff = self.schema_diff(old_schema, new_schema)
        
        if language == "python":
            script = "# Auto-generated migration script\n"
            script += "from pyspark.sql.functions import col, lit\n"
            script += "from pyspark.sql.types import *\n\n"
            script += "def migrate_schema(df):\n"
            script += "    # Apply schema evolution\n"
            
            # Add new fields
            for field in diff['added']:
                script += f"    df = df.withColumn('{field['name']}', "
                script += f"lit(None).cast({field['type']}))\n"
            
            # Remove old fields
            if diff['removed']:
                removed_names = [f['name'] for f in diff['removed']]
                script += f"    df = df.drop({', '.join([repr(n) for n in removed_names])})\n"
            
            # Modify fields
            for field in diff['modified']:
                script += f"    df = df.withColumn('{field['name']}', "
                script += f"col
```python
('{field['name']}').cast({field['new_type']}))\n"
            
            script += "    return df\n"
            
            print(script)
            return script
        
        return None
    
    def create_schema_evolution_dag(self, schema_versions):
        """
        Create a directed acyclic graph of schema evolution
        """
        print("\n--- Schema Evolution DAG ---")
        
        print("Schema Evolution Path:")
        for i, (version, schema) in enumerate(schema_versions.items()):
            field_count = len(schema.fields)
            if i == 0:
                print(f"v{version}: {field_count} fields (Initial)")
            else:
                prev_version = list(schema_versions.keys())[i-1]
                prev_count = len(schema_versions[prev_version].fields)
                change = field_count - prev_count
                change_str = f"+{change}" if change > 0 else str(change)
                print(f"  ↓")
                print(f"v{version}: {field_count} fields ({change_str} fields)")
        
        return True
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate advanced utilities"""
        # Create sample schemas
        schema_v1 = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        schema_v2 = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), True),  # Modified
            StructField("description", StringType(), True)  # Added
        ])
        
        schema_v3 = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("description", StringType(), True),
            StructField("tags", ArrayType(StringType()), True),  # Added
            StructField("metadata", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)  # Added
        ])
        
        # Demonstrate diff
        diff = self.schema_diff(schema_v1, schema_v2)
        
        # Demonstrate merge
        merged = self.merge_schemas(schema_v1, schema_v2, schema_v3)
        
        # Generate migration script
        script = self.generate_migration_script(schema_v1, schema_v2)
        
        # Create evolution DAG
        versions = {1: schema_v1, 2: schema_v2, 3: schema_v3}
        self.create_schema_evolution_dag(versions)
        
        # Validate data
        data = [(1, "Test", 100)]
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema_v1)
        is_valid, issues = self.validate_data_against_schema(df, schema_v1)
        
        return {
            'diff': diff,
            'merged_schema': merged,
            'migration_script': script
        }

class SchemaEvolutionMonitor:
    """
    Monitor schema changes and alert on issues
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        self.alerts = []
        self.metrics = {}
    
    def monitor_schema_changes(self, df_current, expected_schema):
        """
        Monitor for unexpected schema changes
        """
        print("\n--- Monitoring Schema Changes ---")
        
        current_schema = df_current.schema
        
        # Detect changes
        current_fields = {f.name: f for f in current_schema.fields}
        expected_fields = {f.name: f for f in expected_schema.fields}
        
        # Check for unexpected additions
        unexpected_adds = set(current_fields.keys()) - set(expected_fields.keys())
        if unexpected_adds:
            self._create_alert(
                "UNEXPECTED_FIELDS",
                f"Unexpected fields detected: {unexpected_adds}",
                "WARNING"
            )
        
        # Check for unexpected removals
        missing_fields = set(expected_fields.keys()) - set(current_fields.keys())
        if missing_fields:
            self._create_alert(
                "MISSING_FIELDS",
                f"Expected fields missing: {missing_fields}",
                "CRITICAL"
            )
        
        # Check for type mismatches
        for field_name in set(current_fields.keys()) & set(expected_fields.keys()):
            current_type = str(current_fields[field_name].dataType)
            expected_type = str(expected_fields[field_name].dataType)
            
            if current_type != expected_type:
                self._create_alert(
                    "TYPE_MISMATCH",
                    f"Type mismatch for '{field_name}': "
                    f"expected {expected_type}, got {current_type}",
                    "CRITICAL"
                )
        
        return len(self.alerts) == 0
    
    def monitor_data_quality(self, df):
        """
        Monitor data quality metrics
        """
        print("\n--- Monitoring Data Quality ---")
        
        metrics = {}
        
        # Calculate null percentages
        total_rows = df.count()
        
        for field in df.schema.fields:
            null_count = df.filter(col(field.name).isNull()).count()
            null_percentage = (null_count / total_rows) * 100 if total_rows > 0 else 0
            
            metrics[field.name] = {
                'null_count': null_count,
                'null_percentage': null_percentage
            }
            
            # Alert on high null percentage for non-nullable fields
            if not field.nullable and null_percentage > 0:
                self._create_alert(
                    "NULL_IN_REQUIRED_FIELD",
                    f"Field '{field.name}' has {null_percentage:.2f}% nulls "
                    f"but is marked as required",
                    "CRITICAL"
                )
            
            # Alert on suspiciously high null percentage
            if null_percentage > 50:
                self._create_alert(
                    "HIGH_NULL_PERCENTAGE",
                    f"Field '{field.name}' has {null_percentage:.2f}% nulls",
                    "WARNING"
                )
        
        self.metrics['data_quality'] = metrics
        
        print(f"Analyzed {len(metrics)} fields across {total_rows} rows")
        
        return metrics
    
    def monitor_schema_drift(self, df_current, df_baseline):
        """
        Detect schema drift from baseline
        """
        print("\n--- Monitoring Schema Drift ---")
        
        current_schema = df_current.schema
        baseline_schema = df_baseline.schema
        
        # Calculate drift score
        drift_score = 0
        max_score = 100
        
        current_fields = set(f.name for f in current_schema.fields)
        baseline_fields = set(f.name for f in baseline_schema.fields)
        
        # Penalize field additions/removals
        field_diff = len(current_fields.symmetric_difference(baseline_fields))
        drift_score += field_diff * 10
        
        # Penalize type changes
        for field in current_schema.fields:
            if field.name in [f.name for f in baseline_schema.fields]:
                baseline_field = [f for f in baseline_schema.fields if f.name == field.name][0]
                if str(field.dataType) != str(baseline_field.dataType):
                    drift_score += 15
        
        drift_percentage = min(drift_score, max_score)
        
        if drift_percentage > 30:
            self._create_alert(
                "SCHEMA_DRIFT",
                f"Schema drift detected: {drift_percentage}% deviation from baseline",
                "WARNING" if drift_percentage < 50 else "CRITICAL"
            )
        
        self.metrics['schema_drift'] = {
            'drift_percentage': drift_percentage,
            'field_differences': field_diff
        }
        
        print(f"Schema drift: {drift_percentage}%")
        
        return drift_percentage
    
    def _create_alert(self, alert_type, message, severity):
        """
        Create an alert
        """
        alert = {
            'timestamp': datetime.now(),
            'type': alert_type,
            'message': message,
            'severity': severity
        }
        
        self.alerts.append(alert)
        
        # Print alert
        icon = "🔴" if severity == "CRITICAL" else "🟡" if severity == "WARNING" else "🔵"
        print(f"{icon} [{severity}] {alert_type}: {message}")
    
    def get_alert_summary(self):
        """
        Get summary of all alerts
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("ALERT SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        if not self.alerts:
            print("\n✓ No alerts - All checks passed!")
            return
        
        critical = [a for a in self.alerts if a['severity'] == 'CRITICAL']
        warnings = [a for a in self.alerts if a['severity'] == 'WARNING']
        info = [a for a in self.alerts if a['severity'] == 'INFO']
        
        print(f"\nTotal Alerts: {len(self.alerts)}")
        print(f"  Critical: {len(critical)}")
        print(f"  Warnings: {len(warnings)}")
        print(f"  Info: {len(info)}")
        
        if critical:
            print("\n🔴 CRITICAL ALERTS:")
            for alert in critical:
                print(f"  [{alert['timestamp']}] {alert['type']}: {alert['message']}")
        
        if warnings:
            print("\n🟡 WARNINGS:")
            for alert in warnings:
                print(f"  [{alert['timestamp']}] {alert['type']}: {alert['message']}")
        
        return {
            'total': len(self.alerts),
            'critical': len(critical),
            'warnings': len(warnings),
            'info': len(info)
        }
    
    def demonstrate(self):
        """Demonstrate monitoring capabilities"""
        # Create baseline data
        baseline_schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
        ])
        
        baseline_data = [
            (1, "Item1", 100.0),
            (2, "Item2", 200.0),
            (3, "Item3", None)
        ]
        df_baseline = self.spark.createDataFrame(baseline_data, baseline_schema)
        
        # Create current data with changes
        current_schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", StringType(), True),  # Type changed!
            StructField("extra_field", StringType(), True)  # New field!
        ])
        
        current_data = [
            (1, "Item1", "100.0", "extra1"),
            (2, "Item2", None, None),  # Nulls introduced
            (3, "Item3", None, "extra3")
        ]
        df_current = self.spark.createDataFrame(current_data, current_schema)
        
        # Monitor changes
        self.monitor_schema_changes(df_current, baseline_schema)
        
        # Monitor data quality
        self.monitor_data_quality(df_current)
        
        # Monitor drift
        self.monitor_schema_drift(df_current, df_baseline)
        
        # Get summary
        return self.get_alert_summary()

# Execute Monitoring

    def generate_rollback_plan(self, old_schema, new_schema):

            "pre_rollback": [

    def _generate_validation_queries(self, old_schema, new_schema):
        """
        Generate validation queries for rollback
        """
        queries = []
        
        # Row count validation
        queries.append({
            "name": "Row Count Validation",
            "query": "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM old_table vs new_table",
            "expected": "Counts should match"
        })
        
        # Data integrity checks
        common_fields = set(f.name for f in old_schema.fields) & set(f.name for f in new_schema.fields)
        
        for field in common_fields:
            queries.append({
                "name": f"Field '{field}' Integrity",
                "query": f"SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT {field}) FROM old_table vs new_table",
                "expected": "Distinct counts should match"
            })
        
        return queries
