from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import (
    col, current_timestamp, window, from_json, to_timestamp,
    expr, lit, unix_timestamp, struct, to_json
)
from pyspark.sql.types import (
    StructType, StructField, StringType, TimestampType, 
    DoubleType, IntegerType, LongType
)
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import time

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 1: EVENT TIME SEMANTICS PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Uses the timestamp embedded in the event data itself
# Most accurate for out-of-order events and late arrivals

def event_time_semantics_pattern():
    """
    Event Time Semantics: Process events based on when they actually occurred
    Use Case: Financial transactions, IoT sensor readings, user activity logs
    """
    print("=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 1: EVENT TIME SEMANTICS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("EventTimeSemantics") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .config("spark.sql.streaming.schemaInference", "true") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")
    
    # Define schema with event timestamp
    event_schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("event_type", StringType(), True),
        StructField("event_timestamp", TimestampType(), True),  # Event time
        StructField("value", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("location", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    # Simulated streaming source (replace with actual source like Kafka)
    # For demo, we'll use rate source and transform it
    raw_stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 5) \
        .load()
    
    # Transform to simulate event data with event timestamps
    event_stream = raw_stream.selectExpr(
        "CAST(value AS STRING) as event_id",
        "CONCAT('user_', CAST(value % 100 AS STRING)) as user_id",
        "CASE WHEN value % 3 = 0 THEN 'purchase' " +
        "     WHEN value % 3 = 1 THEN 'click' " +
        "     ELSE 'view' END as event_type",
        # Simulate event time with some delay (events from the past)
        "CAST(timestamp - INTERVAL 5 SECONDS as TIMESTAMP) as event_timestamp",
        "CAST(value * 10.5 AS DOUBLE) as value",
        "CONCAT('location_', CAST(value % 10 AS STRING)) as location"
    )
    
    # Apply watermark for handling late events
    # Events arriving more than 10 seconds late will be dropped
    watermarked_stream = event_stream \
        .withWatermark("event_timestamp", "10 seconds")
    
    # Window aggregation based on event time
    windowed_aggregation = watermarked_stream \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_timestamp"), "30 seconds", "15 seconds"),  # Sliding window
            col("event_type")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as event_count"),
            expr("sum(value) as total_value"),
            expr("avg(value) as avg_value"),
            expr("min(event_timestamp) as earliest_event"),
            expr("max(event_timestamp) as latest_event")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("event_type"),
            col("event_count"),
            col("total_value"),
            col("avg_value"),
            col("earliest_event"),
            col("latest_event")
        )
    
    # Write to console for demonstration
    query = windowed_aggregation.writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .option("numRows", 20) \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Event Time Semantics stream started")
    print("  - Using event_timestamp for windowing")
    print("  - Watermark: 10 seconds")
    print("  - Window: 30 seconds sliding by 15 seconds")
    
    # Run for demo purposes
    query.awaitTermination(timeout=30)
    query.stop()
    spark.stop()
    
    return "Event Time Semantics Pattern Completed"


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 2: INGESTION TIME SEMANTICS PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Uses the timestamp when data enters the streaming system
# Good balance between accuracy and simplicity

def ingestion_time_semantics_pattern():
    """
    Ingestion Time Semantics: Process events based on when they arrive in the system
    Use Case: Log aggregation, metrics collection, monitoring systems
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 2: INGESTION TIME SEMANTICS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("IngestionTimeSemantics") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")
    
    # Define schema without ingestion timestamp (we'll add it)
    input_schema = StructType([
        StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("temperature", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("humidity", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("pressure", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    # Create streaming source
    raw_stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 10) \
        .load()
    
    # Add ingestion timestamp at the point of entry
    # This represents when the data enters our streaming pipeline
    ingestion_stream = raw_stream \
        .withColumn("ingestion_time", current_timestamp()) \
        .selectExpr(
            "CONCAT('sensor_', CAST(value % 50 AS STRING)) as sensor_id",
            "CAST(20 + (value % 30) + RAND() * 5 AS DOUBLE) as temperature",
            "CAST(40 + (value % 40) + RAND() * 10 AS DOUBLE) as humidity",
            "CAST(1000 + (value % 50) + RAND() * 20 AS DOUBLE) as pressure",
            "ingestion_time"
        )
    
    # Apply watermark on ingestion time
    watermarked_stream = ingestion_stream \
        .withWatermark("ingestion_time", "5 seconds")
    
    # Tumbling window aggregation based on ingestion time
    sensor_metrics = watermarked_stream \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("ingestion_time"), "20 seconds"),  # Tumbling window
            col("sensor_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as reading_count"),
            expr("avg(temperature) as avg_temperature"),
            expr("min(temperature) as min_temperature"),
            expr("max(temperature) as max_temperature"),
            expr("avg(humidity) as avg_humidity"),
            expr("avg(pressure) as avg_pressure"),
            expr("stddev(temperature) as temp_stddev")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("sensor_id"),
            col("reading_count"),
            col("avg_temperature"),
            col("min_temperature"),
            col("max_temperature"),
            col("avg_humidity"),
            col("avg_pressure"),
            col("temp_stddev")
        )
    
    # Detect anomalies based on ingestion time windows
    anomaly_detection = sensor_metrics \
        .filter(
            (col("temp_stddev") > 2.0) | 
            (col("avg_temperature") > 45) | 
            (col("avg_temperature") < 15)
        ) \
        .withColumn("anomaly_type", 
            expr("""CASE 
                WHEN temp_stddev > 2.0 THEN 'high_variance'
                WHEN avg_temperature > 45 THEN 'high_temp'
                WHEN avg_temperature < 15 THEN 'low_temp'
                ELSE 'unknown' END""")
        )
    
    query = anomaly_detection.writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Ingestion Time Semantics stream started")
    print("  - Using ingestion_time for windowing")
    print("  - Watermark: 5 seconds")
    print("  - Window: 20 seconds tumbling")
    print("  - Anomaly detection enabled")
    
    query.awaitTermination(timeout=30)
    query.stop()
    spark.stop()
    
    return "Ingestion Time Semantics Pattern Completed"


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 3: PROCESSING TIME SEMANTICS PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Uses the system time when the event is processed
# Simplest but least accurate for event ordering

def processing_time_semantics_pattern():
    """
    Processing Time Semantics: Process events based on when they are processed
    Use Case: Real-time dashboards, simple monitoring, non-critical aggregations
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 3: PROCESSING TIME SEMANTICS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("ProcessingTimeSemantics") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")
    
    # Create streaming source
    raw_stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 8) \
        .load()
    
    # Transform to application events
    app_events = raw_stream.selectExpr(
        "CAST(value AS STRING) as request_id",
        "CONCAT('api_', CAST(value % 20 AS STRING)) as endpoint",
        "CASE WHEN value % 5 = 0 THEN 'ERROR' " +
        "     WHEN value % 5 = 1 THEN 'WARN' " +
        "     ELSE 'INFO' END as log_level",
        "CAST(value % 1000 AS INT) as response_time_ms",
        "CAST(value % 10 AS INT) as user_count"
    )
    
    # Add processing timestamp at aggregation time
    # This is implicitly the time when Spark processes the micro-batch
    processed_events = app_events \
        .withColumn("processing_time", current_timestamp())
    
    # Simple count-based trigger (processing time based)
    # No watermark needed as we're using processing time
    endpoint_stats = processed_events \
        .groupBy(
            col("endpoint"),
            col("log_level")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as request_count"),
            expr("avg(response_time_ms) as avg_response_time"),
            expr("max(response_time_ms) as max_response_time"),
            expr("sum(user_count) as total_users"),
            expr("max(processing_time) as last_processed_at")
        )
    
    # Real-time error rate calculation
    error_rate = processed_events \
        .groupBy(col("endpoint")) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as total_requests"),
            expr("sum(CASE WHEN log_level = 'ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as error_count"),
            expr("sum(CASE WHEN log_level = 'WARN' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as warn_count"),
            expr("(sum(CASE WHEN log_level = 'ERROR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / count(*)) * 100 as error_rate_pct")
        ) \
        .filter(col("error_rate_pct") > 10)  # Alert on >10% error rate
    
    # Write endpoint stats
    query1 = endpoint_stats.writeStream \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("endpoint_stats") \
        .trigger(processingTime="8 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    # Write error alerts
    query2 = error_rate.writeStream \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("error_alerts") \
        .trigger(processingTime="8 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Processing Time Semantics streams started")
    print("  - Using current processing time")
    print("  - No watermark (processing time based)")
    print("  - Trigger: Every 8 seconds")
    print("  - Two queries: endpoint_stats and error_alerts")
    
    query1.awaitTermination(timeout=30)
    query1.stop()
    query2.stop()
    spark.stop()
    
    return "Processing Time Semantics Pattern Completed"


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 4: HYBRID TIME SEMANTICS PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Combines multiple time semantics for different purposes
# Most flexible but more complex

def hybrid_time_semantics_pattern():
    """
    Hybrid Time Semantics: Use multiple time dimensions for comprehensive analysis
    Use Case: Financial trading, complex event processing, audit systems
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 4: HYBRID TIME SEMANTICS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("HybridTimeSemantics") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")
    
    # Create streaming source
    raw_stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 6) \
        .load()
    
    # Create events with multiple timestamps
    hybrid_events = raw_stream \
        .withColumn("ingestion_time", current_timestamp()) \
        .selectExpr(
            "CAST(value AS STRING) as transaction_id",
            "CONCAT('account_', CAST(value % 100 AS STRING)) as account_id",
            # Event time: when transaction occurred (simulated past time)
            "CAST(timestamp - INTERVAL 30 SECONDS as TIMESTAMP) as event_time",
            # Ingestion time: when it entered the system
            "ingestion_time",
            "CASE WHEN value % 4 = 0 THEN 'deposit' " +
            "     WHEN value % 4 = 1 THEN 'withdrawal' " +
            "     WHEN value % 4 = 2 THEN 'transfer' " +
            "     ELSE 'payment' END as transaction
```python
            "     ELSE 'payment' END as transaction_type",
            "CAST(100 + (value % 1000) + RAND() * 500 AS DOUBLE) as amount",
            "CASE WHEN value % 10 = 0 THEN 'flagged' ELSE 'normal' END as status"
        ) \
        .withColumn("processing_time", current_timestamp())  # Processing time
    
    # Calculate time deltas for monitoring
    events_with_deltas = hybrid_events \
        .withColumn("ingestion_delay_seconds", 
            unix_timestamp(col("ingestion_time")) - unix_timestamp(col("event_time"))) \
        .withColumn("processing_delay_seconds",
            unix_timestamp(col("processing_time")) - unix_timestamp(col("ingestion_time")))
    
    # Apply watermark on event time for accurate event-time windows
    watermarked_events = events_with_deltas \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "20 seconds")
    
    # ANALYSIS 1: Event-time based aggregation (accurate business metrics)
    event_time_metrics = watermarked_events \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "1 minute"),
            col("transaction_type")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as transaction_count"),
            expr("sum(amount) as total_amount"),
            expr("avg(amount) as avg_amount"),
            expr("avg(ingestion_delay_seconds) as avg_ingestion_delay"),
            expr("max(ingestion_delay_seconds) as max_ingestion_delay")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("event_window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("event_window_end"),
            col("transaction_type"),
            col("transaction_count"),
            col("total_amount"),
            col("avg_amount"),
            col("avg_ingestion_delay"),
            col("max_ingestion_delay")
        )
    
    # ANALYSIS 2: Processing-time based monitoring (system health)
    processing_time_metrics = events_with_deltas \
        .groupBy(col("status")) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as total_processed"),
            expr("avg(processing_delay_seconds) as avg_processing_delay"),
            expr("max(processing_delay_seconds) as max_processing_delay"),
            expr("max(processing_time) as last_processed_at")
        )
    
    # ANALYSIS 3: Hybrid analysis - detect anomalies using both times
    anomaly_detection = watermarked_events \
        .filter(
            (col("ingestion_delay_seconds") > 15) |  # Late arriving events
            (col("amount") > 1000) |                   # Large transactions
            (col("status") == "flagged")               # Flagged transactions
        ) \
        .withColumn("anomaly_reason",
            expr("""CASE 
                WHEN ingestion_delay_seconds > 15 THEN 'late_arrival'
                WHEN amount > 1000 THEN 'large_amount'
                WHEN status = 'flagged' THEN 'flagged_status'
                ELSE 'multiple_reasons' END""")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("transaction_id"),
            col("account_id"),
            col("event_time"),
            col("ingestion_time"),
            col("processing_time"),
            col("transaction_type"),
            col("amount"),
            col("ingestion_delay_seconds"),
            col("processing_delay_seconds"),
            col("anomaly_reason")
        )
    
    # Start multiple queries
    query1 = event_time_metrics.writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("event_time_analysis") \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    query2 = processing_time_metrics.writeStream \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("processing_time_monitoring") \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    query3 = anomaly_detection.writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("hybrid_anomaly_detection") \
        .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Hybrid Time Semantics streams started")
    print("  - Event Time: For accurate business metrics")
    print("  - Ingestion Time: For data pipeline monitoring")
    print("  - Processing Time: For system health monitoring")
    print("  - Three parallel queries running")
    print("  - Anomaly detection using multiple time dimensions")
    
    query1.awaitTermination(timeout=30)
    query1.stop()
    query2.stop()
    query3.stop()
    spark.stop()
    
    return "Hybrid Time Semantics Pattern Completed"


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 5: CUSTOM TIME SEMANTICS PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Implements custom time logic based on business rules
# Most flexible for domain-specific requirements

def custom_time_semantics_pattern():
    """
    Custom Time Semantics: Implement business-specific time logic
    Use Case: SLA tracking, business hours analysis, timezone handling, custom calendars
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 5: CUSTOM TIME SEMANTICS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("CustomTimeSemantics") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")
    
    # Register custom UDFs for business time logic
    from pyspark.sql.functions import udf
    from pyspark.sql.types import BooleanType
    
    # UDF to check if timestamp is during business hours (9 AM - 5 PM, Mon-Fri)
    @udf(returnType=BooleanType())
    def is_business_hours(timestamp):
        if timestamp is None:
            return False
        hour = timestamp.hour
        day_of_week = timestamp.weekday()  # 0 = Monday, 6 = Sunday
        return (9 <= hour < 17) and (day_of_week < 5)
    
    # UDF to calculate business days between timestamps
    @udf(returnType=IntegerType())
    def business_days_diff(start_time, end_time):
        if start_time is None or end_time is None:
            return 0
        
        days = (end_time - start_time).days
        # Simple approximation: 5/7 of total days
        return int(days * 5 / 7)
    
    # UDF to get custom time bucket (morning, afternoon, evening, night)
    @udf(returnType=StringType())
    def get_time_bucket(timestamp):
        if timestamp is None:
            return "unknown"
        hour = timestamp.hour
        if 6 <= hour < 12:
            return "morning"
        elif 12 <= hour < 17:
            return "afternoon"
        elif 17 <= hour < 22:
            return "evening"
        else:
            return "night"
    
    # Create streaming source
    raw_stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 7) \
        .load()
    
    # Create support ticket events with custom time logic
    ticket_events = raw_stream.selectExpr(
        "CAST(value AS STRING) as ticket_id",
        "CONCAT('customer_', CAST(value % 200 AS STRING)) as customer_id",
        "CONCAT('agent_', CAST(value % 20 AS STRING)) as agent_id",
        "CASE WHEN value % 5 = 0 THEN 'critical' " +
        "     WHEN value % 5 = 1 THEN 'high' " +
        "     WHEN value % 5 = 2 THEN 'medium' " +
        "     ELSE 'low' END as priority",
        "CASE WHEN value % 6 = 0 THEN 'open' " +
        "     WHEN value % 6 = 1 THEN 'in_progress' " +
        "     WHEN value % 6 = 2 THEN 'resolved' " +
        "     ELSE 'closed' END as status",
        # Created time (event time)
        "CAST(timestamp - INTERVAL 2 HOURS as TIMESTAMP) as created_at",
        # Current processing time
        "timestamp as current_time"
    )
    
    # Apply custom time semantics
    enriched_tickets = ticket_events \
        .withColumn("is_business_hours", is_business_hours(col("created_at"))) \
        .withColumn("time_bucket", get_time_bucket(col("created_at"))) \
        .withColumn("age_hours", 
            (unix_timestamp(col("current_time")) - unix_timestamp(col("created_at"))) / 3600) \
        .withColumn("business_days_old", 
            business_days_diff(col("created_at"), col("current_time"))) \
        .withColumn("sla_breach", 
            expr("""CASE 
                WHEN priority = 'critical' AND age_hours > 1 THEN true
                WHEN priority = 'high' AND age_hours > 4 THEN true
                WHEN priority = 'medium' AND age_hours > 24 THEN true
                WHEN priority = 'low' AND age_hours > 72 THEN true
                ELSE false END""")
        ) \
        .withColumn("custom_window_start",
            expr("date_trunc('hour', created_at)"))
    
    # Apply watermark on created_at
    watermarked_tickets = enriched_tickets \
        .withWatermark("created_at", "30 seconds")
    
    # ANALYSIS 1: Business hours vs non-business hours metrics
    business_hours_analysis = watermarked_tickets \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("created_at"), "2 minutes"),
            col("is_business_hours"),
            col("priority")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as ticket_count"),
            expr("sum(CASE WHEN status = 'resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as resolved_count"),
            expr("avg(age_hours) as avg_age_hours"),
            expr("sum(CASE WHEN sla_breach THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as sla_breaches")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("is_business_hours"),
            col("priority"),
            col("ticket_count"),
            col("resolved_count"),
            col("avg_age_hours"),
            col("sla_breaches")
        )
    
    # ANALYSIS 2: Time bucket analysis (morning, afternoon, evening, night)
    time_bucket_analysis = watermarked_tickets \
        .groupBy(
            col("time_bucket"),
            col("priority")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as total_tickets"),
            expr("avg(age_hours) as avg_age"),
            expr("sum(CASE WHEN sla_breach THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as total_sla_breaches"),
            expr("(sum(CASE WHEN sla_breach THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / count(*)) * 100 as sla_breach_rate")
        ) \
        .orderBy(col("total_sla_breaches").desc())
    
    # ANALYSIS 3: SLA breach alerts with custom time logic
    sla_breach_alerts = watermarked_tickets \
        .filter(col("sla_breach") == True) \
        .select(
            col("ticket_id"),
            col("customer_id"),
            col("agent_id"),
            col("priority"),
            col("status"),
            col("created_at"),
            col("age_hours"),
            col("business_days_old"),
            col("is_business_hours"),
            col("time_bucket")
        ) \
        .withColumn("alert_severity",
            expr("""CASE 
                WHEN priority = 'critical' AND age_hours > 2 THEN 'URGENT'
                WHEN priority = 'high' AND age_hours > 8 THEN 'HIGH'
                ELSE 'MEDIUM' END""")
        )
    
    # ANALYSIS 4: Custom windowing based on business logic
    # Group by custom hour windows and calculate metrics
    custom_window_metrics = watermarked_tickets \
        .groupBy(
            col("custom_window_start"),
            col("priority")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as hourly_tickets"),
            expr("avg(age_hours) as avg_ticket_age"),
            expr("count(DISTINCT customer_id) as unique_customers"),
            expr("count(DISTINCT agent_id) as active_agents"),
            expr("sum(CASE WHEN is_business_hours THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as business_hour_tickets"),
            expr("sum(CASE WHEN NOT is_business_hours THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) as after_hours_tickets")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("custom_window_start").alias("hour_start"),
            col("priority"),
            col("hourly_tickets"),
            col("avg_ticket_age"),
            col("unique_customers"),
            col("active_agents"),
            col("business_hour_tickets"),
            col("after_hours_tickets")
        )
    
    # Start queries
    query1 = business_hours_analysis.writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("business_hours_analysis") \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    query2 = time_bucket_analysis.writeStream \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("time_bucket_analysis") \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    query3 = sla_breach_alerts.writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("sla_breach_alerts") \
        .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    query4 = custom_window_metrics.writeStream \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("custom_window_metrics") \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Custom Time Semantics streams started")
    print("  - Business hours detection (9 AM - 5 PM, Mon-Fri)")
    print("  - Custom time buckets (morning/afternoon/evening/night)")
    print("  - SLA breach detection based on priority")
    print("  - Business days calculation")
    print("  - Four parallel queries with custom time logic")
    
    query1.awaitTermination(timeout=30)
```python
    query1.stop()
    query2.stop()
    query3.stop()
    query4.stop()
    spark.stop()
    
    return "Custom Time Semantics Pattern Completed"


# ============================================================================
# BONUS: UNIFIED EXAMPLE - ALL PATTERNS COMPARISON
# ============================================================================

def unified_time_semantics_comparison():
    """
    Unified example showing all time semantics patterns side-by-side
    Demonstrates when to use each pattern
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("UNIFIED TIME SEMANTICS COMPARISON")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("UnifiedTimeSemantics") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "2") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")
    
    # Create a single stream with all time dimensions
    raw_stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 5) \
        .load()
    
    # Create comprehensive event with all time semantics
    unified_events = raw_stream \
        .selectExpr(
            "CAST(value AS STRING) as event_id",
            "CONCAT('device_', CAST(value % 30 AS STRING)) as device_id",
            # 1. Event Time: When the event actually occurred (in the past)
            "CAST(timestamp - INTERVAL 45 SECONDS as TIMESTAMP) as event_time",
            "CAST(100 + (value * 2.5) AS DOUBLE) as metric_value"
        ) \
        .withColumn("ingestion_time", current_timestamp()) \
        .withColumn("processing_time", current_timestamp()) \
        .withColumn("event_delay_seconds",
            unix_timestamp(col("ingestion_time")) - unix_timestamp(col("event_time")))
    
    # Apply watermark for event time processing
    watermarked_events = unified_events \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "15 seconds")
    
    # Pattern 1: Event Time Window
    event_time_window = watermarked_events \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "30 seconds"),
            col("device_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as event_count"),
            expr("avg(metric_value) as avg_metric"),
            expr("avg(event_delay_seconds) as avg_delay")
        ) \
        .select(
            lit("EVENT_TIME").alias("pattern_type"),
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("device_id"),
            col("event_count"),
            col("avg_metric"),
            col("avg_delay")
        )
    
    # Pattern 2: Ingestion Time Window
    ingestion_time_window = unified_events \
        .withWatermark("ingestion_time", "10 seconds") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("ingestion_time"), "30 seconds"),
            col("device_id")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as event_count"),
            expr("avg(metric_value) as avg_metric"),
            expr("avg(event_delay_seconds) as avg_delay")
        ) \
        .select(
            lit("INGESTION_TIME").alias("pattern_type"),
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("device_id"),
            col("event_count"),
            col("avg_metric"),
            col("avg_delay")
        )
    
    # Pattern 3: Processing Time (No window, just aggregation)
    processing_time_agg = unified_events \
        .groupBy(col("device_id")) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as event_count"),
            expr("avg(metric_value) as avg_metric"),
            expr("max(processing_time) as last_processed"),
            expr("avg(event_delay_seconds) as avg_delay")
        ) \
        .select(
            lit("PROCESSING_TIME").alias("pattern_type"),
            lit(None).cast(TimestampType()).alias("window_start"),
            lit(None).cast(TimestampType()).alias("window_end"),
            col("device_id"),
            col("event_count"),
            col("avg_metric"),
            col("avg_delay")
        )
    
    # Write comparison results
    query1 = event_time_window.writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("event_time_comparison") \
        .trigger(processingTime="15 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    query2 = ingestion_time_window.writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("ingestion_time_comparison") \
        .trigger(processingTime="15 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    query3 = processing_time_agg.writeStream \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("processing_time_comparison") \
        .trigger(processingTime="15 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Unified Time Semantics Comparison Started")
    print("\n  Comparing three patterns on the same data:")
    print("  1. EVENT_TIME: Most accurate, handles out-of-order events")
    print("  2. INGESTION_TIME: Good balance, tracks data pipeline")
    print("  3. PROCESSING_TIME: Simplest, shows current system state")
    print("\n  All queries running in parallel for comparison...")
    
    query1.awaitTermination(timeout=30)
    query1.stop()
    query2.stop()
    query3.stop()
    spark.stop()
    
    return "Unified Time Semantics Comparison Completed"

║     • Requires watermarking                                                ║
║     • Use Cases: Financial transactions, IoT sensors, user analytics       ║
║                                                                            ║
║  2. INGESTION TIME SEMANTICS                                               ║
║     • Uses timestamp when data enters the system                           ║
║     • Good balance between accuracy and simplicity                         ║
║     • Tracks data pipeline latency                                         ║
║     • Easier than event time, more accurate than processing time           ║
║     • Use Cases: Log aggregation, metrics collection, monitoring           ║
║                                                                            ║
║  3. PROCESSING TIME SEMANTICS                                              ║
║     • Uses system time when event is processed                             ║
║     • Simplest to implement                                                ║
║     • No watermarking needed                                               ║
║     • Not suitable for out-of-order events                                 ║
║     • Use Cases: Real-time dashboards, simple monitoring                   ║
║                                                                            ║
║  4. HYBRID TIME SEMANTICS                                                  ║
║     • Combines multiple time dimensions                                    ║
║     • Most comprehensive analysis                                          ║
║     • Tracks event, ingestion, and processing times                        ║
║     • Complex but powerful                                                 ║
║     • Use Cases: Financial trading, audit systems, SLA tracking            ║
║                                                                            ║
║  5. CUSTOM TIME SEMANTICS                                                  ║
║     • Implements business-specific time logic                              ║
║     • Maximum flexibility                                                  ║
║     • Can include business hours, SLAs, custom calendars                   ║
║     • Requires domain knowledge                                            ║
║     • Use Cases: SLA monitoring, business hours analysis, custom rules     ║
║                                                                            ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║  KEY CONCEPTS:                                                             ║
║  • Watermarking: Handles late-arriving data                                ║
║  • Windowing: Groups events by time intervals                              ║
║  • Triggers: Controls when results are produced                            ║
║  • Output Modes: append, update, complete                                  ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    """
    print(summary)


def demonstrate_watermarking():
    """
    Detailed demonstration of watermarking mechanics
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("WATERMARKING DEMONSTRATION")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("WatermarkingDemo") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")
    
    # Create events with varying delays
    raw_stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 3) \
        .load()
    
    events_with_delays = raw_stream.selectExpr(
        "CAST(value AS STRING) as event_id",
        # Simulate events with different delays
        """CASE 
            WHEN value % 10 = 0 THEN CAST(timestamp - INTERVAL 25 SECONDS as TIMESTAMP)
            WHEN value % 10 = 1 THEN CAST(timestamp - INTERVAL 5 SECONDS as TIMESTAMP)
            ELSE CAST(timestamp - INTERVAL 2 SECONDS as TIMESTAMP)
        END as event_time""",
        "timestamp as arrival_time",
        "CAST(value * 10 AS DOUBLE) as value"
    ) \
    .withColumn("delay_seconds",
        unix_timestamp(col("arrival_time")) - unix_timestamp(col("event_time"))) \
    .withColumn("delay_category",
        expr("""CASE 
            WHEN delay_seconds > 20 THEN 'LATE (>20s)'
            WHEN delay_seconds > 10 THEN 'DELAYED (10-20s)'
            ELSE 'ON_TIME (<10s)'
        END""")
    )
    
    # Apply watermark - events more than 15 seconds late will be dropped
    watermarked = events_with_delays \
        .withWatermark("event_time", "15 seconds")
    
    # Window aggregation to show watermarking in action
    windowed_stats = watermarked \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "20 seconds", "10 seconds"),
            col("delay_category")
        ) \
        .agg(
            expr("count(*) as event_count"),
            expr("avg(delay_seconds) as avg_delay"),
            expr("min(delay_seconds) as min_delay"),
            expr("max(delay_seconds) as max_delay"),
            expr("min(event_time) as earliest_event"),
            expr("max(event_time) as latest_event")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("delay_category"),
            col("event_count"),
            col("avg_delay"),
            col("min_delay"),
            col("max_delay"),
            col("earliest_event"),
            col("latest_event")
        )
    
    query = windowed_stats.writeStream \
        .outputMode("update") \
        .format("console") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .option("numRows", 30) \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Watermarking demonstration started")
    print("  - Watermark threshold: 15 seconds")
    print("  - Events delayed >15s will be dropped")
    print("  - Watch for 'LATE (>20s)' events being filtered")
    print("  - Window: 20 seconds sliding by 10 seconds")
    
    query.awaitTermination(timeout=35)
    query.stop()
    spark.stop()
    
    return "Watermarking Demonstration Completed"

def save_pattern_to_file(pattern_name, output_path="/tmp/streaming_output"):
    """
    Example of how to save streaming results to files instead of console
    """
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName(f"SavePattern_{pattern_name}") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("ERROR")
    
    # Example stream
    stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 5) \
        .load()
    
    processed = stream.selectExpr(
        "CAST(value AS STRING) as id",
        "timestamp as event_time",
        "CAST(value * 2 AS DOUBLE) as metric"
    )
    
    # Write to different formats
    
    # 1. Parquet files (most common for data lake)
    parquet_query = processed.writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("parquet") \
        .option("path", f"{output_path}/parquet/{pattern_name}") \
        .option("checkpointLocation", f"{output_path}/checkpoint/parquet/{pattern_name}") \
        .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    # 2. JSON files (human-readable)
    json_query = processed.writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("json") \
        .option("path", f"{output_path}/json/{pattern_name}") \
        .option("checkpointLocation", f"{output_path}/checkpoint/json/{pattern_name}") \
        .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    # 3. CSV files
    csv_query = processed.writeStream \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .format("csv") \
        .option("path", f"{output_path}/csv/{pattern_name}") \
        .option("checkpointLocation", f"{output_path}/checkpoint/csv/{pattern_name}") \
        .option("header", "true") \
        .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \
        .start()
    
    print(f"\n✓ Streaming to files started for pattern: {pattern_name}")
    print(f"  - Parquet: {output_path}/parquet/{pattern_name}")
    print(f"  - JSON: {output_path}/json/{pattern_name}")
    print(f"  - CSV: {output_path}/csv/{pattern_name}")
    
    # Run for a short duration
    parquet_query.awaitTermination(timeout=60)
    
    # Stop all queries
    parquet_query.stop()
    json_query.stop()
    csv_query.stop()
    spark.stop()


def create_kafka_integration_example():
    """
    Example of integrating time semantics with Kafka
    Note: Requires kafka libraries to be available
    """
    example_code = '''
# Kafka Integration Example for Time Semantics Patterns

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *

def event_time_with_kafka():
    """
    Event Time Semantics with Kafka Source
    """
    spark = SparkSession.builder \\
        .appName("KafkaEventTime") \\
        .master("local[*]") \\
        .config("spark.jars.packages", 
                "org.apache.spark:spark-sql-kafka-0-10_2.12:3.3.0") \\
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Define schema for Kafka messages
    message_schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", StringType()),
        StructField("timestamp", TimestampType()),
        StructField("user_id", StringType()),
        StructField("action", StringType()),
        StructField("value", DoubleType())
    ])
    
    # Read from Kafka
    kafka_stream = spark.readStream \\
        .format("kafka") \\
        .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \\
        .option("subscribe", "events-topic") \\
        .option("startingOffsets", "latest") \\
        .load()
    
    # Parse JSON from Kafka value
    parsed_events = kafka_stream.select(
        from_json(col("value").cast("string"), message_schema).alias("data"),
        col("timestamp").alias("kafka_timestamp")  # Kafka ingestion time
    ).select("data.*", "kafka_timestamp")
    
    # Apply watermark on event timestamp
    watermarked = parsed_events \\
        .withWatermark("timestamp", "1 minute")
    
    # Window aggregation
    windowed = watermarked \\
        .groupBy(
            window(col("timestamp"), "5 minutes", "1 minute"),
            col("action")
        ) \\
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("event_count"),
            sum("value").alias("total_value"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value")
        )
    
    # Write back to Kafka or other sink
    query = windowed.selectExpr(
        "to_json(struct(*)) AS value"
    ).writeStream \\
        .format("kafka") \\
        .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \\
        .option("topic", "aggregated-events") \\
        .option("checkpointLocation", "/tmp/checkpoint/kafka-event-time") \\
        .outputMode("update") \\
        .start()
    
    query.awaitTermination()

# Usage:
# event_time_with_kafka()
    '''
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("KAFKA INTEGRATION EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 80)
    print(example_code)
    print("\n✓ Kafka integration example displayed")


def create_delta_lake_integration_example():
    """
    Example of integrating time semantics with Delta Lake
    """
    example_code = '''
# Delta Lake Integration Example for Time Semantics Patterns

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from delta import *

def event_time_with_delta_lake():
    """
    Event Time Semantics with Delta Lake Sink
    Provides ACID transactions and time travel capabilities
    """
    builder = SparkSession.builder \\
        .appName("DeltaLakeEventTime") \\
        .master("local[*]") \\
        .config("spark.jars.packages", 
                "io.delta:delta-core_2.12:2.3.0") \\
        .config("spark.sql.extensions", 
                "io.delta.sql.DeltaSparkSessionExtension") \\
        .config("spark.sql.catalog.spark_catalog", 
                "org.apache.spark.sql.delta.catalog.DeltaCatalog")
    
    spark = configure_spark_with_delta_pip(builder).getOrCreate()
    
    # Create streaming source
    events = spark.readStream \\
        .format("rate") \\
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 100) \\
        .load()
    
    # Transform with event time
    processed = events.selectExpr(
        "CAST(value AS STRING) as event_id",
        "CAST(timestamp - INTERVAL 10 SECONDS as TIMESTAMP) as event_time",
        "timestamp as processing_time",
        "CAST(value * 1.5 AS DOUBLE) as metric"
    )
    
    # Apply watermark
    watermarked = processed \\
        .withWatermark("event_time", "30 seconds")
    
    # Window aggregation
    aggregated = watermarked \\
        .groupBy(
            window(col("event_time"), "1 minute"),
            date_format(col("event_time"), "yyyy-MM-dd").alias("date")
        ) \\
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("event_count"),
            avg("metric").alias("avg_metric"),
            min("event_time").alias("min_event_time"),
            max("event_time").alias("max_event_time")
        )
    
    # Write to Delta Lake with partitioning
    delta_path = "/tmp/delta/event_time_metrics"
    
    query = aggregated \\
        .writeStream \\
        .format("delta") \\
        .outputMode("update") \\
        .option("checkpointLocation", "/tmp/checkpoint/delta-event-time") \\
        .partitionBy("date") \\
        .start(delta_path)
    
    print(f"Writing to Delta Lake: {delta_path}")
    
    query.awaitTermination(timeout=60)
    
    # After stopping, you can query the Delta table
    # df = spark.read.format("delta").load(delta_path)
    # df.show()
    
    # Time travel example:
    # df_v1 = spark.read.format("delta").option("versionAsOf", 1).load(delta_path)
    # df_timestamp = spark.read.format("delta") \\
    #     .option("timestampAsOf", "2024-01-01 00:00:00").load(delta_path)

# Usage:
# event_time_with_delta_lake()
    '''
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("DELTA LAKE INTEGRATION EXAMPLE")
    print("=" * 80)
    print(example_code)
    print("\n✓ Delta Lake integration example displayed")


def create_monitoring_dashboard_example():
    """
    Example of creating monitoring metrics for time semantics
    """
    example_code = '''
# Monitoring Dashboard Example for Stream Time Semantics

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *

def create_streaming_metrics_dashboard():
    """
    Creates comprehensive monitoring metrics for streaming applications
    Tracks latency, throughput, and data quality
    """
    spark = SparkSession.builder \\
        .appName("StreamingMetricsDashboard") \\
        .master("local[*]") \\
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Create stream with multiple timestamps
    events = spark.readStream \\
        .format("rate") \\
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 50) \\
        .load() \\
        .selectExpr(
            "value as event_id",
            "CAST(timestamp - INTERVAL 5 SECONDS as TIMESTAMP) as event_time",
            "timestamp as ingestion_time"
        ) \\
        .withColumn("processing_time", current_timestamp())
    
    # Calculate comprehensive metrics
    metrics = events \\
        .withColumn("e2e_latency_ms", 
            (unix_timestamp("processing_time") - 
             unix_timestamp("event_time")) * 1000) \\
        .withColumn("ingestion_latency_ms",
            (unix_timestamp("ingestion_time") - 
             unix_timestamp("event_time")) * 1000) \\
        .withColumn("processing_latency_ms",
            (unix_timestamp("processing_time") - 
             unix_timestamp("ingestion_time")) * 1000)
    
    # Aggregate metrics by time window
    dashboard_metrics = metrics \\
        .withWatermark("event_time", "1 minute") \\
        .groupBy(window(col("event_time"), "30 seconds")) \\
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("throughput_events_per_window"),
            avg("e2e_latency_ms").alias("avg_e2e_latency_ms"),
            percentile_approx("e2e_latency_ms", 0.95).alias("p95_e2e_latency_ms"),
            percentile_approx("e2e_latency_ms", 0.99).alias("p99_e2e_latency_ms"),
            max("e2e_latency_ms").alias("max_e2e_latency_ms"),
            avg("ingestion_latency_ms").alias("avg_ingestion_latency_ms"),
            avg("processing_latency_ms").alias("avg_processing_latency_ms"),
            min("event_time").alias("earliest_event"),
            max("event_time").alias("latest_event")
        ) \\
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("throughput_events_per_window"),
            col("avg_e2e_latency_ms"),
            col("p95_e2e_latency_ms"),
            col("p99_e2e_latency_ms"),
            col("max_e2e_latency_ms"),
            col("avg_ingestion_latency_ms"),
            col("avg_processing_latency_ms"),
            (col("latest_event").cast("long") - 
             col("earliest_event").cast("long")).alias("window_span_seconds")
        )
    
    # Write to monitoring sink (console for demo)
    query = dashboard_metrics.writeStream \\
        .outputMode("update") \\
        .format("console") \\
        .option("truncate", "false") \\
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \\
        .start()
    
    # In production, write to:
    # - Prometheus for metrics
    # - InfluxDB for time-series data
    # - Grafana for visualization
    # - Custom monitoring system
    
    query.awaitTermination()

# Usage:
# create_streaming_metrics_dashboard()
    '''
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("MONITORING DASHBOARD EXAMPLE")
    print("
```python
=" * 80)
    print(example_code)
    print("\n✓ Monitoring dashboard example displayed")


def create_best_practices_guide():
    """
    Display best practices for stream time semantics
    """
    best_practices = """
╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║              STREAM TIME SEMANTICS - BEST PRACTICES GUIDE                  ║
╠════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                            ║
║  1. CHOOSING THE RIGHT TIME SEMANTICS                                      ║
║     ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐    ║
║     │ Use EVENT TIME when:                                           │    ║
║     │  • Accuracy is critical (financial, compliance)                │    ║
║     │  • Events can arrive out of order                              │    ║
║     │  • You need reproducible results                               │    ║
║     │  • Event timestamps are reliable                               │    ║
║     │                                                                 │    ║
║     │ Use INGESTION TIME when:                                       │    ║
║     │  • You need to track data pipeline performance                 │    ║
║     │  • Event timestamps are unreliable or missing                  │    ║
║     │  • Moderate accuracy is acceptable                             │    ║
║     │  • You want simpler implementation than event time             │    ║
║     │                                                                 │    ║
║     │ Use PROCESSING TIME when:                                      │    ║
║     │  • Real-time dashboards with current state                     │    ║
║     │  • Simple monitoring and alerting                              │    ║
║     │  • Event ordering doesn't matter                               │    ║
║     │  • Lowest latency is required                                  │    ║
║     │                                                                 │    ║
║     │ Use HYBRID TIME when:                                          │    ║
║     │  • You need comprehensive analysis                             │    ║
║     │  • SLA tracking across multiple dimensions                     │    ║
║     │  • Debugging and troubleshooting pipelines                     │    ║
║     │  • Audit and compliance requirements                           │    ║
║     │                                                                 │    ║
║     │ Use CUSTOM TIME when:                                          │    ║
║     │  • Business-specific time rules apply                          │    ║
║     │  • Complex SLA calculations needed                             │    ║
║     │  • Multiple timezone handling required                         │    ║
║     │  • Domain-specific calendars (trading days, etc.)              │    ║
║     └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘    ║
║                                                                            ║
║  2. WATERMARKING BEST PRACTICES                                            ║
║     • Set watermark based on expected maximum delay                        ║
║     • Too small: drops valid late events                                   ║
║     • Too large: increases state size and memory usage                     ║
║     • Monitor late event metrics to tune watermark                         ║
║     • Typical values: 10s-5min depending on use case                       ║
║     • Formula: watermark = P99_latency + buffer                            ║
║                                                                            ║
║  3. WINDOW SIZING RECOMMENDATIONS                                          ║
║     • Tumbling windows: Non-overlapping, good for aggregations             ║
║       Example: .window(col("timestamp"), "5 minutes")                      ║
║     • Sliding windows: Overlapping, good for moving averages               ║
║       Example: .window(col("timestamp"), "10 minutes", "2 minutes")        ║
║     • Session windows: Gap-based, good for user sessions                   ║
║       (Use groupBy with session_window in Spark 3.2+)                      ║
║                                                                            ║
║  4. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION                                               ║
║     • Partition your data appropriately                                    ║
║     • Use appropriate trigger intervals (not too frequent)                 ║
║     • Enable adaptive query execution                                      ║
║     • Monitor state store size                                             ║
║     • Use checkpointing for fault tolerance                                ║
║     • Consider using Delta Lake for ACID guarantees                        ║
║                                                                            ║
║  5. STATE MANAGEMENT                                                       ║
║     • State grows with number of active windows                            ║
║     • Watermark helps clean up old state                                   ║
║     • Monitor state store metrics                                          ║
║     • Use RocksDB state store for large state                              ║
║     • Configure state cleanup appropriately                                ║
║                                                                            ║
║  6. MONITORING AND ALERTING                                                ║
║     • Track end-to-end latency                                             ║
║     • Monitor watermark lag                                                ║
║     • Alert on excessive late events                                       ║
║     • Track throughput and processing rate                                 ║
║     • Monitor memory and CPU usage                                         ║
║     • Set up dead letter queues for failed events                          ║
║                                                                            ║
║  7. TESTING STRATEGIES                                                     ║
║     • Test with out-of-order events                                        ║
║     • Simulate late arrivals                                               ║
║     • Test watermark behavior                                              ║
║     • Validate window boundaries                                           ║

║     • Load test with realistic data volumes                                ║
║                                                                            ║

    """
