def advanced_boundary_detection_scenarios():
    """
    Advanced scenarios demonstrating complex boundary detection use cases
    """
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ADVANCED BOUNDARY DETECTION SCENARIOS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # SCENARIO 1: HIERARCHICAL BOUNDARY DETECTION
    # ========================================================================
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO 1: HIERARCHICAL BOUNDARY DETECTION")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Detecting boundaries at multiple hierarchical levels")
    
    # Create hierarchical data
    hierarchical_data = [
        (1, "USA", "CA", "San Francisco", 1000, "2024-01-01"),
        (2, "USA", "CA", "Los Angeles", 2000, "2024-01-01"),
        (3, "USA", "NY", "New York", 3000, "2024-01-01"),
        (4, "USA", "NY", "Buffalo", 500, "2024-01-01"),
        (5, "UK", "England", "London", 2500, "2024-01-01"),
        (6, "UK", "Scotland", "Edinburgh", 800, "2024-01-01"),
    ]
    
    hierarchical_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        hierarchical_data,
        ["id", "country", "state", "city", "value", "date"]
    )
    
    print("\nHierarchical Data Sample:")
    hierarchical_df.show()
    
    # Define hierarchical boundaries
    class HierarchicalBoundaryDetector:
        """Detect boundaries at different aggregation levels"""
        
        def __init__(self, spark_session):
            self.spark = spark_session
        
        def detect_hierarchical_boundaries(self, df, hierarchy_cols, value_col, threshold_multiplier=2.0):
            """
            Detect boundaries at each level of hierarchy
            """
            results = {}
            
            for i in range(1, len(hierarchy_cols) + 1):
                level_cols = hierarchy_cols[:i]
                level_name = "_".join(level_cols)
                
                # Aggregate at this level
                level_stats = df.groupBy(*level_cols).agg(
                    _sum(value_col).alias("total_value"),
                    count("*").alias("record_count"),
                    mean(value_col).alias("avg_value")
                )
                
                # Calculate boundaries using percentiles
                percentiles = level_stats.select(
                    percentile_approx("total_value", [0.25, 0.75]).alias("quartiles")
                ).first()["quartiles"]
                
                q1, q3 = percentiles[0], percentiles[1]
                iqr = q3 - q1
                lower_bound = q1 - (threshold_multiplier * iqr)
                upper_bound = q3 + (threshold_multiplier * iqr)
                
                # Detect outliers at this level
                outliers = level_stats.filter(
                    (col("total_value") < lower_bound) | 
                    (col("total_value") > upper_bound)
                ).withColumn("hierarchy_level", lit(level_name))
                
                results[level_name] = {
                    'stats': level_stats,
                    'outliers': outliers,
                    'boundaries': {'lower': lower_bound, 'upper': upper_bound}
                }
                
                print(f"\nLevel: {level_name}")
                print(f"  Boundaries: [{lower_bound:.2f}, {upper_bound:.2f}]")
                print(f"  Outliers detected: {outliers.count()}")
                if outliers.count() > 0:
                    outliers.show()
            
            return results
    
    # Apply hierarchical boundary detection
    hierarchical_detector = HierarchicalBoundaryDetector(spark)
    hierarchical_results = hierarchical_detector.detect_hierarchical_boundaries(
        hierarchical_df,
        hierarchy_cols=["country", "state", "city"],
        value_col="value",
        threshold_multiplier=1.5
    )
    
    # ========================================================================
    # SCENARIO 2: CROSS-DATASET BOUNDARY VALIDATION
    # ========================================================================
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO 2: CROSS-DATASET BOUNDARY VALIDATION")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Validating boundaries across multiple related datasets")
    
    # Create related datasets
    orders_data = [
        (1, "CUST001", 100.0, "2024-01-01", "confirmed"),
        (2, "CUST002", 250.0, "2024-01-01", "confirmed"),
        (3, "CUST003", 75.0, "2024-01-01", "pending"),
        (4, "CUST001", 150.0, "2024-01-02", "confirmed"),
    ]
    
    customers_data = [
        ("CUST001", "Gold", 1000.0),
        ("CUST002", "Silver", 500.0),
        ("CUST003", "Bronze", 250.0),
    ]
    
    orders_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        orders_data,
        ["order_id", "customer_id", "amount", "order_date", "status"]
    )
    
    customers_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        customers_data,
        ["customer_id", "tier", "credit_limit"]
    )
    
    class CrossDatasetBoundaryValidator:
        """Validate boundaries across multiple datasets"""
        
        def __init__(self, spark_session):
            self.spark = spark_session
        
        def validate_referential_boundaries(self, df1, df2, join_key):
            """
            Validate that all records in df1 have corresponding records in df2
            """
            # Find orphaned records
            orphaned = df1.join(df2, join_key, "left_anti")
            
            orphaned_count = orphaned.count()
            total_count = df1.count()
            
            print(f"\nReferential Integrity Check:")
            print(f"  Total records: {total_count}")
            print(f"  Orphaned records: {orphaned_count}")
            print(f"  Integrity: {((total_count - orphaned_count) / total_count * 100):.2f}%")
            
            if orphaned_count > 0:
                print("\n  Orphaned records:")
                orphaned.show()
            
            return orphaned
        
        def validate_cross_dataset_constraints(self, orders_df, customers_df):
            """
            Validate business rules across datasets
            """
            # Join datasets
            joined = orders_df.join(customers_df, "customer_id", "left")
            
            # Check if order amount exceeds credit limit
            violations = joined.filter(
                col("amount") > col("credit_limit")
            ).withColumn(
                "violation_type", lit("EXCEEDS_CREDIT_LIMIT")
            ).withColumn(
                "violation_amount", col("amount") - col("credit_limit")
            )
            
            violation_count = violations.count()
            
            print(f"\nCross-Dataset Constraint Violations:")
            print(f"  Orders exceeding credit limit: {violation_count}")
            
            if violation_count > 0:
                violations.select(
                    "order_id", "customer_id", "amount", 
                    "credit_limit", "violation_amount"
                ).show()
            
            return violations
    
    # Apply cross-dataset validation
    cross_validator = CrossDatasetBoundaryValidator(spark)
    
    orphaned_orders = cross_validator.validate_referential_boundaries(
        orders_df, customers_df, "customer_id"
    )
    
    credit_violations = cross_validator.validate_cross_dataset_constraints(
        orders_df, customers_df
    )
    
    # ========================================================================
    # SCENARIO 3: TEMPORAL BOUNDARY EVOLUTION
    # ========================================================================
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO 3: TEMPORAL BOUNDARY EVOLUTION")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Tracking how boundaries change over time")
    
    # Create time-series data with evolving patterns
    import random
    random.seed(42)
    
    temporal_data = []
    base_date = datetime(2024, 1, 1)
    
    for day in range(30):
        current_date = base_date + timedelta(days=day)
        
        # Simulate changing patterns
        if day < 10:
            base_value = 100
            variance = 10
        elif day < 20:
            base_value = 150  # Pattern shift
            variance = 15
        else:
            base_value = 200  # Another shift
            variance = 20
        
        for hour in range(24):
            timestamp = current_date + timedelta(hours=hour)
            value = base_value + random.gauss(0, variance)
            
            temporal_data.append((timestamp, value, day))
    
    temporal_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        temporal_data,
        ["timestamp", "value", "day_number"]
    ).withColumn("timestamp", col("timestamp").cast(TimestampType()))
    
    class TemporalBoundaryEvolutionDetector:
        """Detect and track boundary evolution over time"""
        
        def __init__(self, spark_session):
            self.spark = spark_session
        
        def detect_boundary_shifts(self, df, timestamp_col, value_col, window_size_days=7):
            """
            Detect when boundaries shift significantly over time
            """
            # Calculate rolling statistics
            days = Window.orderBy(timestamp_col).rangeBetween(
                -window_size_days * 86400, 0
            )
            
            df_with_stats = df.withColumn(
                "rolling_mean",
                mean(value_col).over(days)
            ).withColumn(
                "rolling_stddev",
                stddev(value_col).over(days)
            ).withColumn(
                "upper_bound",
                col("rolling_mean") + (2 * col("rolling_stddev"))
            ).withColumn(
                "lower_bound",
                col("rolling_mean") - (2 * col("rolling_stddev"))
            )
            
            # Detect when current value exceeds rolling boundaries
            df_with_stats = df_with_stats.withColumn(
                "exceeds_upper",
                col(value_col) > col("upper_bound")
            ).withColumn(
                "exceeds_lower",
                col(value_col) < col("lower_bound")
            ).withColumn(
                "is_anomaly",
                col("exceeds_upper") | col("exceeds_lower")
            )
            
            # Detect boundary shifts (when mean changes significantly)
            window_prev = Window.orderBy(timestamp_col).rowsBetween(-1, -1)
            
            df_with_shifts = df_with_stats.withColumn(
                "prev_rolling_mean",
                expr("lag(rolling_mean) over (order by timestamp)")
            ).withColumn(
                "mean_change",
                col("rolling_mean") - col("prev_rolling_mean")
            ).withColumn(
                "mean_change_pct",
                when(col("prev_rolling_mean") != 0,
                     (col("mean_change") / col("prev_rolling_mean")) * 100)
                .otherwise(lit(None))
            ).withColumn(
                "boundary_shift",
                when(expr("abs(mean_change_pct) > 20"), lit(True))
                .otherwise(lit(False))
            )
            
            return df_with_shifts
        
        def summarize_boundary_evolution(self, df_with_stats):
            """
            Summarize boundary evolution patterns
            """
            # Group by day and summarize
            daily_summary = df_with_stats.withColumn(
                "date", expr("date(timestamp)")
            ).groupBy("date").agg(
                mean("rolling_mean").alias("avg_boundary_center"),
                mean("rolling_stddev").alias("avg_boundary_width"),
                _sum(when(col("is_anomaly"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("anomaly_count"),
                _sum(when(col("boundary_shift"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("shift_count")
            ).orderBy("date")
            
            return daily_summary
    
    # Apply temporal boundary evolution detection
    temporal_detector = TemporalBoundaryEvolutionDetector(spark)
    
    temporal_analysis = temporal_detector.detect_boundary_shifts(
        temporal_df,
        timestamp_col="timestamp",
        value_col="value",
        window_size_days=3
    )
    
    print("\nTemporal Boundary Analysis (Sample):")
    temporal_analysis.select(
        "timestamp", "value", "rolling_mean", 
        "upper_bound", "lower_bound", "is_anomaly", "boundary_shift"
    ).show(10)
    
    boundary_evolution = temporal_detector.summarize_boundary_evolution(temporal_analysis)
    
    print("\nBoundary Evolution Summary:")
    boundary_evolution.show()
    
    # Detect significant shifts
    significant_shifts = boundary_evolution.filter(col("shift_count") > 0)
    
    print(f"\nDays with significant boundary shifts: {significant_shifts.count()}")
    if significant_shifts.count() > 0:
        significant_shifts.show()
    
    # ========================================================================
    # SCENARIO 4: MULTI-DIMENSIONAL BOUNDARY DETECTION
    # ========================================================================
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO 4: MULTI-DIMENSIONAL BOUNDARY DETECTION")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Detecting boundaries in multi-dimensional space")
    
    # Create multi-dimensional data
    multi_dim_data = []
    for i in range(200):
        x = random.gauss(50, 10)
        y = random.gauss(50, 10)
        z = random.gauss(50, 10)
        
        # Add some outliers
        if i % 20 == 0:
            x += random.choice([-50, 50])
        if i % 23 == 0:
            y += random.choice([-50, 50])
        
        multi_dim_data.append((i, x, y, z))
    
    multi_dim_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        multi_dim_data,
        ["id", "dimension_x", "dimension_y", "dimension_z"]
    )
    
    class MultiDimensionalBoundaryDetector:
        """Detect boundaries in multi-dimensional space"""
        
        def __init__(self, spark_session):
            self.spark = spark_session
        
        def detect_mahalanobis_outliers(self, df, dimension_cols, threshold=3.0):
            """
            Detect outliers using Mahalanobis distance (simplified version)
            """
            # Calculate means and standard deviations
            stats = df.select([
                mean(col(c)).alias(f"{c}_mean") for c in dimension_cols
            ] + [
                stddev(col(c)).alias(f"{c}_stddev") for c in dimension_cols
            ]).first()
            
            # Calculate normalized distances
            df_normalized = df
            for col_name in dimension_cols:
                col_mean = stats[f"{col_name}_
```python
                col_mean = stats[f"{col_name}_mean"]
                col_stddev = stats[f"{col_name}_stddev"]
                
                df_normalized = df_normalized.withColumn(
                    f"{col_name}_normalized",
                    (col(col_name) - lit(col_mean)) / lit(col_stddev)
                )
            
            # Calculate Euclidean distance in normalized space (simplified Mahalanobis)
            normalized_cols = [f"{c}_normalized" for c in dimension_cols]
            
            distance_expr = " + ".join([
                f"power({c}, 2)" for c in normalized_cols
            ])
            
            df_with_distance = df_normalized.withColumn(
                "mahalanobis_distance",
                expr(f"sqrt({distance_expr})")
            ).withColumn(
                "is_outlier",
                col("mahalanobis_distance") > threshold
            ).withColumn(
                "outlier_severity",
                when(col("mahalanobis_distance") > threshold * 2, lit("HIGH"))
                .when(col("mahalanobis_distance") > threshold * 1.5, lit("MEDIUM"))
                .when(col("mahalanobis_distance") > threshold, lit("LOW"))
                .otherwise(lit("NORMAL"))
            )
            
            return df_with_distance
        
        def detect_dimensional_boundaries(self, df, dimension_cols):
            """
            Detect boundaries for each dimension independently
            """
            boundaries = {}
            
            for col_name in dimension_cols:
                # Calculate percentile-based boundaries
                percentiles = df.select(
                    percentile_approx(col(col_name), [0.01, 0.99]).alias("bounds")
                ).first()["bounds"]
                
                boundaries[col_name] = {
                    'lower': percentiles[0],
                    'upper': percentiles[1]
                }
                
                print(f"\n{col_name} boundaries: [{percentiles[0]:.2f}, {percentiles[1]:.2f}]")
            
            # Find violations for each dimension
            violations_df = df
            for col_name, bounds in boundaries.items():
                violations_df = violations_df.withColumn(
                    f"{col_name}_violates_lower",
                    col(col_name) < bounds['lower']
                ).withColumn(
                    f"{col_name}_violates_upper",
                    col(col_name) > bounds['upper']
                ).withColumn(
                    f"{col_name}_violation",
                    col(f"{col_name}_violates_lower") | col(f"{col_name}_violates_upper")
                )
            
            return violations_df, boundaries
    
    # Apply multi-dimensional boundary detection
    multi_dim_detector = MultiDimensionalBoundaryDetector(spark)
    
    # Detect using Mahalanobis distance
    print("\nMulti-Dimensional Outlier Detection (Mahalanobis):")
    outliers_df = multi_dim_detector.detect_mahalanobis_outliers(
        multi_dim_df,
        dimension_cols=["dimension_x", "dimension_y", "dimension_z"],
        threshold=3.0
    )
    
    outliers = outliers_df.filter(col("is_outlier") == True)
    print(f"\nOutliers detected: {outliers.count()}")
    if outliers.count() > 0:
        outliers.select(
            "id", "dimension_x", "dimension_y", "dimension_z",
            "mahalanobis_distance", "outlier_severity"
        ).show(10)
    
    # Detect dimensional boundaries
    print("\nDimensional Boundary Detection:")
    violations_df, boundaries = multi_dim_detector.detect_dimensional_boundaries(
        multi_dim_df,
        dimension_cols=["dimension_x", "dimension_y", "dimension_z"]
    )
    
    # Show violations
    any_violation = " OR ".join([
        f"dimension_{dim}_violation" for dim in ["x", "y", "z"]
    ])
    
    dimensional_violations = violations_df.filter(expr(any_violation))
    print(f"\nDimensional boundary violations: {dimensional_violations.count()}")
    if dimensional_violations.count() > 0:
        dimensional_violations.select(
            "id", "dimension_x", "dimension_y", "dimension_z",
            "dimension_x_violation", "dimension_y_violation", "dimension_z_violation"
        ).show(10)
    
    # ========================================================================
    # SCENARIO 5: ADAPTIVE BOUNDARY LEARNING
    # ========================================================================
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO 5: ADAPTIVE BOUNDARY LEARNING")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Boundaries that adapt based on historical data patterns")
    
    class AdaptiveBoundaryLearner:
        """Learn and adapt boundaries from historical data"""
        
        def __init__(self, spark_session):
            self.spark = spark_session
            self.learned_boundaries = {}
        
        def learn_boundaries_from_history(self, df, value_col, group_cols=None, 
                                         confidence_level=0.95):
            """
            Learn boundaries from historical data using statistical methods
            """
            if group_cols:
                # Learn boundaries per group
                for group_values in df.select(group_cols).distinct().collect():
                    group_filter = " AND ".join([
                        f"{col_name} = '{getattr(group_values, col_name)}'"
                        for col_name in group_cols
                    ])
                    
                    group_df = df.filter(expr(group_filter))
                    group_key = "_".join([str(getattr(group_values, c)) for c in group_cols])
                    
                    self.learned_boundaries[group_key] = self._calculate_boundaries(
                        group_df, value_col, confidence_level
                    )
            else:
                # Learn global boundaries
                self.learned_boundaries['global'] = self._calculate_boundaries(
                    df, value_col, confidence_level
                )
            
            return self.learned_boundaries
        
        def _calculate_boundaries(self, df, value_col, confidence_level):
            """Calculate statistical boundaries"""
            stats = df.select(
                mean(value_col).alias("mean"),
                stddev(value_col).alias("stddev"),
                _min(value_col).alias("min"),
                _max(value_col).alias("max"),
                count(value_col).alias("count")
            ).first()
            
            # Calculate confidence interval
            from scipy import stats as scipy_stats
            z_score = scipy_stats.norm.ppf((1 + confidence_level) / 2)
            
            margin = z_score * stats["stddev"]
            
            boundaries = {
                'mean': stats["mean"],
                'stddev': stats["stddev"],
                'lower_bound': stats["mean"] - margin,
                'upper_bound': stats["mean"] + margin,
                'absolute_min': stats["min"],
                'absolute_max': stats["max"],
                'sample_size': stats["count"],
                'confidence_level': confidence_level
            }
            
            return boundaries
        
        def apply_learned_boundaries(self, df, value_col, group_cols=None):
            """Apply learned boundaries to new data"""
            if not self.learned_boundaries:
                raise ValueError("No boundaries learned yet. Call learn_boundaries_from_history first.")
            
            df_with_violations = df
            
            if group_cols:
                # Apply group-specific boundaries
                for group_key, boundaries in self.learned_boundaries.items():
                    # This is a simplified version - in production, use proper joins
                    df_with_violations = df_with_violations.withColumn(
                        f"boundary_group_{group_key}_violation",
                        (col(value_col) < boundaries['lower_bound']) |
                        (col(value_col) > boundaries['upper_bound'])
                    )
            else:
                # Apply global boundaries
                global_bounds = self.learned_boundaries['global']
                df_with_violations = df_with_violations.withColumn(
                    "violates_learned_boundary",
                    (col(value_col) < global_bounds['lower_bound']) |
                    (col(value_col) > global_bounds['upper_bound'])
                ).withColumn(
                    "distance_from_mean",
                    expr(f"abs({value_col} - {global_bounds['mean']})")
                ).withColumn(
                    "num_stddevs",
                    col("distance_from_mean") / global_bounds['stddev']
                )
            
            return df_with_violations
        
        def update_boundaries(self, new_data_df, value_col, learning_rate=0.1):
            """
            Update boundaries incrementally with new data
            """
            if 'global' not in self.learned_boundaries:
                raise ValueError("No global boundaries to update")
            
            # Calculate new statistics
            new_stats = new_data_df.select(
                mean(value_col).alias("new_mean"),
                stddev(value_col).alias("new_stddev")
            ).first()
            
            # Update with exponential moving average
            old_bounds = self.learned_boundaries['global']
            
            updated_mean = (1 - learning_rate) * old_bounds['mean'] + \
                          learning_rate * new_stats['new_mean']
            updated_stddev = (1 - learning_rate) * old_bounds['stddev'] + \
                            learning_rate * new_stats['new_stddev']
            
            # Recalculate boundaries
            from scipy import stats as scipy_stats
            z_score = scipy_stats.norm.ppf((1 + old_bounds['confidence_level']) / 2)
            margin = z_score * updated_stddev
            
            self.learned_boundaries['global'].update({
                'mean': updated_mean,
                'stddev': updated_stddev,
                'lower_bound': updated_mean - margin,
                'upper_bound': updated_mean + margin
            })
            
            print(f"\nBoundaries updated:")
            print(f"  New mean: {updated_mean:.2f} (was {old_bounds['mean']:.2f})")
            print(f"  New stddev: {updated_stddev:.2f} (was {old_bounds['stddev']:.2f})")
            print(f"  New bounds: [{updated_mean - margin:.2f}, {updated_mean + margin:.2f}]")
            
            return self.learned_boundaries['global']
    
    # Create historical and new data
    historical_data = [(i, random.gauss(100, 15)) for i in range(1000)]
    historical_df = spark.createDataFrame(historical_data, ["id", "value"])
    
    new_data = [(i, random.gauss(110, 20)) for i in range(100)]  # Pattern shift
    new_df = spark.createDataFrame(new_data, ["id", "value"])
    
    # Learn boundaries from historical data
    adaptive_learner = AdaptiveBoundaryLearner(spark)
    
    print("\nLearning boundaries from historical data...")
    learned_bounds = adaptive_learner.learn_boundaries_from_history(
        historical_df,
        value_col="value",
        confidence_level=0.95
    )
    
    print(f"\nLearned boundaries:")
    for key, bounds in learned_bounds.items():
        print(f"  {key}:")
        print(f"    Mean: {bounds['mean']:.2f}")
        print(f"    StdDev: {bounds['stddev']:.2f}")
        print(f"    Bounds: [{bounds['lower_bound']:.2f}, {bounds['upper_bound']:.2f}]")
        print(f"    Sample size: {bounds['sample_size']}")
    
    # Apply to new data
    print("\nApplying learned boundaries to new data...")
    new_data_validated = adaptive_learner.apply_learned_boundaries(new_df, "value")
    
    violations = new_data_validated.filter(col("violates_learned_boundary") == True)
    print(f"Violations in new data: {violations.count()} out of {new_df.count()}")
    
    if violations.count() > 0:
        violations.select("id", "value", "distance_from_mean", "num_stddevs").show(10)
    
    # Update boundaries with new data
    print("\nUpdating boundaries with new data...")
    updated_bounds = adaptive_learner.update_boundaries(
        new_df,
        value_col="value",
        learning_rate=0.2
    )
    
    # ========================================================================
    # SCENARIO 6: COMPOSITE BOUNDARY SCORING
    # ========================================================================
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO 6: COMPOSITE BOUNDARY SCORING")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Scoring records based on multiple boundary violations")
    
    class CompositeBoundaryScorer:
        """Score records based on multiple boundary violations"""
        
        def __init__(self, spark_session):
            self.spark = spark_session
            self.violation_weights = {}
        
        def set_violation_weights(self, weights):
            """
            Set weights for different types of violations
            weights: dict of {violation_type: weight}
            """
            self.violation_weights = weights
        
        def calculate_boundary_score(self, df, violation_columns):
            """
            Calculate composite score based on multiple boundary violations
            """
            # Start with base score of 100
            df_scored = df.withColumn("boundary_score", lit(100.0))
            
            # Deduct points for each violation
            for col_name in violation_columns:
                weight = self.violation_weights.get(col_name, 10.0)
                
                df_scored = df_scored.withColumn(
                    "boundary_score",
                    when(col(col_name) == True, 
                         col("boundary_score") - lit(weight))
                    .otherwise(col("boundary_score"))
                )
            
            # Add risk category
            df_scored = df_scored.withColumn(
                "risk_category",
                when(col("boundary_score") >= 80, lit("LOW_RISK"))
                .when(col("boundary_score") >= 60, lit("MEDIUM_RISK"))
                .when(col("boundary_score") >= 40, lit("HIGH_RISK"))
                .otherwise(lit("CRITICAL_RISK"))
            ).withColumn(
                "num_violations",
                sum([when(col(c) == True, 1).otherwise(0) for c in violation_columns])
            )
            
            return df_scored
        
        def generate_risk_report(self, df_scored):
            """Generate risk distribution report"""
            risk_summary = df_scored.groupBy("risk_category").agg(
                count("*").alias("record_count"),
                mean("boundary_score").alias("avg_score"),
                mean("num_violations").alias("avg_violations")
            ).orderBy("avg_score", ascending=False)
            
            return risk_summary
    
    # Create test data with multiple potential violations
    test_data = []
    for i in range(100):
        record = {
            'id': i,
            'value1': random.gauss(100, 20),
            'value2': random.gauss(50, 10),
            'value3': random.gauss(75, 15)
        }
        test_data.append((
            record['id'],
            record['value1'],
            record['value
```python
            record['value2'],
            record['value3']
        ))
    
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, ["id", "value1", "value2", "value3"])
    
    # Apply multiple boundary checks
    test_df = test_df.withColumn(
        "value1_violation",
        (col("value1") < 60) | (col("value1") > 140)
    ).withColumn(
        "value2_violation",
        (col("value2") < 30) | (col("value2") > 70)
    ).withColumn(
        "value3_violation",
        (col("value3") < 45) | (col("value3") > 105)
    ).withColumn(
        "extreme_value1",
        (col("value1") < 40) | (col("value1") > 160)
    ).withColumn(
        "extreme_value2",
        (col("value2") < 20) | (col("value2") > 80)
    )
    
    # Calculate composite scores
    scorer = CompositeBoundaryScorer(spark)
    
    scorer.set_violation_weights({
        'value1_violation': 15.0,
        'value2_violation': 10.0,
        'value3_violation': 10.0,
        'extreme_value1': 25.0,
        'extreme_value2': 20.0
    })
    
    print("\nCalculating composite boundary scores...")
    scored_df = scorer.calculate_boundary_score(
        test_df,
        violation_columns=[
            'value1_violation', 'value2_violation', 'value3_violation',
            'extreme_value1', 'extreme_value2'
        ]
    )
    
    print("\nSample scored records:")
    scored_df.select(
        "id", "value1", "value2", "value3",
        "boundary_score", "num_violations", "risk_category"
    ).orderBy("boundary_score").show(10)
    
    # Generate risk report
    print("\nRisk Distribution Report:")
    risk_report = scorer.generate_risk_report(scored_df)
    risk_report.show()
    
    # Show high-risk records
    high_risk = scored_df.filter(col("risk_category").isin(["HIGH_RISK", "CRITICAL_RISK"]))
    print(f"\nHigh/Critical risk records: {high_risk.count()}")
    
    if high_risk.count() > 0:
        high_risk.select(

        ).show(10)

def ml_based_boundary_detection():
    """
    Advanced boundary detection using machine learning techniques
    """
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO 7: ML-BASED BOUNDARY DETECTION")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Using machine learning for intelligent boundary detection")
    
    from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler, StandardScaler
    from pyspark.ml.clustering import KMeans
    from pyspark.ml.stat import Correlation
    
    # Create dataset with normal and anomalous patterns
    ml_data = []
    
    # Normal data cluster 1
    for i in range(300):
        ml_data.append((
            i,
            random.gauss(50, 5),
            random.gauss(50, 5),
            random.gauss(100, 10),
            'normal'
        ))
    
    # Normal data cluster 2
    for i in range(300, 600):
        ml_data.append((
            i,
            random.gauss(80, 5),
            random.gauss(30, 5),
            random.gauss(150, 10),
            'normal'
        ))
    
    # Anomalies
    for i in range(600, 650):
        ml_data.append((
            i,
            random.gauss(120, 10),
            random.gauss(10, 3),
            random.gauss(50, 5),
            'anomaly'
        ))
    
    ml_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        ml_data,
        ["id", "feature1", "feature2", "feature3", "label"]
    )
    
    class MLBoundaryDetector:
        """Machine learning-based boundary detection"""
        
        def __init__(self, spark_session):
            self.spark = spark_session
            self.model = None
            self.scaler = None
        
        def detect_using_clustering(self, df, feature_cols, n_clusters=3):
            """
            Detect boundaries using K-means clustering
            """
            print("\nTraining K-means clustering model...")
            
            # Assemble features
            assembler = VectorAssembler(
                inputCols=feature_cols,
                outputCol="features_raw"
            )
            
            df_assembled = assembler.transform(df)
            
            # Scale features
            scaler = StandardScaler(
                inputCol="features_raw",
                outputCol="features",
                withStd=True,
                withMean=True
            )
            
            scaler_model = scaler.fit(df_assembled)
            df_scaled = scaler_model.transform(df_assembled)
            
            # Train K-means
            kmeans = KMeans(
                k=n_clusters,
                seed=42,
                featuresCol="features",
                predictionCol="cluster"
            )
            
            model = kmeans.fit(df_scaled)
            
            # Make predictions
            predictions = model.transform(df_scaled)
            
            # Calculate distance to cluster centers
            predictions = predictions.withColumn(
                "distance_to_center",
                expr("sqrt(sum(pow(features[i] - centers[prediction][i], 2) for i in range(size(features))))")
            )
            
            # Store model
            self.model = model
            self.scaler = scaler_model
            
            print(f"✓ Model trained with {n_clusters} clusters")
            print(f"  Cluster centers:")
            for i, center in enumerate(model.clusterCenters()):
                print(f"    Cluster {i}: {center}")
            
            return predictions
        
        def identify_anomalous_clusters(self, predictions_df, threshold_percentile=0.95):
            """
            Identify clusters or points that are anomalous
            """
            # Calculate statistics per cluster
            cluster_stats = predictions_df.groupBy("cluster").agg(
                count("*").alias("cluster_size"),
                mean("distance_to_center").alias("avg_distance"),
                stddev("distance_to_center").alias("stddev_distance"),
                _max("distance_to_center").alias("max_distance")
            )
            
            print("\nCluster Statistics:")
            cluster_stats.show()
            
            # Identify outliers within clusters
            # Points far from their cluster center
            distance_threshold = predictions_df.select(
                percentile_approx("distance_to_center", threshold_percentile).alias("threshold")
            ).first()["threshold"]
            
            outliers = predictions_df.filter(
                col("distance_to_center") > distance_threshold
            ).withColumn(
                "anomaly_type", lit("FAR_FROM_CLUSTER")
            )
            
            # Identify small clusters (potential anomaly clusters)
            total_records = predictions_df.count()
            small_cluster_threshold = total_records * 0.05  # Clusters with < 5% of data
            
            small_clusters = cluster_stats.filter(
                col("cluster_size") < small_cluster_threshold
            ).select("cluster").rdd.flatMap(lambda x: x).collect()
            
            small_cluster_outliers = predictions_df.filter(
                col("cluster").isin(small_clusters)
            ).withColumn(
                "anomaly_type", lit("SMALL_CLUSTER")
            )
            
            # Combine outliers
            all_outliers = outliers.union(small_cluster_outliers).distinct()
            
            print(f"\nAnomalies detected:")
            print(f"  Far from cluster center: {outliers.count()}")
            print(f"  In small clusters: {small_cluster_outliers.count()}")
            print(f"  Total unique anomalies: {all_outliers.count()}")
            
            return all_outliers
        
        def calculate_anomaly_scores(self, predictions_df):
            """
            Calculate anomaly scores based on distance and cluster size
            """
            # Get cluster sizes
            cluster_sizes = predictions_df.groupBy("cluster").agg(
                count("*").alias("cluster_size")
            )
            
            # Join cluster sizes
            df_with_scores = predictions_df.join(
                cluster_sizes,
                "cluster",
                "left"
            )
            
            # Calculate anomaly score
            # Higher score = more anomalous
            # Based on: distance to center + inverse cluster size
            total_records = predictions_df.count()
            
            df_with_scores = df_with_scores.withColumn(
                "cluster_size_score",
                (lit(total_records) - col("cluster_size")) / lit(total_records) * 50
            ).withColumn(
                "distance_score",
                col("distance_to_center") * 10  # Scale distance
            ).withColumn(
                "anomaly_score",
                col("cluster_size_score") + col("distance_score")
            ).withColumn(
                "anomaly_level",
                when(col("anomaly_score") > 75, lit("HIGH"))
                .when(col("anomaly_score") > 50, lit("MEDIUM"))
                .when(col("anomaly_score") > 25, lit("LOW"))
                .otherwise(lit("NORMAL"))
            )
            
            return df_with_scores
    
    # Apply ML-based boundary detection
    ml_detector = MLBoundaryDetector(spark)
    
    feature_columns = ["feature1", "feature2", "feature3"]
    
    # Detect using clustering
    predictions = ml_detector.detect_using_clustering(
        ml_df,
        feature_cols=feature_columns,
        n_clusters=3
    )
    
    print("\nSample predictions:")
    predictions.select(
        "id", "feature1", "feature2", "feature3",
        "cluster", "distance_to_center", "label"
    ).show(10)
    
    # Identify anomalies
    anomalies = ml_detector.identify_anomalous_clusters(predictions)
    
    if anomalies.count() > 0:
        print("\nDetected anomalies:")
        anomalies.select(
            "id", "feature1", "feature2", "feature3",
            "cluster", "distance_to_center", "anomaly_type"
        ).show(10)
    
    # Calculate anomaly scores
    scored_predictions = ml_detector.calculate_anomaly_scores(predictions)
    
    print("\nAnomaly Score Distribution:")
    scored_predictions.groupBy("anomaly_level").agg(
        count("*").alias("count")
    ).orderBy("anomaly_level").show()
    
    print("\nTop anomalies by score:")
    scored_predictions.orderBy(col("anomaly_score").desc()).select(
        "id", "feature1", "feature2", "feature3",
        "anomaly_score", "anomaly_level", "label"
    ).show(15)
    
    # Evaluate against true labels
    print("\nEvaluation against true labels:")
    evaluation = scored_predictions.groupBy("label", "anomaly_level").agg(
        count("*").alias("count")
    ).orderBy("label", "anomaly_level")
    evaluation.show()

def realtime_boundary_monitoring_system():
    """
    Simulated real-time boundary monitoring system
    """
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO 8: REAL-TIME BOUNDARY MONITORING")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Continuous monitoring and alerting system")
    
    class RealTimeBoundaryMonitor:
        """Real-time boundary monitoring with alerting"""
        
        def __init__(self, spark_session):
            self.spark = spark_session
            self.alert_history = []
            self.boundary_config = {}
        
        def configure_boundaries(self, config):
            """Configure boundary rules for monitoring"""
            self.boundary_config = config
            print(f"✓ Configured {len(config)} boundary rules")
        
        def process_batch(self, batch_df, batch_id):
            """
            Process a batch of data and check boundaries
            """
            print(f"\n--- Processing Batch {batch_id} ---")
            print(f"Records in batch: {batch_df.count()}")
            
            violations = []
            
            for rule_name, rule_config in self.boundary_config.items():
                # Apply rule
                rule_violations = batch_df.filter(
                    expr(rule_config['condition'])
                )
                
                violation_count = rule_violations.count()
                
                if violation_count > 0:
                    severity = rule_config.get('severity', 'MEDIUM')
                    
                    alert = {
                        'batch_id': batch_id,
                        'timestamp': datetime.now(),
                        'rule_name': rule_name,
                        'severity': severity,
                        'violation_count': violation_count,
                        'total_records': batch_df.count(),
                        'violation_rate': violation_count / batch_df.count()
                    }
                    
                    violations.append(alert)
                    self.alert_history.append(alert)
                    
                    # Trigger alert if threshold exceeded
                    if violation_count > rule_config.get('alert_threshold', 0):
                        self._trigger_alert(alert, rule_violations)
            
            if violations:
                print(f"⚠ {len(violations)} boundary violations detected")
                for v in violations:
                    print(f"  - {v['rule_name']}: {v['violation_count']} violations ({v['severity']})")
            else:
                print("✓ No boundary violations")
            
            return violations
        
        def _trigger_alert(self, alert, violation_df):
            """Trigger alert for boundary violation"""
            print(f"\n🚨 ALERT TRIGGERED:")
            print(f"   Rule: {alert['rule_name']}")
            print(f"   Severity: {alert['severity']}")
            print(f"   Violations: {alert['violation_count']}")
            print(f"   Rate: {alert['violation_rate']*100:.2f}%")

            # e.g., PagerDuty, Slack, email, etc.

            critical_alerts = sum(1 for a in self.alert_history if a['severity'] == 'CRITICAL')
            high_alerts = sum(1 for a in self.alert_history if a['severity
```python
            high_alerts = sum(1 for a in self.alert_history if a['severity'] == 'HIGH')
            
            dashboard.append(f"\nTotal Alerts: {total_alerts}")
            dashboard.append(f"Critical: {critical_alerts}")
            dashboard.append(f"High: {high_alerts}")
            dashboard.append(f"Medium/Low: {total_alerts - critical_alerts - high_alerts}")
            
            # Recent alerts

            for alert in self.alert_history[-5:]:
                dashboard.append(

                )
            
            # Alert frequency by rule

    # Simulate real-time monitoring

def boundary_detection_optimization():
    """
    Advanced optimization techniques for boundary detection at scale
    """
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 80)
    print("SCENARIO 9: BOUNDARY DETECTION OPTIMIZATION")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Performance optimization for large-scale boundary detection")
    
    class OptimizedBoundaryDetector:
        """Optimized boundary detection for large datasets"""
        
        def __init__(self, spark_session):
            self.spark = spark_session
        
        def incremental_boundary_update(self, existing_stats, new_batch_df, 
                                       value_col, alpha=0.1):
            """
            Incrementally update boundary statistics without full recalculation
            Using exponential moving average
            """
            # Calculate new batch statistics
            new_stats = new_batch_df.select(
                count(value_col).alias("new_count"),
                mean(value_col).alias("new_mean"),
                stddev(value_col).alias("new_stddev"),
                _min(value_col).alias("new_min"),
                _max(value_col).alias("new_max")
            ).first()
            
            if existing_stats is None:
                # First batch - initialize
                return {
                    'count': new_stats['new_count'],
                    'mean': new_stats['new_mean'],
                    'stddev': new_stats['new_stddev'],
                    'min': new_stats['new_min'],
                    'max': new_stats['new_max']
                }
            
            # Update statistics incrementally
            updated_stats = {
                'count': existing_stats['count'] + new_stats['new_count'],
                'mean': (1 - alpha) * existing_stats['mean'] + alpha * new_stats['new_mean'],
                'stddev': (1 - alpha) * existing_stats['stddev'] + alpha * new_stats['new_stddev'],
                'min': min(existing_stats['min'], new_stats['new_min']),
                'max': max(existing_stats['max'], new_stats['new_max'])
            }
            
            print(f"\nIncremental Update:")
            print(f"  Previous mean: {existing_stats['mean']:.2f} -> New mean: {updated_stats['mean']:.2f}")
            print(f"  Previous stddev: {existing_stats['stddev']:.2f} -> New stddev: {updated_stats['stddev']:.2f}")
            
            return updated_stats
        
        def parallel_boundary_detection(self, df, column_groups, num_partitions=10):
            """
            Detect boundaries in parallel across column groups
            """
            print(f"\nParallel boundary detection across {len(column_groups)} column groups...")
            
            # Repartition for parallel processing
            df_partitioned = df.repartition(num_partitions)
            
            results = {}
            
            for group_name, columns in column_groups.items():
                print(f"  Processing group: {group_name}")
                
                # Process each column in the group
                group_results = {}
                for col_name in columns:
                    stats = df_partitioned.select(
                        mean(col_name).alias("mean"),
                        stddev(col_name).alias("stddev"),
                        _min(col_name).alias("min"),
                        _max(col_name).alias("max")
                    ).first()
                    
                    group_results[col_name] = {
                        'mean': stats['mean'],
                        'stddev': stats['stddev'],
                        'lower_bound': stats['mean'] - 2 * stats['stddev'],
                        'upper_bound': stats['mean'] + 2 * stats['stddev'],
                        'absolute_min': stats['min'],
                        'absolute_max': stats['max']
                    }
                
                results[group_name] = group_results
            
            print(f"✓ Parallel processing complete")
            return results
        
        def sampling_based_boundary_estimation(self, df, sample_fraction=0.1, 
                                              confidence_level=0.95):
            """
            Estimate boundaries using sampling for very large datasets
            """
            print(f"\nSampling-based boundary estimation (sample: {sample_fraction*100}%)...")
            
            # Take stratified sample
            sample_df = df.sample(withReplacement=False, fraction=sample_fraction, seed=42)
            
            sample_count = sample_df.count()
            total_count = df.count()
            
            print(f"  Sample size: {sample_count:,} ({sample_count/total_count*100:.1f}% of {total_count:,})")
            
            # Calculate boundaries on sample
            boundaries = {}
            
            for col_name in sample_df.columns:
                if col_name in ['id', 'timestamp']:  # Skip non-numeric
                    continue
                
                try:
                    stats = sample_df.select(
                        mean(col_name).alias("mean"),
                        stddev(col_name).alias("stddev")
                    ).first()
                    
                    # Adjust for sampling error
                    from scipy import stats as scipy_stats
                    z_score = scipy_stats.norm.ppf((1 + confidence_level) / 2)
                    margin_of_error = z_score * (stats['stddev'] / (sample_count ** 0.5))
                    
                    boundaries[col_name] = {
                        'estimated_mean': stats['mean'],
                        'estimated_stddev': stats['stddev'],
                        'margin_of_error': margin_of_error,
                        'lower_bound': stats['mean'] - 2 * stats['stddev'] - margin_of_error,
                        'upper_bound': stats['mean'] + 2 * stats['stddev'] + margin_of_error
                    }
                    
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"  Warning: Could not process column {col_name}: {e}")
            
            print(f"✓ Estimated boundaries for {len(boundaries)} columns")
            return boundaries
        
        def cached_boundary_detection(self, df, cache_key="default"):
            """
            Use caching to avoid recomputing boundaries
            """
            cache_file = f"/tmp/boundary_cache_{cache_key}.json"
            
            # Try to load from cache
            try:
                import json
                import os
                
                if os.path.exists(cache_file):
                    with open(cache_file, 'r') as f:
                        cached_boundaries = json.load(f)
                    
                    print(f"✓ Loaded boundaries from cache: {cache_file}")
                    return cached_boundaries
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Cache load failed: {e}")
            
            # Calculate boundaries
            print("Calculating boundaries (cache miss)...")
            boundaries = {}
            
            for col_name in df.columns:
                try:
                    stats = df.select(
                        mean(col_name).alias("mean"),
                        stddev(col_name).alias("stddev")
                    ).first()
                    
                    boundaries[col_name] = {
                        'mean': float(stats['mean']),
                        'stddev': float(stats['stddev']),
                        'lower_bound': float(stats['mean'] - 2 * stats['stddev']),
                        'upper_bound': float(stats['mean'] + 2 * stats['stddev'])
                    }
                except:
                    pass
            
            # Save to cache
            try:
                import json
                with open(cache_file, 'w') as f:
                    json.dump(boundaries, f)
                print(f"✓ Saved boundaries to cache: {cache_file}")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Cache save failed: {e}")
            
            return boundaries
        
        def approximate_boundary_detection(self, df, approx_percentiles=[0.01, 0.99]):
            """

            """
            print("\nApproximate boundary detection using percentiles...")

                    }

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import List, Dict, Optional
import time

# ============================================================================
# Base Classes and Data Models
# ============================================================================

class Task:
    """Represents a task/job that requires resources"""
    def __init__(self, task_id: str, priority: int, resources_required: int, 
                 duration: int, arrival_time: datetime, owner: str):
        self.task_id = task_id
        self.priority = priority  # Higher value = higher priority
        self.resources_required = resources_required
        self.duration = duration  # in seconds
        self.arrival_time = arrival_time
        self.owner = owner
        self.start_time = None
        self.preempted_count = 0
        self.total_wait_time = 0

class ResourcePreemptionStrategy(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for resource preemption strategies"""
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, total_resources: int):
        self.spark = spark
        self.total_resources = total_resources
        self.available_resources = total_resources
        
    @abstractmethod
    def should_preempt(self, running_tasks: List[Task], new_task: Task) -> List[Task]:
        """
        Determine which tasks should be preempted for the new task
        Returns list of tasks to preempt
        """
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_strategy_name(self) -> str:
        """Return the name of the strategy"""
        pass

# ============================================================================
# Pattern 1: Priority-Based Preemption Pattern
# ============================================================================

class PriorityBasedPreemption(ResourcePreemptionStrategy):
    """
    Preempts lower priority tasks to make room for higher priority tasks.
    
    Use Case:
    - Critical tasks need immediate execution
    - SLA-driven workloads
    - Emergency job processing
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, total_resources: int, 
                 min_priority_diff: int = 1):
        super().__init__(spark, total_resources)
        self.min_priority_diff = min_priority_diff
        
    def should_preempt(self, running_tasks: List[Task], new_task: Task) -> List[Task]:
        """
        Preempt tasks with lower priority than the new task
        """
        tasks_to_preempt = []
        resources_needed = new_task.resources_required - self.available_resources
        
        if resources_needed <= 0:
            return tasks_to_preempt
        
        # Sort running tasks by priority (ascending) to preempt lowest priority first
        sorted_tasks = sorted(running_tasks, key=lambda t: t.priority)
        
        for task in sorted_tasks:
            # Only preempt if new task has significantly higher priority
            if new_task.priority > task.priority + self.min_priority_diff:
                tasks_to_preempt.append(task)
                resources_needed -= task.resources_required
                
                if resources_needed <= 0:
                    break
        
        return tasks_to_preempt
    
    def get_strategy_name(self) -> str:
        return "Priority-Based Preemption"

def demonstrate_priority_based_preemption(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate Priority-Based Preemption Pattern"""
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 1: Priority-Based Preemption Pattern")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create sample task data
    task_data = [
        ("task_001", 3, 100, 300, datetime.now() - timedelta(minutes=5), "user_a"),
        ("task_002", 5, 150, 200, datetime.now() - timedelta(minutes=4), "user_b"),
        ("task_003", 2, 120, 400, datetime.now() - timedelta(minutes=3), "user_c"),
        ("task_004", 8, 200, 150, datetime.now(), "user_d"),  # High priority new task
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("task_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("priority", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("resources_required", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("duration", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("arrival_time", TimestampType(), False),
        StructField("owner", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    tasks_df = spark.createDataFrame(task_data, schema)
    
    # Add preemption decision logic using window functions
    window_spec = Window.orderBy(col("priority").desc(), col("arrival_time"))
    
    result_df = tasks_df.withColumn(
        "rank", row_number().over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "cumulative_resources", 
        sum("resources_required").over(
            Window.orderBy(col("priority").desc(), col("arrival_time"))
            .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
        )
    ).withColumn(
        "status",
        when(col("cumulative_resources") <= 400, "Running")
        .when(col("priority") < 5, "Preempted")
        .otherwise("Queued")
    ).withColumn(
        "preemption_reason",
        when(col("status") == "Preempted", 
             concat(lit("Preempted by higher priority task (priority >= 5)")))
        .otherwise(lit("N/A"))
    )
    
    print("\nPriority-Based Preemption Analysis:")
    result_df.select(
        "task_id", "priority", "resources_required", 
        "status", "preemption_reason"
    ).orderBy("priority", ascending=False).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Statistics
    print("\nPreemption Statistics:")
    result_df.groupBy("status").agg(
        count("*").alias("task_count"),
        sum("resources_required").alias("total_resources"),
        avg("priority").alias("avg_priority")
    ).show()

# ============================================================================
# Pattern 2: Time-Based Preemption Pattern
# ============================================================================

class TimeBasedPreemption(ResourcePreemptionStrategy):
    """
    Preempts tasks based on their execution time (e.g., longest running first).
    
    Use Case:
    - Prevent resource hogging
    - Fair time-sharing
    - Deadline-driven scheduling
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, total_resources: int, 
                 max_execution_time: int = 3600):
        super().__init__(spark, total_resources)
        self.max_execution_time = max_execution_time  # in seconds
        
    def should_preempt(self, running_tasks: List[Task], new_task: Task) -> List[Task]:
        """
        Preempt tasks that have been running longest or exceeded time limits
        """
        tasks_to_preempt = []
        resources_needed = new_task.resources_required - self.available_resources
        
        if resources_needed <= 0:
            return tasks_to_preempt
        
        current_time = datetime.now()
        
        # Sort by execution time (longest running first)
        sorted_tasks = sorted(
            running_tasks, 
            key=lambda t: (current_time - t.start_time).total_seconds() 
            if t.start_time else 0,
            reverse=True
        )
        
        for task in sorted_tasks:
            if task.start_time:
                execution_time = (current_time - task.start_time).total_seconds()
                
                # Preempt if exceeded max time or if longest running
                if execution_time > self.max_execution_time or resources_needed > 0:
                    tasks_to_preempt.append(task)
                    resources_needed -= task.resources_required
                    
                    if resources_needed <= 0:
                        break
        
        return tasks_to_preempt
    
    def get_strategy_name(self) -> str:
        return "Time-Based Preemption"

class ResourceBasedPreemption(ResourcePreemptionStrategy):
    """
    Preempts tasks based on resource utilization efficiency.
    
    Use Case:
    - Optimize resource utilization
    - Minimize resource fragmentation
    - Efficient packing of tasks
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, total_resources: int, 
                 efficiency_threshold: float = 0.5):
        super().__init__(spark, total_resources)
        self.efficiency_threshold = efficiency_threshold
        
    def should_preempt(self, running_tasks: List[Task], new_task: Task) -> List[Task]:
        """
        Preempt tasks with lowest resource efficiency
        Resource efficiency = resources_required / duration
        """
        tasks_to_preempt = []
        resources_needed = new_task.resources_required - self.available_resources
        
        if resources_needed <= 0:
            return tasks_to_preempt
        
        # Calculate efficiency for each task
        task_efficiency = []
        for task in running_tasks:
            efficiency = task.resources_required / max(task.duration, 1)
            task_efficiency.append((task, efficiency))
        
        # Sort by efficiency (ascending) - preempt least efficient first
        sorted_tasks = sorted(task_efficiency, key=lambda x: x[1])
        
        for task, efficiency in sorted_tasks:
            if efficiency < self.efficiency_threshold or resources_needed > 0:
                tasks_to_preempt.append(task)
                resources_needed -= task.resources_required
                
                if resources_needed <= 0:
                    break
        
        return tasks_to_preempt
    
    def get_strategy_name(self) -> str:
        return "Resource-Based Preemption"

class FairPreemptionPattern(ResourcePreemptionStrategy):
    """
    Ensures fair resource distribution among users/teams.
    Preempts tasks from users who have consumed more than their fair share.
    
    Use Case:
    - Multi-tenant environments
    - Ensuring fairness across teams
    - Preventing resource monopolization
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, total_resources: int, 
                 user_quotas: Dict[str, int] = None):
        super().__init__(spark, total_resources)
        self.user_quotas = user_quotas or {}
        self.user_usage = {}
        
    def should_preempt(self, running_tasks: List[Task], new_task: Task) -> List[Task]:
        """
        Preempt tasks from users who have exceeded their fair share
        """
        tasks_to_preempt = []
        resources_needed = new_task.resources_required - self.available_resources
        
        if resources_needed <= 0:
            return tasks_to_preempt
        
        # Calculate current usage per user
        user_usage = {}
        for task in running_tasks:
            user_usage[task.owner] = user_usage.get(task.owner, 0) + task.resources_required
        
        # Calculate fair share
        num_users = len(set([t.owner for t in running_tasks] + [new_task.owner]))
        fair_share = self.total_resources / num_users if num_users > 0 else self.total_resources
        
        # Find users exceeding fair share
        exceeding_users = {
            user: usage for user, usage in user_usage.items() 
            if usage > fair_share
        }
        
        # Sort tasks by how much their user exceeds fair share
        sorted_tasks = sorted(
            [t for t in running_tasks if t.owner in exceeding_users],
            key=lambda t: user_usage[t.owner] - fair_share,
            reverse=True
        )
        
        for task in sorted_tasks:
            tasks_to_preempt.append(task)
            resources_needed -= task.resources_required
            user_usage[task.owner] -= task.resources_required
            
            if resources_needed <= 0:
                break
        
        return tasks_to_preempt
    
    def get_strategy_name(self) -> str:
        return "Fair Preemption Pattern"

def demonstrate_fair_preemption(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate Fair Preemption Pattern"""
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 4: Fair Preemption Pattern")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create sample multi-user task data
    task_data = [
        ("task_301", "team_a", 150, 5, "Running"),
        ("task_302", "team_a", 200, 5, "Running"),  # Team A using 350 total
        ("task_303", "team_b", 100, 5, "Running"),  # Team B using 100 total
        ("task_304", "team_c", 120, 5, "Running"),  # Team C using 120 total
        ("task_305", "team_b", 180, 8, "Waiting"),  # Team B wants more
        ("task_306", "team_d", 90, 3, "Waiting"),   # New team D
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("task_id", StringType(), False),
        StructField("owner", StringType(), False),
        StructField("resources_required", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("priority", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("status", StringType(), False)
    ])
    
    tasks_df = spark.createDataFrame(task_data, schema)
    
    # Calculate fair share and usage per team
    total_resources = 600  # Total available resources
    
    # Calculate current usage per team
    team_usage_df = tasks_df.filter(col("status") == "Running") \
        .groupBy("owner") \
        .agg(
            sum("resources_required").alias("current_usage"),
            count("*").alias("task_count")
        )
    
    # Calculate fair share
    num_teams = tasks_df.select("owner").distinct().count()
    fair_share = total_resources / num_teams
    
    # Add fair share analysis
    fairness_df = team_usage_df.withColumn(
        "fair_share", lit(fair_share)
    ).withColumn(
        "usage_vs_fair_share", 
        round(col("current_usage") - col("fair_share"), 2)
    ).withColumn(
        "fairness_ratio",
        round(col("current_usage") / col("fair_share"), 2)
    ).withColumn(
        "status",
        when(col("usage_vs_fair_share") > 50, "Significantly Over Fair Share")
        .when(col("usage_vs_fair_share") > 0, "Over Fair Share")
        .when(col("usage_vs_fair_share") < 0, "Under Fair Share")
        .otherwise("At Fair Share")
    )
    
    print("\nFair Share Analysis by Team:")
    fairness_df.orderBy("usage_vs_fair_share", ascending=False).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Determine preemption candidates
    preemption_df = tasks_df.alias("t").join(
        fairness_df.alias("f"),
        col("t.owner") == col("f.owner"),
        "left"
    ).select(
        col("t.task_id"),
        col("t.owner"),
        col("t.resources_required"),
        col("t.status"),
        col("f.current_usage"),
        col("f.fair_share"),
        col("f.usage_vs_fair_share"),
        col("f.status").alias("team_status")
    ).withColumn(
        "preemption_priority",
        when(col("team_status") == "Significantly Over Fair Share", 1)
        .when(col("team_status") == "Over Fair Share", 2)
        .otherwise(3)
    ).withColumn(
        "preemption_decision",
        when(col("status") == "Waiting", "New Task - Needs Resources")
        .when(col("preemption_priority") == 1, "Preempt - Team Over Fair Share")
        .otherwise("Continue Running")
    )
    
    print("\nPreemption Decisions for Fair Resource Distribution:")
    preemption_df.select(
        "task_id", "owner", "resources_required", "team_status",
        "usage_vs_fair_share", "preemption_decision"
    ).orderBy("preemption_priority", "usage_vs_fair_share", ascending=[True, False]).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Calculate fairness metrics
    print("\nFairness Metrics:")
    fairness_df.agg(
        avg("fairness_ratio").alias("avg_fairness_ratio"),
        stddev("fairness_ratio").alias("fairness_std_dev"),
        max("usage_vs_fair_share").alias("max_deviation"),
        min("usage_vs_fair_share").alias("min_deviation")
    ).show(truncate=False)

class NoPreemptionPattern(ResourcePreemptionStrategy):
    """
    Never preempts running tasks. New tasks must wait in queue.
    
    Use Case:
    - Tasks cannot be interrupted (stateful operations)
    - Transaction-based workloads
    - Critical data processing pipelines
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, total_resources: int, 
                 max_queue_size: int = 100):
        super().__init__(spark, total_resources)
        self.max_queue_size = max_queue_size
        self.task_queue = []
        
    def should_preempt(self, running_tasks: List[Task], new_task: Task) -> List[Task]:
        """
        Never preempt - always return empty list
        """
        return []  # No preemption
    
    def can_queue_task(self, new_task: Task) -> bool:
        """Check if task can be added to queue"""
        return len(self.task_queue) < self.max_queue_size
    
    def get_strategy_name(self) -> str:
        return "No Preemption Pattern"

def demonstrate_no_preemption(spark: SparkSession):

    ])

    result_df = tasks_df.withColumn(

        .otherwise(
            count("*").over(Window.partitionBy(lit(1))) - 
            count(when(col("status") == "Running", 1)).over(Window.partitionBy(lit(1)))
        )
    ).withColumn(
        "time_in_queue_minutes",
        when(col("status") != "Running",
             round((unix_timestamp(lit(current_time)) - unix_timestamp("arrival_time")) / 60, 2))
        .otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        "preemption_allowed",
        lit(False)
    ).withColumn(
        "scheduling_policy",
        when(col("status") == "Running", "FIFO - Running to Completion")
        .when(col("status") == "Queued", "FIFO - Waiting in Queue")
        .otherwise("FIFO - New Arrival")
    )
    
    print("\nNo Preemption Queue Analysis:")
    result_df.select(
        "task_id", "status", "resources_required",

    ).orderBy("queue_position").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Queue statistics
    print("\nQueue Statistics:")
    result_df.groupBy("status").agg(
        count("*").alias("task_count"),
        avg("time_in_queue_minutes").alias("avg_wait_time_minutes"),
        max("time_in_queue_minutes").alias("max_wait_time_minutes"),
        sum("resources_required").alias("total_resources")
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Calculate resource utilization over time
    print("\nResource Utilization (No Preemption):")
    running_resources = result_df.filter(col("status") == "Running") \
        .agg(sum("resources_required").alias("resources_in_use")).collect()[0][0]
    
    total_resources = 400
    utilization_pct = (running_resources / total_resources) * 100 if running_resources else 0
    
    utilization_df = spark.createDataFrame([
        ("Total Available Resources", total_resources),
        ("Resources In Use", running_resources or 0),
        ("Available Resources", total_resources - (running_resources or 0)),
        ("Utilization Percentage", round(utilization_pct, 2))
    ], ["Metric", "Value"])
    
    utilization_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Estimate completion times
    print("\nEstimated Task Completion Timeline:")
    result_df.withColumn(
        "completion_status",
        when(col("status") == "Running", "In Progress - Will Complete Without Interruption")
        .when(col("status") == "Queued", 
              concat(lit("Queued - Position "), col("queue_position").cast("string")))
        .otherwise("New - Will Be Queued")
    ).select(
        "task_id", "status", "completion_status", 
        "estimated_start_time", "estimated_wait_minutes"
    ).orderBy("queue_position").show(truncate=False)
