def comprehensive_window_analytics(df):
    """
    Combines multiple window patterns for comprehensive analytics.
    This demonstrates a real-world analytics pipeline.
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import (
        percent_rank, ntile, cume_dist, first, last
    )
    
    # Define multiple window specifications
    time_window = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp")
    value_window = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("value")
    
    # Rolling windows of different sizes
    rolling_3 = time_window.rowsBetween(-2, 0)
    rolling_5 = time_window.rowsBetween(-4, 0)
    rolling_10 = time_window.rowsBetween(-9, 0)
    
    # Full partition window
    full_window = Window.partitionBy("category")
    
    result = df.withColumn(
        # Ranking functions
        "row_number", row_number().over(time_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "rank_by_value", rank().over(value_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "dense_rank_by_value", dense_rank().over(value_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "percentile_rank", percent_rank().over(value_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "quartile", ntile(4).over(value_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "cumulative_dist", cume_dist().over(value_window)
    ).withColumn(
        # Lag/Lead functions
        "prev_value", lag("value", 1).over(time_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "next_value", lead("value", 1).over(time_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "value_change", col("value") - col("prev_value")
    ).withColumn(
        "value_change_pct", 
        when(col("prev_value") > 0, 
             ((col("value") - col("prev_value")) / col("prev_value")) * 100)
        .otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        # Rolling aggregations - 3 period
        "ma_3", avg("value").over(rolling_3)
    ).withColumn(
        "sum_3", _sum("value").over(rolling_3)
    ).withColumn(
        "min_3", _min("value").over(rolling_3)
    ).withColumn(
        "max_3", _max("value").over(rolling_3)
    ).withColumn(
        "range_3", col("max_3") - col("min_3")
    ).withColumn(
        # Rolling aggregations - 5 period
        "ma_5", avg("value").over(rolling_5)
    ).withColumn(
        "stddev_5", stddev("value").over(rolling_5)
    ).withColumn(
        # Rolling aggregations - 10 period
        "ma_10", avg("value").over(rolling_10)
    ).withColumn(
        # Cumulative aggregations
        "cumulative_sum", _sum("value").over(
            time_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
        )
    ).withColumn(
        "cumulative_avg", avg("value").over(
            time_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
        )
    ).withColumn(
        "cumulative_count", count("*").over(
            time_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
        )
    ).withColumn(
        # First and last values
        "first_value", first("value").over(
            time_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
        )
    ).withColumn(
        "last_value", last("value").over(
            time_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
        )
    ).withColumn(
        # Global statistics
        "category_avg", avg("value").over(full_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "category_stddev", stddev("value").over(full_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "category_min", _min("value").over(full_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "category_max", _max("value").over(full_window)
    ).withColumn(
        # Derived metrics
        "deviation_from_category_avg",
        col("value") - col("category_avg")
    ).withColumn(
        "z_score_global",
        when(col("category_stddev") > 0,
             (col("value") - col("category_avg")) / col("category_stddev"))
        .otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        # Trend indicators
        "is_uptrend", 
        when((col("ma_3") > col("ma_5")) & (col("ma_5") > col("ma_10")), True)
        .otherwise(False)
    ).withColumn(
        "is_downtrend",
        when((col("ma_3") < col("ma_5")) & (col("ma_5") < col("ma_10")), True)
        .otherwise(False)
    ).withColumn(
        # Volatility indicator
        "volatility_ratio",
        when(col("ma_5") > 0, col("stddev_5") / col("ma_5")).otherwise(0)
    )
    
    return result

def validate_window_patterns(df):
    """
    Validates that window patterns are working correctly.
    """
    print("\n1. Testing Non-Overlapping Windows:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # Test: Each record should appear in exactly one window
    from pyspark.sql.functions import window as time_window
    
    non_overlap_test = df.withColumn(
        "window", time_window("timestamp", "60 minutes")
    ).groupBy("id").agg(
        count("*").alias("window_count")
    ).filter(col("window_count") > 1)
    
    overlap_count = non_overlap_test.count()
    print(f"Records appearing in multiple windows: {overlap_count}")
    print(f"✓ PASS" if overlap_count == 0 else "✗ FAIL")
    
    print("\n2. Testing Overlapping Windows:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # Test: Moving average should be calculable
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-2, 0)
    overlap_test = df.withColumn(
        "ma_3", avg("value").over(window_spec)
    ).withColumn(
        "count_3", count("*").over(window_spec)
    )
    
    # First two records in each category should have count < 3
    early_records = overlap_test.withColumn(
        "rn", row_number().over(Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp"))
    ).filter(col("rn") <= 2)
    
    print(f"Early records with partial windows: {early_records.count()}")
    print("✓ PASS - Overlapping windows handle partial windows correctly")
    
    print("\n3. Testing Sliding Windows:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # Test: Records should appear in multiple sliding windows
    sliding_test = df.groupBy(
        time_window("timestamp", "30 minutes", "15 minutes"),
        "category"
    ).agg(
        count("*").alias("count")
    )
    
    total_windows = sliding_test.count()
    print(f"Total sliding windows created: {total_windows}")
    print("✓ PASS - Sliding windows created successfully")
    
    print("\n4. Testing Window Boundaries:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # Test: Window boundaries should be consistent
    boundary_test = df.withColumn(
        "window", time_window("timestamp", "60 minutes")
    ).select(
        col("window.start").alias("start"),
        col("window.end").alias("end")
    ).distinct().withColumn(
        "duration_minutes",
        (unix_timestamp("end") - unix_timestamp("start")) / 60
    )
    
    boundary_test.show(5, truncate=False)
    
    invalid_boundaries = boundary_test.filter(col("duration_minutes") != 60).count()
    print(f"Invalid window boundaries: {invalid_boundaries}")
    print(f"✓ PASS" if invalid_boundaries == 0 else "✗ FAIL")

validate_window_patterns(df)

def optimized_window_pattern(df):
    """
    Demonstrates optimized window operations.
    """
    print("\n1. Using Bounded Windows (Memory Efficient):")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # GOOD: Bounded window
    bounded_window = Window.partitionBy("category") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-99, 0)  # Last 100 rows
    
    result_bounded = df.withColumn(
        "ma_100_bounded", avg("value").over(bounded_window)
    )
    
    print("✓ Bounded window - Memory efficient")
    
    # BAD: Unbounded window (commented out for safety)
    # unbounded_window = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp")
    # result_unbounded = df.withColumn(
    #     "cumsum_unbounded", sum("value").over(unbounded_window)
    # )
    # print("✗ Unbounded window - Can cause memory issues")
    
    print("\n2. Optimizing Multiple Window Operations:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # GOOD: Reuse window specification
    shared_window = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-4, 0)
    
    result_optimized = df.withColumn(
        "ma_5", avg("value").over(shared_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "sum_5", _sum("value").over(shared_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "max_5", _max("value").over(shared_window)
    )
    
    print("✓ Reusing window specification - Efficient")
    
    print("\n3. Partitioning Strategy:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # Check partition distribution
    partition_dist = df.groupBy("category").count().orderBy("category")
    print("Partition distribution:")
    partition_dist.show()
    
    print("\n4. Caching Strategy for Multiple Window Operations:")
    print("-" * 40)
    
    # Cache base DataFrame if used multiple times
    df_cached = df.cache()
    
    # Perform multiple window operations
    result1 = df_cached.withColumn(
        "ma", avg("value").over(Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-4, 0))
    )
    
    result2 = df_cached.withColumn(
        "rank", rank().over(Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("value"))
    )
    
    print("✓ Base DataFrame cached for reuse")
    
    df_cached.unpersist()
    
    return result_optimized

optimized_result = optimized_window_pattern(df)
optimized_result.select("timestamp", "category", "value", "ma_5", "sum_5", "max_5") \
    .orderBy("category", "timestamp").show(10, truncate=False)

streaming_example = """
For Structured Streaming applications, window patterns work similarly
but with additional considerations:

1. WATERMARKING (Handle Late Data):
   ```python
   streaming_df.withWatermark("timestamp", "10 minutes") \\
       .groupBy(window("timestamp", "5 minutes", "1 minute")) \\
       .agg(count("*"))
   ```

2. OUTPUT MODES:
   - Append: Only new windows (complete windows only)
   - Update: Updated aggregations
   - Complete: All aggregations (memory intensive)

3. STATE MANAGEMENT:
   - Bounded state with watermarking
   - Checkpointing for fault tolerance
   - State store configuration

4. EXAMPLE STREAMING WINDOW:
   ```python
   # Read from streaming source
   stream_df = spark.readStream \\
       .format("kafka") \\
       .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \\
       .load()
   
   # Apply sliding window
   windowed_counts = stream_df \\
       .withWatermark("timestamp", "1 hour") \\
       .groupBy(
           window("timestamp", "10 minutes", "5 minutes"),
           "category"
       ).count()
   
   # Write output
   query = windowed_counts.writeStream \\
       .outputMode("update") \\
       .format("console") \\
       .start()
   ```

5. BEST PRACTICES FOR STREAMING:
   - Always use watermarking for time windows
   - Choose appropriate window size vs slide
   - Monitor state size and memory usage
   - Use append mode when possible
   - Configure checkpointing
"""

def ecommerce_order_analysis(df):
    """
    Real-world e-commerce scenario using multiple window patterns.
    """
    print("\nScenario: Analyzing order patterns for an e-commerce platform")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Simulate e-commerce orders (reusing our sample data)
    orders_df = df.withColumnRenamed("value", "order_amount") \
        .withColumnRenamed("quantity", "items_count") \
        .withColumnRenamed("category", "customer_segment")
    
    # 1. NON-OVERLAPPING: Daily revenue by segment
    print("\n1. DAILY REVENUE (Non-Overlapping Windows):")
    from pyspark.sql.functions import window as time_window, date_trunc
    
    daily_revenue = orders_df.groupBy(
        time_window("timestamp", "1 day"),
        "customer_segment"
    ).agg(
        count("*").alias("order_count"),
        _sum("order_amount").alias("total_revenue"),
        avg("order_amount").alias("avg_order_value"),
        _sum("items_count").alias("total_items")
    ).select(
        col("window.start").alias("date"),
        "customer_segment",
        "order_count",
        "total_revenue",
        "avg_order_value",
        "total_items"
    ).orderBy("date", "customer_segment")
    
    daily_revenue.show(10, truncate=False)
    
    # 2. OVERLAPPING: Moving average of orders
    print("\n2. ORDER TRENDS (Overlapping Windows - 7-day moving average):")
    
    daily_orders = orders_df.groupBy(
        date_trunc("day", "timestamp").alias("date"),
        "customer_segment"
    ).agg(
        count("*").alias("daily_orders"),
        _sum("order_amount").alias("daily_revenue")
    )
    
    window_7day = Window.partitionBy("customer_segment") \
        .orderBy("date") \
        .rowsBetween(-6, 0)
    
    trend_analysis = daily_orders.withColumn(
        "ma_7_orders", avg("daily_orders").over(window_7day)
    ).withColumn(
        "ma_7_revenue", avg("daily_revenue").over(window_7day)
    ).withColumn(
        "trend",
        when(col("daily_orders") > col("ma_7_orders") * 1.1, "Growing")
        .when(col("daily_orders") < col("ma_7_orders") * 0.9, "Declining")
        .otherwise("Stable")
    ).orderBy("customer_segment", "date")
    
    trend_analysis.show(20, truncate=False)
    
    # 3. SLIDING: Real-time order monitoring (hourly windows, 30-min slide)
    print("\n3. REAL-TIME MONITORING (Sliding Windows):")
    
    realtime_monitoring = orders_df.groupBy(
        time_window("timestamp", "1 hour", "30 minutes"),
        "customer_segment"
    ).agg(
        count("*").alias("orders"),
        _sum("order_amount").alias("revenue"),
        avg("order_amount").alias("avg_order"),
        _max("order_amount").alias("max_order")
    ).select(
        col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
        col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
        "customer_segment",
        "orders",
        "revenue",
        "avg_order",
        "max_order"
    ).orderBy("window_start", "customer_segment")
    
    realtime_monitoring.show(15, truncate=False)
    
    # 4. CUSTOM: Customer lifetime value with recency
    print("\n4. CUSTOMER LIFETIME VALUE (Custom Windows):")
    
    customer_window = Window.partitionBy("customer_segment") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
    
    clv_analysis = orders_df.withColumn(
        "order_number", row_number().over(
            Window.partitionBy("customer_segment").orderBy("timestamp")
        )
    ).withColumn(
        "cumulative_revenue", _sum("order_amount").over(customer_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "cumulative_orders", count("*").over(customer_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "avg_order_value_lifetime", 
        col("cumulative_revenue") / col("cumulative_orders")
    ).withColumn(
        "days_since_first_order",
        (unix_timestamp("timestamp") - 
         unix_timestamp(first("timestamp").over(customer_window))) / 86400
    )
    
    # Customer segmentation based on behavior
    clv_summary = clv_analysis.groupBy("customer_segment").agg(
        _max("cumulative_orders").alias("max_orders_per_customer"),
        avg("cumulative_revenue").alias("avg_lifetime_value"),
        _max("cumulative_revenue").alias("max_lifetime_value"),
        avg("avg_order_value_lifetime").alias("avg_order_value")
    ).orderBy(col("avg_lifetime_value").desc())
    
    clv_summary.show(truncate=False)
    
    # 5. ANOMALY DETECTION: Unusual order patterns
    print("\n5. ANOMALY DETECTION (Overlapping Windows for Context):")
    
    anomaly_window = Window.partitionBy("customer_segment") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-19, 0)  # 20-order window
    
    anomaly_detection = orders_df.withColumn(
        "window_avg", avg("order_amount").over(anomaly_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "window_stddev", stddev("order_amount").over(anomaly_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "z_score",
        when(col("window_stddev") > 0,
             (col("order_amount") - col("window_avg")) / col("window_stddev"))
        .otherwise(0)
    ).withColumn(
        "is_anomaly",
        _abs(col("z_score")) > 2.5
    ).withColumn(
        "anomaly_type",
        when(col("z_score") > 2.5, "Unusually High")
        .when(col("z_score") < -2.5, "Unusually Low")
        .otherwise("Normal")
    )
    
    # Show only anomalies
    anomalies = anomaly_detection.filter(col("is_anomaly") == True) \
        .select(
            "timestamp",
            "customer_segment",
            "order_amount",
            "window_avg",
            "z_score",
            "anomaly_type"
        ).orderBy("timestamp")
    
    print(f"\nTotal Anomalies Detected: {anomalies.count()}")
    anomalies.show(15, truncate=False)
    
    return {
        'daily_revenue': daily_revenue,
        'trend_analysis': trend_analysis,
        'realtime_monitoring': realtime_monitoring,
        'clv_summary': clv_summary,
        'anomalies': anomalies
    }

# Run comprehensive e-commerce analysis
ecommerce_results = ecommerce_order_analysis(df)

performance_summary = """
EXECUTION STATISTICS:
=====================

Pattern Performance Characteristics:

1. Non-Overlapping Windows:
   - Processing: O(n) - Each record processed once
   - Memory: O(1) per partition
   - Shuffle: Minimal (partition-based)
   - Best for: Batch aggregations
   - Scalability: Excellent

2. Overlapping Windows (Row-based):
   - Processing: O(n * w) where w = window size
   - Memory: O(w) per partition
   - Shuffle: Moderate (partition + sort)
   - Best for: Moving calculations
   - Scalability: Good (bounded windows)

3. Sliding Windows (Time-based):
   - Processing: O(n * s/t) where s = slide, t = window
   - Memory: O(window_size)
   - Shuffle: Moderate to High
   - Best for: Real-time analytics
   - Scalability: Good (with watermarking)

4. Fixed Overlap Windows:
   - Processing: O(n * overlap_ratio)
   - Memory: O(window_size + overlap)
   - Shuffle: Moderate
   - Best for: Pattern matching
   - Scalability: Good

5. Custom Overlap Windows:
   - Processing: Variable (depends on logic)
   - Memory: Variable (can be high)
   - Shuffle: High (often requires joins)
   - Best for: Complex analytics
   - Scalability: Depends on implementation

OPTIMIZATION RECOMMENDATIONS:
==============================

1. Use appropriate partitioning:
   - Partition by high-cardinality columns
   - Avoid data skew
   - Balance partition sizes

2. Bound your windows:
   - Use rowsBetween with limits
   - Avoid unbounded windows in streaming
   - Implement watermarking for time windows

3. Cache strategically:
   - Cache base DataFrames used multiple times
   - Don't cache intermediate window results
   - Monitor memory usage

4. Choose the right window type:
   - rowsBetween: For count-based windows
   - rangeBetween: For value/time-based windows
   - Use built-in window functions when possible

5. Monitor and tune:
   - Check shuffle operations
   - Monitor partition sizes
   - Tune spark.sql.shuffle.partitions
   - Use explain() to understand query plans
"""

print(performance_summary)

troubleshooting = """
COMMON ISSUES AND SOLUTIONS:
============================

1. OUT OF MEMORY ERRORS
   Problem: Window operations consuming too much memory
   Solutions:
   ✓ Use bounded windows (rowsBetween with limits)
   ✓ Increase executor memory
   ✓ Reduce window size
   ✓ Partition data more granularly
   ✓ Use approximate functions for large windows

   Example:
   # Bad - Unbounded
   Window.partitionBy("id").orderBy("timestamp")
   
   # Good - Bounded
   Window.partitionBy("id").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-100, 0)

2. SLOW PERFORMANCE
   Problem: Window operations taking too long
   Solutions:
   ✓ Check partition distribution (avoid skew)
   ✓ Increase parallelism
   ✓ Use appropriate window boundaries
   ✓ Cache frequently used DataFrames
   ✓ Consider approximate aggregations

   Example:
   # Check partition sizes
   df.groupBy(spark_partition_id()).count().show()
   
   # Repartition if needed
   df.repartition("partition_key")

3. INCORRECT RESULTS
   Problem: Window calculations returning wrong values
   Solutions:
   ✓ Verify orderBy clause
   ✓ Check partition columns
   ✓ Ensure timestamp format is correct
   ✓ Handle null values properly
   ✓ Verify window boundaries

   Example:
   # Ensure proper ordering
   Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy(col("timestamp").asc())
   
   # Handle nulls
   df.na.fill({"value": 0})

4. DATA SKEW
   Problem: Some partitions much larger than others
   Solutions:
   ✓ Add salt to skewed keys
   ✓ Use broadcast joins for small tables
   ✓ Repartition with better keys
   ✓ Use adaptive query execution

   Example:
   # Add salt for skewed keys
   df.withColumn("salt", (rand() * 10).cast("int"))
     .withColumn("salted_key", concat(col("key"), lit("_"), col("salt")))

5. STREAMING WINDOW ISSUES
   Problem: State growing unbounded in streaming
   Solutions:
   ✓ Always use watermarking
   ✓ Set appropriate watermark delay
   ✓ Use append mode when possible
   ✓ Configure state timeout
   ✓ Monitor state size

   Example:
   df.withWatermark("timestamp", "1 hour")
     .groupBy(window("timestamp", "10 minutes"))
     .agg(count("*"))

6. NULL HANDLING IN WINDOWS
   Problem: Unexpected nulls in window calculations
   Solutions:
   ✓ Use coalesce() for null handling
   ✓ Filter nulls before window operations
   ✓ Use ignorenulls parameter in first/last
   ✓ Check for null timestamps

   Example:
   # Ignore nulls in first/last
   first("value", ignorenulls=True).over(window_spec)
   
   # Coalesce for safety
   coalesce(avg("value").over(window_spec), lit(0))

7. TIMESTAMP PRECISION ISSUES
   Problem: Time-based windows not aligning correctly
   Solutions:
   ✓ Ensure consistent timestamp format
   ✓ Convert to proper timestamp type
   ✓ Account for timezone differences
   ✓ Use unix_timestamp for calculations

   Example:
   # Standardize timestamps
   df.withColumn("timestamp", 
                 to_timestamp(col("timestamp_str"), "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"))

8. WINDOW BOUNDARY CONFUSION
   Problem: Not understanding rowsBetween vs rangeBetween
   Solutions:
   ✓ rowsBetween: Physical row count
   ✓ rangeBetween: Logical value range
   ✓ Use rangeBetween for time-based windows
   ✓ Use rowsBetween for count-based windows

   Example:
   # Row-based: Last 5 rows
   .rowsBetween(-4, 0)
   
   # Range-based: Last 1 hour (in seconds)
   .rangeBetween(-3600, 0)
"""

def test_window_patterns():
    """
    Comprehensive testing framework for window patterns.
    """
    print("\nRunning Window Pattern Tests...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Create small test dataset
    test_data = [
        (1, "2024-01-01 10:00:00", "A", 100.0),
        (2, "2024-01-01 10:05:00", "A", 110.0),
        (3, "2024-01-01 10:10:00", "A", 105.0),
        (4, "2024-01-01 10:15:00", "A", 115.0),
        (5, "2024-01-01 10:20:00", "A", 120.0),
    ]
    
    test_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("timestamp_str", StringType(), False),
        StructField("category", StringType(), False),
        StructField("value", DoubleType(), False)
    ])
    
    test_df = spark.createDataFrame(test_data, test_schema) \
        .withColumn("timestamp", 
                   to_timestamp(col("timestamp_str"), "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss"))
    
    # Test 1: Moving Average Calculation
    print("\nTest 1: Moving Average (3-period)")
    window_3 = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-2, 0)
    
    ma_result = test_df.withColumn(
        "ma_3", avg("value").over(window_3)
    ).withColumn(
        "expected_ma_3",
        when(col("id") == 1, 100.0)
        .when(col("id") == 2, 105.0)
        .when(col("id") == 3, 105.0)
        .when(col("id") == 4, 110.0)
        .when(col("id") == 5, 113.33)
    )
    
    ma_test = ma_result.withColumn(
        "test_passed",
        _abs(col("ma_3") - col("expected_ma_3")) < 0.01
    )
    
    passed = ma_test.filter(col("test_passed") == True).count()
    total = ma_test.count()
    
    print(f"  Result: {passed}/{total} tests passed")
    ma_test.select("id", "value", "ma_3", "expected_ma_3", "test_passed").show()
    
    # Test 2: Lag Function
    print("\nTest 2: Lag Function")
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp")
    
    lag_result = test_df.withColumn(
        "prev_value", lag("value", 1).over(window_spec)
    )
    
    lag_test = lag_result.filter(col("id") > 1).withColumn(
        "test_passed",
        col("prev_value").isNotNull()
    )
    
    passed = lag_test.filter(col("test_passed") == True).count()
    total = lag_test.count()
    
    print(f"  Result: {passed}/{total} tests passed")
    lag_result.select("id", "value", "prev_value").show()
    
    # Test 3: Cumulative Sum
    print("\nTest 3: Cumulative Sum")
    cumsum_window = Window.partitionBy("category") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
    
    cumsum_result = test_df.withColumn(
        "cumsum", _sum("value").over(cumsum_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "expected_cumsum",
        when(col("id") == 1, 100.0)
        .when(col("id") == 2, 210.0)
        .when(col("id") == 3, 315.0)
        .when(col("id") == 4, 430.0)
        .when(col("id") == 5, 550.0)
    )
    
    cumsum_test = cumsum_result.withColumn(
        "test_passed",
        col("cumsum") == col("expected_cumsum")
    )
    
    passed = cumsum_test.filter(col("test_passed") == True).count()
    total = cumsum_test.count()
    
    print(f"  Result: {passed}/{total} tests passed")
    cumsum_result.select("id", "value", "cumsum", "expected_cumsum", "test_passed").show()
    
    # Test 4: Rank Functions
    print("\nTest 4: Rank Functions")
    rank_window = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy(col("value").desc())
    
    rank_result = test_df.withColumn(
        "rank", rank().over(rank_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "dense_rank", dense_rank().over(rank_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "row_number", row_number().over(rank_window)
    )
    
    print("  Rank results:")
    rank_result.select("id", "value", "rank", "dense_rank", "row_number") \
        .orderBy("rank").show()
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ALL TESTS COMPLETED")
    print("=" * 80)

# Run tests

1. INTRODUCTION TO WINDOW FUNCTIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Window functions perform calculations across a set of rows that are related to
the current row. Unlike GROUP BY, window functions don't collapse rows.

Key Concepts:
-------------
• PARTITION BY: Divides data into partitions
• ORDER BY: Defines row ordering within partitions
• Frame Specification: Defines the window boundaries
  - rowsBetween: Physical row-based boundaries
  - rangeBetween: Logical value-based boundaries

Window Types:
-------------
• Tumbling (Non-Overlapping): Fixed, non-overlapping intervals
• Sliding (Overlapping): Fixed size, moves by specified interval
• Session: Dynamic windows based on activity gaps
• Custom: User-defined logic

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

2. PATTERN IMPLEMENTATIONS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

2.1 NON-OVERLAPPING WINDOW PATTERN
───────────────────────────────────

Description:
Divides data into distinct, non-overlapping time intervals where each record
belongs to exactly one window.

Syntax:
```python
from pyspark.sql.functions import window

df.groupBy(
    window("timestamp", "1 hour"),
    "category"
).agg(
    count("*").alias("count"),
    sum("value").alias("total")
)
```

Use Cases:
• Daily/hourly/monthly aggregations
• Batch processing
• Fixed-period reporting
• ETL pipelines

Advantages:
✓ Simple and efficient
✓ No data duplication
✓ Low memory footprint
✓ Easy to understand

Disadvantages:
✗ No context across boundaries
✗ Can miss patterns at edges
✗ Not suitable for
```python
✗ Not suitable for trend analysis
✗ Fixed granularity

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.2 OVERLAPPING WINDOW PATTERN
───────────────────────────────

Description:
Creates windows where each record can belong to multiple windows, providing
context from surrounding data points.

Syntax:
```python
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category") \\
    .orderBy("timestamp") \\
    .rowsBetween(-4, 0)  # 5-row window including current

df.withColumn("moving_avg", avg("value").over(window_spec))
```

Use Cases:
• Moving averages (SMA, EMA)
• Trend detection
• Data smoothing
• Technical indicators

Advantages:
✓ Captures trends and patterns
✓ Smooths noisy data
✓ Provides context
✓ Flexible window sizes

Disadvantages:
✗ Higher computational cost
✗ Records processed multiple times
✗ Increased memory usage
✗ Edge cases at boundaries

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.3 SLIDING OVERLAP PATTERN
───────────────────────────

Description:
Windows of fixed size that slide by a specified interval, creating controlled
overlap between consecutive windows.

Syntax:
```python
from pyspark.sql.functions import window

df.groupBy(
    window("timestamp", "1 hour", "30 minutes"),  # 1hr window, 30min slide
    "category"
).agg(count("*").alias("count"))
```

Use Cases:
• Real-time dashboards
• Streaming analytics
• Continuous monitoring
• Alert systems

Advantages:
✓ Balances granularity and performance
✓ Configurable overlap
✓ Good for streaming
✓ Predictable resource usage

Disadvantages:
✗ Data duplication in overlaps
✗ More complex than tumbling
✗ Requires careful tuning
✗ Higher storage for results

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.4 FIXED OVERLAP PATTERN
──────────────────────────

Description:
Creates windows with a predetermined, fixed amount of overlap between
consecutive windows.

Syntax:
```python
window_size = 10
overlap_size = 3

df.withColumn(
    "window_id", 
    ((col("row_num") - 1) / (window_size - overlap_size)).cast("int")
)
```

Use Cases:
• Quality control with context
• Audio/video processing
• Signal processing
• Pattern matching

Advantages:
✓ Controlled redundancy
✓ Predictable overlap
✓ Good for pattern detection
✓ Maintains context at boundaries

Disadvantages:
✗ Fixed overlap ratio
✗ More complex implementation
✗ Increased processing time
✗ Requires careful design

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.5 CUSTOM OVERLAP PATTERN
───────────────────────────

Description:
Flexible overlapping windows based on custom business logic, conditions, or
multi-dimensional criteria.

Syntax:
```python
# Custom logic: time + value similarity
df_a.join(
    df_b,
    (col("a.category") == col("b.category")) &
    (col("b.timestamp") >= col("a.timestamp") - interval) &
    (col("b.value").between(col("a.value") * 0.8, col("a.value") * 1.2)),
    "left"
).groupBy("a.id").agg(...)
```

Use Cases:
• ML feature engineering
• Complex event processing
• Fraud detection
• Recommendation systems

Advantages:
✓ Highly flexible
✓ Domain-specific logic
✓ Multi-dimensional analysis
✓ Powerful for complex scenarios

Disadvantages:
✗ Complex to implement
✗ Performance can vary
✗ Harder to optimize
✗ Requires domain knowledge

3. REAL-WORLD USE CASES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

3.1 FINANCIAL ANALYTICS
───────────────────────

Stock Price Analysis:
```python
# Multiple moving averages for trading signals
window_20 = Window.partitionBy("symbol").orderBy("date").rowsBetween(-19, 0)
window_50 = Window.partitionBy("symbol").orderBy("date").rowsBetween(-49, 0)

stock_df.withColumn("MA_20", avg("close").over(window_20)) \\
        .withColumn("MA_50", avg("close").over(window_50)) \\
        .withColumn("signal", 
                    when(col("MA_20") > col("MA_50"), "BUY")
                    .when(col("MA_20") < col("MA_50"), "SELL")
                    .otherwise("HOLD"))
```

Risk Management:
```python
# Value at Risk (VaR) calculation using rolling windows
window_252 = Window.partitionBy("portfolio").orderBy("date").rowsBetween(-251, 0)

portfolio_df.withColumn("returns", (col("value") - col("prev_value")) / col("prev_value")) \\
            .withColumn("volatility", stddev("returns").over(window_252)) \\
            .withColumn("VaR_95", col("volatility") * 1.645)
```

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

3.2 E-COMMERCE ANALYTICS
────────────────────────

Customer Lifetime Value:
```python
# Cumulative customer metrics
customer_window = Window.partitionBy("customer_id") \\
                        .orderBy("order_date") \\
                        .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)

orders_df.withColumn("total_orders", count("*").over(customer_window)) \\
         .withColumn("lifetime_value", sum("order_amount").over(customer_window)) \\
         .withColumn("avg_order_value", col("lifetime_value") / col("total_orders"))
```

Basket Analysis:
```python
# Session-based analysis with 30-minute timeout
session_window = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy("timestamp")

sessions_df.withColumn("time_gap", 
                       (unix_timestamp("timestamp") - 
                        unix_timestamp(lag("timestamp").over(session_window))) / 60) \\
           .withColumn("new_session", when(col("time_gap") > 30, 1).otherwise(0)) \\
           .withColumn("session_id", sum("new_session").over(
               session_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)))
```

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

3.3 IOT AND SENSOR DATA
───────────────────────

Anomaly Detection:
```python
# Detect anomalies in sensor readings
sensor_window = Window.partitionBy("sensor_id") \\
                      .orderBy("timestamp") \\
                      .rowsBetween(-99, 0)  # 100-reading window

sensor_df.withColumn("mean", avg("reading").over(sensor_window)) \\
         .withColumn("stddev", stddev("reading").over(sensor_window)) \\
         .withColumn("z_score", (col("reading") - col("mean")) / col("stddev")) \\
         .withColumn("is_anomaly", abs(col("z_score")) > 3)
```

Predictive Maintenance:
```python
# Calculate degradation trends
maintenance_window = Window.partitionBy("machine_id") \\
                           .orderBy("timestamp") \\
                           .rowsBetween(-29, 0)  # 30-day window

equipment_df.withColumn("avg_temperature", avg("temperature").over(maintenance_window)) \\
            .withColumn("avg_vibration", avg("vibration").over(maintenance_window)) \\
            .withColumn("trend", col("temperature") - col("avg_temperature")) \\
            .withColumn("alert", 
                       when((col("trend") > 5) & (col("avg_vibration") > threshold), "HIGH")
                       .otherwise("NORMAL"))
```

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

3.4 WEB ANALYTICS
─────────────────

User Session Analysis:
```python
# Identify user sessions and engagement
user_window = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("event_time")

clickstream_df.withColumn("prev_event_time", lag("event_time").over(user_window)) \\
              .withColumn("time_since_last", 
                         unix_timestamp("event_time") - 
                         unix_timestamp("prev_event_time")) \\
              .withColumn("session_break", col("time_since_last") > 1800) \\
              .withColumn("session_id", 
                         sum(col("session_break").cast("int")).over(
                             user_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)))
```

Conversion Funnel:
```python
# Track user journey through conversion funnel
funnel_window = Window.partitionBy("user_id", "session_id").orderBy("event_time")

events_df.withColumn("step_number", row_number().over(funnel_window)) \\
         .withColumn("time_to_next", 
                    lead("event_time").over(funnel_window).cast("long") - 
                    col("event_time").cast("long")) \\
         .withColumn("converted", 
                    max(when(col("event_type") == "purchase", 1).otherwise(0))
                    .over(Window.partitionBy("user_id", "session_id")))
```

4. PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

4.1 PARTITIONING STRATEGIES
────────────────────────────

Optimal Partitioning:
```python
# Good: Partition by high-cardinality column
df.repartition("customer_id")

# Better: Partition by multiple columns for better distribution
df.repartition("date", "region")

# Best: Partition with explicit partition count
df.repartition(200, "customer_id")
```

Avoid Data Skew:
```python
# Add salt to skewed keys
df.withColumn("salt", (rand() * 100).cast("int")) \\
  .withColumn("salted_key", concat(col("customer_id"), lit("_"), col("salt"))) \\
  .repartition("salted_key")
```

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

4.2 WINDOW OPTIMIZATION
────────────────────────

Bounded Windows:
```python
# Good: Bounded window
Window.partitionBy("id").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-100, 0)

# Bad: Unbounded window (can cause OOM)
# Window.partitionBy("id").orderBy("timestamp")
```

Reuse Window Specifications:
```python
# Efficient: Define once, use multiple times
window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-4, 0)

df.withColumn("ma", avg("value").over(window_spec)) \\
  .withColumn("sum", sum("value").over(window_spec)) \\
  .withColumn("max", max("value").over(window_spec))
```

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

4.3 CACHING STRATEGIES
──────────────────────

Strategic Caching:
```python
# Cache base DataFrame if used in multiple window operations
df_cached = df.cache()

# Perform multiple window operations
result1 = df_cached.withColumn("ma", avg("value").over(window1))
result2 = df_cached.withColumn("rank", rank().over(window2))

# Don't forget to unpersist
df_cached.unpersist()
```

───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

4.4 CONFIGURATION TUNING
────────────────────────

Spark Configuration:
```python
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
spark.conf.set("spark.sql.window.exec.buffer.in.memory.threshold", "4096")
```

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

✓ Always specify partitionBy() for window functions
✓ Use bounded windows (rowsBetween/rangeBetween) when possible
✓ Reuse window specifications across multiple columns

✓ Monitor partition sizes and avoid data skew
✓ Use appropriate data types (timestamp for time-based windows)
✓ Handle null values explicitly
✓ Use watermarking in streaming applications
✓ Test with representative data volumes
✓ Monitor memory usage and tune accordingly
✓ Use explain() to understand query plans

6. QUICK REFERENCE CHEAT SHEET
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

WINDOW FRAME SPECIFICATIONS:
─────────────────────────────

rowsBetween(-n, 0)          → Last n+1 rows (including current)
rowsBetween(0, n)           → Next n+1 rows (including current)
rowsBetween(-n, n)          → n rows before and after current
rowsBetween(unbounded, 0)   → All rows from start to current
rowsBetween(0, unbounded)   → All rows from current to end
rangeBetween(-3600, 0)      → Last hour (for timestamp in seconds)

COMMON WINDOW FUNCTIONS:
────────────────────────

Aggregate: sum, avg, min, max, count, stddev
Ranking: rank, dense_rank, row_number, ntile, percent_rank
Analytic: lag, lead, first, last, nth_value
Cumulative: cume_dist

window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category") \\
    .orderBy("timestamp") \\
    .rowsBetween(-19, 0)  # 20-period window

result = df.withColumn(
    "mean", avg("value").over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "stddev", stddev("value").over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "z_score", 
    when(col("stddev") > 0, (col("value") - col("mean")) / col("stddev"))
    .otherwise(0)
).withColumn(
    "is_anomaly", _abs(col("z_score")) > 3
).withColumn(
    "severity",
    when(_abs(col("z_score")) > 4, "CRITICAL")
    .when(_abs(col("z_score")) > 3, "HIGH")
    .when(_abs(col("z_score")) > 2, "MEDIUM")
    .otherwise("NORMAL")
)

# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 5: SESSION ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import lag, sum as _sum, unix_timestamp

window_spec = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("timestamp")

session_timeout_minutes = 30

result = df.withColumn(
    "prev_timestamp", lag("timestamp").over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "time_gap_minutes",
    (unix_timestamp("timestamp") - unix_timestamp("prev_timestamp")) / 60
).withColumn(
    "is_new_session",
    when(col("time_gap_minutes").isNull(), 1)
    .when(col("time_gap_minutes") > session_timeout_minutes, 1)
    .otherwise(0)
).withColumn(
    "session_id",
    _sum("is_new_session").over(
        window_spec.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
    )
)

# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 6: CUMULATIVE METRICS
# ============================================================================

from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import sum as _sum, count, avg

cumulative_window = Window.partitionBy("customer_id") \\
    .orderBy("order_date") \\
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)

result = df.withColumn(
    "cumulative_orders", count("*").over(cumulative_window)
).withColumn(
    "cumulative_revenue", _sum("order_amount").over(cumulative_window)
).withColumn(
    "lifetime_avg_order", col("cumulative_revenue") / col("cumulative_orders")
).withColumn(
    "order_number", row_number().over(
        Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy("order_date")
    )
)

# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 7: TREND DETECTION
# ============================================================================

from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import avg

window_short = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-4, 0)
window_medium = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-9, 0)
window_long = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp").rowsBetween(-19, 0)

result = df.withColumn(
    "ma_5", avg("value").over(window_short)
).withColumn(
    "ma_10", avg("value").over(window_medium)
).withColumn(
    "ma_20", avg("value").over(window_long)
).withColumn(
    "trend",
    when((col("ma_5") > col("ma_10")) & (col("ma_10") > col("ma_20")), "STRONG_UPTREND")
    .when((col("ma_5") > col("ma_10")), "UPTREND")
    .when((col("ma_5") < col("ma_10")) & (col("ma_10") < col("ma_20")), "STRONG_DOWNTREND")
    .when((col("ma_5") < col("ma_10")), "DOWNTREND")
    .otherwise("SIDEWAYS")
)

# ============================================================================
# TEMPLATE 8: RANKING AND PERCENTILES
# ============================================================================

from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import rank, dense_rank, row_number, percent_rank, ntile

window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy(col("value").desc())

result = df.withColumn(
    "rank", rank().over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "dense_rank", dense_rank().over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "row_number", row_number().over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "percentile", percent_rank().over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "quartile", ntile(4).over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "decile", ntile(10).over(window_spec)
)

from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import lag, lead

window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp")

result = df.withColumn(
    "prev_value", lag("value", 1).over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "next_value", lead("value", 1).over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "prev_2_value", lag("value", 2).over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "change_from_prev", col("value") - col("prev_value")
).withColumn(
    "pct_change", 
    when(col("prev_value") > 0, 
         ((col("value") - col("prev_value")) / col("prev_value")) * 100)
    .otherwise(0)
).withColumn(
    "momentum", col("value") - col("prev_2_value")
)

from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from pyspark.sql.functions import first, last

window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category") \\
    .orderBy("timestamp") \\
    .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.unboundedFollowing)

result = df.withColumn(
    "first_value", first("value", ignorenulls=True).over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "last_value", last("value", ignorenulls=True).over(window_spec)
).withColumn(
    "change_from_first", col("value") - col("first_value")
).withColumn(
    "pct_of_range", 
    (col("value") - col("first_value")) / (col("last_value") - col("first_value")) * 100
)

# ============================================================================
# MONITORING DASHBOARD FOR WINDOW OPERATIONS
# ============================================================================

from pyspark.sql.functions import current_timestamp, lit
import time

class WindowOperationMonitor:
    '''
    Monitors and tracks window operation performance metrics.
    '''
    
    def __init__(self, spark):
        self.spark = spark
        self.metrics = []
    
    def start_operation(self, operation_name, pattern_type):
        '''Start tracking an operation'''
        return {
            'operation_name': operation_name,
            'pattern_type': pattern_type,
            'start_time': time.time(),
            'start_timestamp': current_timestamp()
        }
    
    def end_operation(self, operation_context, df_result):
        '''End tracking and record metrics'''
        end_time = time.time()
        duration = end_time - operation_context['start_time']
        
        # Get result statistics
        record_count = df_result.count()
        partition_count = df_result.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        metric = {
            'operation_name': operation_context['operation_name'],
            'pattern_type': operation_context['pattern_type'],
            'duration_seconds': duration,
            'record_count': record_count,
            'partition_count': partition_count,
            'records_per_second': record_count / duration if duration > 0 else 0,
            'timestamp': time.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')
        }
        
        self.metrics.append(metric)
        return metric
    
    def get_metrics_df(self):
        '''Convert metrics to DataFrame'''
        if not self.metrics:
            return None
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(self.metrics)
    
    def print_summary(self):
        '''Print metrics summary'''
        if not self.metrics:
            print("No metrics recorded")
            return
        
        metrics_df = self.get_metrics_df()
        
        print("\\n" + "=" * 80)
        print("PERFORMANCE METRICS SUMMARY")
        print("=" * 80)
        
        metrics_df.groupBy("pattern_type").agg(
            count("*").alias("operation_count"),
            avg("duration_seconds").alias("avg_duration"),
            sum("record_count").alias("total_records"),
            avg("records_per_second").alias("avg_throughput")
        ).show(truncate=False)

# Usage Example:
# monitor = WindowOperationMonitor(spark)
# ctx = monitor.start_operation("daily_aggregation", "non_overlapping")
# result = perform_window_operation(df)
# metrics = monitor.end_operation(ctx, result)
# monitor.print_summary()

# ============================================================================
# ALERTING SYSTEM
# ============================================================================

class WindowOperationAlerter:
    '''
    Alert system for window operation anomalies.
    '''
    
    def __init__(self, thresholds):
        self.thresholds = thresholds
        self.alerts = []
    
    def check_performance(self, metrics):
        '''Check if metrics exceed thresholds'''
        alerts = []
        
        # Check duration
        if metrics['duration_seconds'] > self.thresholds.get('max_duration', 3600):
            alerts.append({
                'severity': 'WARNING',
                'type': 'SLOW_EXECUTION',
                'message': f"Operation took {metrics['duration_seconds']:.2f}s",
                'metric': metrics
            })
        
        # Check throughput
        if metrics['records_per_second'] < self.thresholds.get('min_throughput', 1000):
            alerts.append({
                'severity': 'WARNING',
                'type': 'LOW_THROUGHPUT',
                'message': f"Throughput: {metrics['records_per_second']:.2f} rec/s",
                'metric': metrics
            })
        
        self.alerts.extend(alerts)
        return alerts
    
    def send_alerts(self, alerts):
        '''Send alerts (implement based on your notification system)'''
        for alert in alerts:
            print(f"[{alert['severity']}] {alert['type']}: {alert['message']}")
            # Implement: Send email, Slack, PagerDuty, etc.

# Usage:

#     'max_duration': 1800,
#     'min_throughput': 5000
# })

# ============================================================================
# UNIT TESTS FOR WINDOW PATTERNS
# ============================================================================

import unittest
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, avg, sum as _sum
from pyspark.sql.window import Window

class TestWindowPatterns(unittest.TestCase):
    
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.spark = SparkSession.builder \\
            .appName("WindowPatternTests") \\
            .master("local[2]") \\
            .getOrCreate()
    
    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.spark.stop()
    
    def setUp(self):
        '''Create test data before each test'''
        self.test_data = [
            (1, "2024-01-01 10:00:00", "A", 100.0),
            (2, "2024-01-01 10:05:00", "A", 110.0),
            (3, "2024-01-01 10:10:00", "A", 105.0),
            (4, "2024-01-01 10:15:00", "A", 115.0),
            (5, "2024-01-01 10:20:00", "A", 120.0),
        ]
        
        self.df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            self.test_data,
            ["id", "timestamp", "category", "value"]
        )
    
    def test_moving_average_calculation(self):
        '''Test moving average window calculation'''
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category") \\
            .orderBy("id") \\
            .rowsBetween(-2, 0)
        
        result = self.df.withColumn(
            "ma_3", avg("value").over(window_spec)
        )
        
        # Test first record (only 1 value)
        first_ma = result.filter(col("id") == 1).select("ma_3").collect()[0][0]
        self.assertAlmostEqual(first_ma, 100.0, places=2)
        
        # Test third record (3 values: 100, 110, 105)
        third_ma = result.filter(col("id") == 3).select("ma_3").collect()[0][0]
        self.assertAlmostEqual(third_ma, 105.0, places=2)
    
    def test_cumulative_sum(self):
        '''Test cumulative sum calculation'''
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category") \\
            .orderBy("id") \\
            .rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, 0)
        
        result = self.df.withColumn(
            "cumsum", _sum("value").over(window_spec)
        )
        
        # Test last record cumulative sum
        last_cumsum = result.filter(col("id") == 5).select("cumsum").collect()[0][0]
        expected_sum = 100 + 110 + 105 + 115 + 120
        self.assertEqual(last_cumsum, expected_sum)
    
    def test_null_handling(self):
        '''Test handling of null values in windows'''
        # Add null value
        test_data_with_null = self.test_data + [
            (6, "2024-01-01 10:25:00", "A", None)
        ]
        
        df_with_null = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            test_data_with_null,
            ["id", "timestamp", "category", "value"]
        )
        
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category") \\
            .orderBy("id") \\
            .rowsBetween(-2, 0)
        
        result = df_with_null.withColumn(
            "ma_3", avg("value").over(window_spec)
        )
        
        # Moving average should ignore nulls
        last_ma = result.filter(col("id") == 6).select("ma_3").collect()[0][0]
        self.assertIsNotNone(last_ma)
    
    def test_empty_partition(self):
        '''Test behavior with empty partitions'''
        empty_df = self.spark.createDataFrame([], self.df.schema)
        
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category") \\
            .orderBy("id") \\
            .rowsBetween(-2, 0)
        
        result = empty_df.withColumn(
            "ma_3", avg("value").over(window_spec)
        )
        
        # Should not raise error
        self.assertEqual(result.count(), 0)
    
    def test_window_boundaries(self):
        '''Test window boundary conditions'''
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category") \\
            .orderBy("id") \\
            .rowsBetween(-1, 1)  # Previous, current, next
        
        result = self.df.withColumn(
            "window_count", count("*").over(window_spec)
        )
        
        # First record: only current and next (2 rows)
        first_count = result.filter(col("id") == 1).select("window_count").collect()[0][0]
        self.assertEqual(first_count, 2)
        
        # Middle record: previous, current, next (3 rows)
        middle_count = result.filter(col("id") == 3).select("window_count").collect()[0][0]
        self.assertEqual(middle_count, 3)
        
        # Last record: previous and current (2 rows)
        last_count = result.filter(col("id") == 5).select("window_count").collect()[0][0]
        self.assertEqual(last_count, 2)

# Run tests
if __name__ == '__main__':
    unittest.main(argv=[''], exit=False)

print("\n1. MULTI-LEVEL WINDOW AGGREGATIONS")

def multi_level_window_aggregation(df):
    """
    Demonstrates nested window aggregations - windows on windows.
    Useful for hierarchical analysis.
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import col, avg, stddev, when
    
    # First level: Calculate moving average
    window_level1 = Window.partitionBy("category") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-4, 0)
    
    df_level1 = df.withColumn(
        "ma_5", avg("value").over(window_level1)
    )
    
    # Second level: Calculate moving average of moving averages
    window_level2 = Window.partitionBy("category") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-2, 0)
    
    df_level2 = df_level1.withColumn(
        "ma_of_ma", avg("ma_5").over(window_level2)
    )
    
    # Third level: Detect divergence
    df_level3 = df_level2.withColumn(
        "divergence", col("ma_5") - col("ma_of_ma")
    ).withColumn(
        "signal",
        when(col("divergence") > 5, "STRONG_TREND")
        .when(col("divergence") > 2, "TREND")
        .when(col("divergence") < -5, "STRONG_REVERSAL")
        .when(col("divergence") < -2, "REVERSAL")
        .otherwise("NEUTRAL")
    )
    
    return df_level3

# Example usage
print("\nMulti-Level Window Example:")
print("Level 1: 5-period moving average")
print("Level 2: 3-period MA of MA")
print("Level 3: Divergence detection")

def conditional_window_pattern(df):
    """
    Windows that change behavior based on conditions.
    Different window sizes for different scenarios.
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import when, col
    
    window_small = Window.partitionBy("category") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-2, 0)
    
    window_large = Window.partitionBy("category") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-9, 0)
    
    # Calculate both windows
    result = df.withColumn(
        "ma_small", avg("value").over(window_small)
    ).withColumn(
        "ma_large", avg("value").over(window_large)
    ).withColumn(
        "volatility", stddev("value").over(window_small)
    ).withColumn(
        # Use different MA based on volatility
        "adaptive_ma",
        when(col("volatility") > 10, col("ma_small"))  # High volatility: use small window
        .otherwise(col("ma_large"))  # Low volatility: use large window
    )
    
    return result

print("\nConditional Window Example:")
print("Adapts window size based on volatility")
print("High volatility → smaller window (more responsive)")
print("Low volatility → larger window (more stable)")

print("\n3. CROSS-PARTITION WINDOW ANALYSIS")
print("-" * 80)

def cross_partition_window(df):
    """
    Analyze relationships across different partitions.
    Useful for comparative analysis.
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import col, avg, lag
    
    # Calculate metrics within each partition
    partition_window = Window.partitionBy("category") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-4, 0)
    
    # Calculate global metrics (no partition)
    global_window = Window.orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-4, 0)
    
    result = df.withColumn(
        "category_ma", avg("value").over(partition_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "global_ma", avg("value").over(global_window)
    ).withColumn(
        "relative_performance",
        (col("category_ma") - col("global_ma")) / col("global_ma") * 100
    ).withColumn(
        "category_rank",
        rank().over(Window.partitionBy().orderBy(col("category_ma").desc()))
    )
    
    return result

print("\nCross-Partition Analysis:")
print("Compares category performance against global average")
print("Ranks categories relative to each other")

def time_weighted_window(df):
    """
    Windows where recent data has more weight than older data.
    Implements exponential moving average (EMA).
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import col, exp, sum as _sum, lit
    
    # Add time-based weights (exponential decay)
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-9, 0)
    
    alpha = 0.3  # Smoothing factor
    
    result = df.withColumn(
        "row_num", row_number().over(Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy("timestamp"))
    ).withColumn(
        # Simple EMA approximation
        "ema",
        avg("value").over(window_spec)  # Simplified - full EMA requires iterative calculation
    )
    
    # For true EMA, need to use custom aggregation or iterative approach
    # This is a simplified demonstration
    
    return result

print("\nTime-Weighted Windows:")

def dynamic_window_sizing(df):
    """
    Window size changes based on data characteristics.
    Adapts to data density and patterns.
    """
    from pyspark.sql.functions import col, count, when
    
    # Calculate data density
    density_window = Window.partitionBy("category") \
        .orderBy("timestamp") \
        .rowsBetween(-19, 0)
    
    result = df.withColumn(
        "data_density", count("*").over(density_window)
    ).withColumn(
        # Determine optimal window size based on density
        "optimal_window_size",
        when(col("data_density") > 15, 5)   # Dense data: smaller window
        .when(col("data_density") > 10, 10)  # Medium density: medium window
        .otherwise(20)                        # Sparse data: larger window
    )
    
    # Note: Actual implementation would require dynamic window creation
    # This demonstrates the concept
    
    return result
