def run_complete_null_handling_example():
    """
    Complete end-to-end null handling example
    """
    from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
    from pyspark.sql.functions import *
    from pyspark.sql.types import *
    
    # Initialize Spark
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("CompleteNullHandlingExample") \
        .master("local[*]") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPLETE NULL HANDLING WORKFLOW - EMPLOYEE DATASET")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Step 1: Create sample data
    print("\n[STEP 1] Creating Sample Employee Dataset...")
    
    employee_data = [
        (1, "John Doe", "john@company.com", 28, 75000.0, "Engineering", "2020-01-15", "Senior"),
        (2, "Jane Smith", None, 32, 85000.0, "Marketing", "2019-03-20", None),
        (3, None, "bob@company.com", None, 65000.0, "Engineering", "2021-06-10", "Junior"),
        (4, "Alice Wong", "alice@company.com", 35, None, None, "2018-11-05", "Senior"),
        (5, "Charlie Brown", "charlie@company.com", 29, 70000.0, "Sales", None, "Mid"),
        (6, None, None, None, None, "Engineering", "2022-02-14", None),
        (7, "Diana Prince", "diana@company.com", 31, 80000.0, "Marketing", "2020-07-22", "Senior"),
        (8, "Eve Anderson", None, 27, None, "Sales", "2021-09-30", "Junior"),
        (9, "Frank Miller", "frank@company.com", None, 72000.0, None, None, None),
        (10, None, "guest@company.com", 26, 68000.0, "Engineering", "2022-05-18", "Junior")
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("emp_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("email", StringType(), True),
        StructField("age", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("salary", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("department", StringType(), True),
        StructField("hire_date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("level", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(employee_data, schema)
    
    print(f"✓ Created dataset with {df.count()} employees")
    df.show()
    
    # Step 2: Analyze null patterns
    print("\n[STEP 2] Analyzing Null Patterns...")
    
    null_analysis = df.select([
        count(when(col(c).isNull(), c)).alias(c) for c in df.columns
    ])
    
    print("\nNull Count by Column:")
    null_analysis.show()
    
    total_rows = df.count()
    print("\nNull Percentage by Column:")
    for column in df.columns:
        null_count = df.filter(col(column).isNull()).count()
        null_pct = (null_count / total_rows) * 100
        print(f"  {column:15s}: {null_count:2d} nulls ({null_pct:5.1f}%)")
    
    # Step 3: Apply pattern-based null handling
    print("\n[STEP 3] Applying Null Handling Patterns...")
    
    # Pattern 1: Critical fields - Null-As-Default or Elimination
    print("\n  → Pattern 1: Handling Critical Fields (name, email)")
    df_step1 = df.withColumn(
        "name",
        coalesce(col("name"), 
                concat(lit("Employee_"), col("emp_id").cast("string")))
    ).withColumn(
        "email",
        coalesce(col("email"), 
                concat(lit("emp"), col("emp_id").cast("string"), lit("@pending.com")))
    )
    
    # Pattern 2: Numeric fields - Statistical Replacement
    print("  → Pattern 2: Imputing Numeric Fields (age, salary)")
    
    # Calculate statistics
    stats = df_step1.select(
        mean("age").alias("mean_age"),
        mean("salary").alias("mean_salary")
    ).collect()[0]
    
    df_step2 = df_step1.withColumn(
        "age",
        coalesce(col("age"), lit(int(stats.mean_age)))
    ).withColumn(
        "salary",
        coalesce(col("salary"), lit(round(stats.mean_salary, 2)))
    )
    
    # Pattern 3: Categorical fields - Mode Replacement
    print("  → Pattern 3: Handling Categorical Fields (department, level)")
    
    # Get mode for department
    dept_mode = df_step2.groupBy("department").count() \
        .orderBy(col("count").desc()).first()
    most_common_dept = dept_mode[0] if dept_mode else "General"
    
    # Get mode for level
    level_mode = df_step2.groupBy("level").count() \
        .orderBy(col("count").desc()).first()
    most_common_level = level_mode[0] if level_mode else "Mid"
    
    df_step3 = df_step2.withColumn(
        "department",
        coalesce(col("department"), lit(most_common_dept))
    ).withColumn(
        "level",
        coalesce(col("level"), lit(most_common_level))
    )
    
    # Pattern 4: Date fields - Default or Current Date
    print("  → Pattern 4: Handling Date Fields (hire_date)")
    
    df_step4 = df_step3.withColumn(
        "hire_date",
        coalesce(col("hire_date"), lit("2023-01-01"))
    )
    
    # Pattern 5: Add Missing Indicators
    print("  → Pattern 5: Adding Missing Value Indicators")
    
    df_final = df_step4 \
        .withColumn("name_was_missing", 
                   when(df["name"].isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)) \
        .withColumn("email_was_missing", 
                   when(df["email"].isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)) \
        .withColumn("age_was_missing", 
                   when(df["age"].isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)) \
        .withColumn("salary_was_missing", 
                   when(df["salary"].isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)) \
        .withColumn("department_was_missing", 
                   when(df["department"].isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)) \
        .withColumn("hire_date_was_missing", 
                   when(df["hire_date"].isNull(), 1).otherwise(0)) \
        .withColumn("level_was_missing", 
                   when(df["level"].isNull(), 1).otherwise(0))
    
    # Add data quality score
    df_final = df_final.withColumn(
        "data_quality_score",
        ((7 - (col("name_was_missing") + col("email_was_missing") + 
               col("age_was_missing") + col("salary_was_missing") + 
               col("department_was_missing") + col("hire_date_was_missing") + 
               col("level_was_missing"))) / 7 * 100).cast("int")
    )
    
    # Step 4: Display results
    print("\n[STEP 4] Final Results After Null Handling...")
    
    print("\n✓ Cleaned Employee Data:")
    df_final.select(
        "emp_id", "name", "email", "age", "salary", 
        "department", "level", "data_quality_score"
    ).show(truncate=False)
    
    # Step 5: Validation
    print("\n[STEP 5] Validation and Quality Checks...")
    
    print("\nNull Count After Processing:")
    null_check = df_final.select([
        count(when(col(c).isNull(), c)).alias(c) 
        for c in ["name", "email", "age", "salary", "department", "hire_date", "level"]
    ])
    null_check.show()
    
    print("\nData Quality Score Distribution:")
    df_final.groupBy("data_quality_score").count() \
        .orderBy("data_quality_score").show()
    
    print("\nImputation Summary:")
    imputation_summary = df_final.select(
        sum("name_was_missing").alias("names_imputed"),
        sum("email_was_missing").alias("emails_imputed"),
        sum("age_was_missing").alias("ages_imputed"),
        sum("salary_was_missing").alias("salaries_imputed"),
        sum("department_was_missing").alias("departments_imputed"),
        sum("hire_date_was_missing").alias("hire_dates_imputed"),
        sum("level_was_missing").alias("levels_imputed")
    )
    imputation_summary.show()
    
    # Step 6: Business insights
    print("\n[STEP 6] Business Insights...")
    
    print("\nEmployees by Department:")
    df_final.groupBy("department").agg(
        count("*").alias("employee_count"),
        round(avg("salary"), 2).alias("avg_salary"),
        round(avg("age"), 1).alias("avg_age")
    ).orderBy("employee_count", ascending=False).show()
    
    print("\nEmployees by Level:")
    df_final.groupBy("level").agg(
        count("*").alias("employee_count"),
        round(avg("salary"), 2).alias("avg_salary"),
        round(avg("age"), 1).alias("avg_age")
    ).orderBy("employee_count", ascending=False).show()
    
    print("\nEmployees Requiring Data Update:")
    df_final.filter(col("data_quality_score") < 100).select(
        "emp_id", "name", "email", "data_quality_score"
    ).show()
    
    # Step 7: Export results
    print("\n[STEP 7] Exporting Results...")
    
    try:
        # Save to CSV
        output_path = "/tmp/cleaned_employees"
        df_final.select(
            "emp_id", "name", "email", "age", "salary", 
            "department", "hire_date", "level", "data_quality_score"
        ).coalesce(1).write.mode("overwrite").csv(output_path, header=True)
        print(f"✓ Results saved to: {output_path}")
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Could not save results: {e}")
    
    # Final summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("WORKFLOW COMPLETE!")
    print("="*80)
    
    summary = f"""
    Summary Statistics:
    -------------------
    Total Employees: {df.count()}
    Employees After Cleaning: {df_final.count()}
    
    Null Handling Applied:
    ----------------------
    ✓ Name: Generated from emp_id for {df.filter(col('name').isNull()).count()} records
    ✓ Email: Generated from emp_id for {df.filter(col('email').isNull()).count()} records
    ✓ Age: Imputed with mean for {df.filter(col('age').isNull()).count()} records
    ✓ Salary: Imputed with mean for {df.filter(col('salary').isNull()).count()} records
    ✓ Department: Imputed with mode for {df.filter(col('department').isNull()).count()} records
    ✓ Level: Imputed with mode for {df.filter(col('level').isNull()).count()} records
    ✓ Hire Date: Set default for {df.filter(col('hire_date').isNull()).count()} records
    
    Data Quality:
    -------------
    Average Quality Score: {df_final.select(avg('data_quality_score')).collect()[0][0]:.1f}%
    Perfect Records (100%): {df_final.filter(col('data_quality_score') == 100).count()}
    Records Needing Review: {df_final.filter(col('data_quality_score') < 100).count()}
    """
    
    print(summary)
    
    # Cleanup
    spark.stop()
    print("\n✓ Spark session stopped")

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
import time

# Initialize Spark Session with Structured Streaming support
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("StreamTriggerStrategyPatterns") \
    .master("local[*]") \
    .config("spark.sql.streaming.schemaInference", "true") \
    .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "2") \
    .getOrCreate()

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")

# Define schema for streaming data
schema = StructType([
    StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
    StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), True),
    StructField("value", DoubleType(), True),
    StructField("category", StringType(), True)
])

print("=" * 80)
print("PYSPARK STRUCTURED STREAMING - TRIGGER STRATEGY PATTERNS")
print("=" * 80)

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 1: MICRO-BATCH TRIGGER PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Micro-Batch Trigger Pattern:
- Processes data in small batches at fixed intervals
- Default trigger mode in Structured Streaming
- Best for: Regular batch processing with predictable latency
- Trade-off: Latency vs throughput
"""

def micro_batch_trigger_pattern():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 1: MICRO-BATCH TRIGGER PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create streaming DataFrame from socket (replace with your source)
    # For demo purposes, using rate source
    streaming_df = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 10) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("value", (rand() * 100).cast("double")) \
        .withColumn("category", 
                   when(col("value") < 33, "LOW")
                   .when(col("value") < 66, "MEDIUM")
                   .otherwise("HIGH"))
    
    # Apply transformations
    processed_df = streaming_df \
        .withColumn("processed_time", current_timestamp()) \
        .withColumn("value_squared", col("value") * col("value"))
    
    # Micro-batch trigger with 5-second interval
    query_microbatch_5sec = processed_df.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .option("numRows", 5) \
        .queryName("MicroBatch_5sec") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Micro-Batch Trigger (5 seconds) - Processing data every 5 seconds")
    print("  Use Case: Regular batch processing with acceptable latency")
    
    # Alternative: Micro-batch with 10-second interval
    query_microbatch_10sec = processed_df.writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
        .queryName("MicroBatch_10sec") \
        .start()
    
    print("✓ Micro-Batch Trigger (10 seconds) - Lower frequency, higher throughput")
    
    # Alternative: Default micro-batch (as fast as possible)
    query_microbatch_default = streaming_df \
        .groupBy("category") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value"),
            max("value").alias("max_value")
        ) \
        .writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .trigger(processingTime="0 seconds")  # Process as fast as possible \
        .queryName("MicroBatch_Default") \
        .start()
    
    print("✓ Micro-Batch Trigger (default) - Process as fast as possible")
    
    # Let it run for demonstration
    time.sleep(15)
    
    # Stop queries
    query_microbatch_5sec.stop()
    query_microbatch_10sec.stop()
    query_microbatch_default.stop()
    
    print("\n✓ Micro-Batch Pattern completed")
    return True


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 2: CONTINUOUS TRIGGER PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Continuous Trigger Pattern:
- Provides low-latency processing (millisecond latency)
- Uses continuous processing engine (experimental)
- Best for: Ultra-low latency requirements
- Limitations: Limited operations supported (map-like operations)
"""

def continuous_trigger_pattern():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 2: CONTINUOUS TRIGGER PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create streaming DataFrame
    streaming_df = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 100) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("value", (rand() * 1000).cast("double"))
    
    # Simple transformations (continuous mode supports limited operations)
    processed_df = streaming_df \
        .select(
            col("timestamp"),
            col("value"),
            (col("value") * 2).alias("doubled_value"),
            when(col("value") > 500, "HIGH").otherwise("LOW").alias("threshold")
        )
    
    # Continuous trigger with 1-second checkpoint interval
    query_continuous = processed_df.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(continuous="1 second") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .option("numRows", 5) \
        .queryName("Continuous_1sec") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Continuous Trigger (1 second checkpoint)")
    print("  Use Case: Ultra-low latency requirements (millisecond level)")
    print("  Note: Experimental feature with limited operation support")
    print("  Supported: Map-like operations, selections, filters")
    print("  Not Supported: Aggregations, joins in continuous mode")
    
    # Let it run for demonstration
    time.sleep(10)
    
    query_continuous.stop()
    
    print("\n✓ Continuous Pattern completed")
    return True


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 3: ONCE TRIGGER PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Once Trigger Pattern:
- Processes all available data once and stops
- Best for: Batch processing of streaming sources, testing
- Use cases: One-time migration, scheduled batch jobs
"""

def once_trigger_pattern():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 3: ONCE TRIGGER PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create a sample data source (simulating accumulated data)
    streaming_df = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 50) \
        .option("numPartitions", 2) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("value", (rand() * 100).cast("double")) \
        .withColumn("category", 
                   when(col("value") < 50, "Category_A")
                   .otherwise("Category_B"))
    
    # Perform aggregations
    aggregated_df = streaming_df \
        .groupBy("category") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("total_count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value"),
            min("value").alias("min_value"),
            max("value").alias("max_value"),
            stddev("value").alias("stddev_value")
        )
    
    # Once trigger - processes available data once and stops
    query_once = aggregated_df.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .trigger(once=True) \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("Once_Trigger") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Once Trigger - Processing all available data once")
    print("  Use Case: One-time batch processing, data migration, testing")
    print("  Behavior: Processes all available data and stops automatically")
    
    # Wait for completion
    query_once.awaitTermination()
    
    print("\n✓ Once Pattern completed - Query stopped automatically")
    return True


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 4: AVAILABLE-NOW TRIGGER PATTERN
# ============================================================================
"""
Available-Now Trigger Pattern:
- Processes all available data in multiple micro-batches
- Stops when all current data is processed
- Best for: Processing backlog, catch-up scenarios
- Difference from Once: Processes in multiple batches for better resource management
"""

def available_now_trigger_pattern():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 4: AVAILABLE-NOW TRIGGER PATTERN")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create streaming DataFrame
    streaming_df = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 100) \
        .option("numPartitions", 4) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("value", (rand() * 1000).cast("double")) \
        .withColumn("region", 
                   when(col("value") < 250, "North")
                   .when(col("value") < 500, "South")
                   .when(col("value") < 750, "East")
                   .otherwise("West"))
    
    # Complex transformations
    processed_df = streaming_df \
        .withWatermark("timestamp", "10 seconds") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("timestamp"), "5 seconds"),
            col("region")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value"),
            sum("value").alias("total_value")
        ) \
        .select(
            col("window.start").alias("window_start"),
            col("window.end").alias("window_end"),
            col("region"),
            col("count"),
            col("avg_value"),
            col("total_value")
        )
    
    # Available-Now trigger
    query_available_now = processed_df.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(availableNow=True) \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .option("numRows", 10) \
        .queryName("AvailableNow_Trigger") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Available-Now Trigger - Processing all available data in micro-batches")
    print("  Use Case: Backlog processing, catch-up scenarios")
    print("  Behavior: Processes all current data in multiple batches then stops")
    print("  Advantage: Better resource management than 'once' for large datasets")
    
    # Wait for completion
    query_available_now.awaitTermination()
    
    print("\n✓ Available-Now Pattern completed")
    return True


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 5: CUSTOM TRIGGER PATTERN (REFINED)
# ============================================================================
"""
Custom Trigger Pattern:
- Implements custom triggering logic
- Combines multiple trigger strategies
- Best for: Complex business requirements, adaptive processing
"""

def custom_trigger_pattern():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 5: CUSTOM TRIGGER PATTERN (REFINED)")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create streaming DataFrame
    streaming_df = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 20) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("value", (rand() * 100).cast("double")) \
        .withColumn("priority", 
                   when(col("value") > 90, "CRITICAL")
                   .when(col("value") > 70, "HIGH")
                   .when(col("value") > 40, "MEDIUM")
                   .otherwise("LOW"))
    
    # Custom Pattern 1: Time-based with business logic
    # Process critical data more frequently
    critical_df = streaming_df.filter(col("priority") == "CRITICAL")
    
    query_critical = critical_df.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="2 seconds")  # Fast processing for critical \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("Custom_Critical_Fast") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Custom Pattern 1: Priority-based processing")
    print("  Critical data: 2-second intervals (fast)")
    
    # Custom Pattern 2: Adaptive trigger based on data volume
    # Aggregate non-critical data with longer intervals
    non_critical_df = streaming_df \
        .filter(col("priority") != "CRITICAL") \
        .groupBy("priority") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value")
        )
    
    query_non_critical = non_critical_df.writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds")  # Slower for non-critical \
        .queryName("Custom_NonCritical_Slow") \
        .start()
    
    print("✓ Custom Pattern 2: Non-critical data: 10-second intervals (efficient)")
    
    # Custom Pattern 3: Hybrid approach - Windowed aggregation with custom trigger
    windowed_df = streaming_df \
        .withWatermark("timestamp", "30 seconds") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("timestamp"), "15 seconds", "5 seconds"),
            col("priority")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("event_count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value"),
            max("value").alias("max_value"),
            min("value").alias("min_value")
        )
    
    query_windowed = windowed_df.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .option("numRows", 5) \
        .queryName("Custom_Windowed_Hybrid") \
        .start()
    
    print("✓ Custom Pattern 3: Windowed aggregation with 5-second trigger")
    
    # Custom Pattern 4: Stateful processing with custom trigger
    from pyspark.sql.streaming import GroupState, GroupStateTimeout
    
    # Define state update function for custom stateful processing
    def update_state(key, values, state):
        """
        Custom state update function
        Maintains running statistics per priority level
        """
        if state.exists:
            old_count, old_sum = state.get
        else:
            old_count, old_sum = 0, 0.0
        
        new_count = sum(1 for _ in values)
        new_sum = sum(v.value for v in values)
        
        total_count = old_count + new_count
        total_sum = old_sum + new_sum
        
        state.update((total_count, total_sum))
        
        return (key[0], total_count, total_sum / total_count if total_count > 0 else 0.0)
    
    print("✓ Custom Pattern 4: Stateful processing with custom logic")
    
    print("\n" + "
" + "=" * 80)
    print("CUSTOM TRIGGER PATTERNS SUMMARY:")
    print("=" * 80)
    print("1. Priority-based: Critical data processed every 2 seconds")
    print("2. Volume-based: Non-critical data processed every 10 seconds")
    print("3. Windowed: Sliding windows with 5-second micro-batches")
    print("4. Stateful: Custom state management with adaptive triggers")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Let queries run for demonstration
    time.sleep(30)
    
    # Stop all queries
    query_critical.stop()
    query_non_critical.stop()
    query_windowed.stop()
    
    print("\n✓ Custom Pattern completed")
    return True

# COMPREHENSIVE EXAMPLE: COMBINING ALL PATTERNS

"""
Real-world scenario combining multiple trigger patterns:
- IoT sensor data processing system
- Different triggers for different data types and priorities
"""

def comprehensive_trigger_example():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE EXAMPLE: MULTI-PATTERN IoT DATA PROCESSING")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Simulate IoT sensor data stream
    iot_schema = StructType([
        StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), True),
        StructField("temperature", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("humidity", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("pressure", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("location", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    # Create base streaming DataFrame
    iot_stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 50) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("sensor_id", concat(lit("SENSOR_"), (col("value") % 10).cast("string"))) \
        .withColumn("temperature", 15 + (rand() * 20)) \
        .withColumn("humidity", 30 + (rand() * 50)) \
        .withColumn("pressure", 980 + (rand() * 40)) \
        .withColumn("location", 
                   when((col("value") % 4) == 0, "Zone_A")
                   .when((col("value") % 4) == 1, "Zone_B")
                   .when((col("value") % 4) == 2, "Zone_C")
                   .otherwise("Zone_D")) \
        .select("sensor_id", "timestamp", "temperature", "humidity", "pressure", "location")
    
    print("\n📊 IoT Data Stream Created")
    print("   Sensors: 10 devices")
    print("   Metrics: Temperature, Humidity, Pressure")
    print("   Locations: 4 zones")
    
    # STREAM 1: Critical alerts - Continuous processing
    critical_alerts = iot_stream \
        .filter(
            (col("temperature") > 30) | 
            (col("humidity") > 70) | 
            (col("pressure") < 990)
        ) \
        .withColumn("alert_type",
                   when(col("temperature") > 30, "HIGH_TEMP")
                   .when(col("humidity") > 70, "HIGH_HUMIDITY")
                   .otherwise("LOW_PRESSURE")) \
        .withColumn("severity", lit("CRITICAL"))
    
    query_alerts = critical_alerts.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="1 second")  # Fast trigger for alerts \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .option("numRows", 3) \
        .queryName("IoT_Critical_Alerts") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Stream 1: Critical Alerts (1-second micro-batch)")
    print("   Monitors: Temperature > 30°C, Humidity > 70%, Pressure < 990 hPa")
    
    # STREAM 2: Real-time aggregations - Micro-batch (5 seconds)
    realtime_stats = iot_stream \
        .withWatermark("timestamp", "10 seconds") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("timestamp"), "10 seconds", "5 seconds"),
            col("location")
        ) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("reading_count"),
            avg("temperature").alias("avg_temp"),
            avg("humidity").alias("avg_humidity"),
            avg("pressure").alias("avg_pressure"),
            max("temperature").alias("max_temp"),
            min("temperature").alias("min_temp")
        )
    
    query_realtime = realtime_stats.writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
        .queryName("IoT_Realtime_Stats") \
        .start()
    
    print("✓ Stream 2: Real-time Statistics (5-second micro-batch)")
    print("   Aggregates: 10-second sliding windows per location")
    
    # STREAM 3: Hourly reports - Available-Now pattern (for batch processing)
    hourly_summary = iot_stream \
        .groupBy("sensor_id", "location") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("total_readings"),
            avg("temperature").alias("avg_temperature"),
            avg("humidity").alias("avg_humidity"),
            avg("pressure").alias("avg_pressure"),
            stddev("temperature").alias("temp_stddev")
        )
    
    # This would typically run on a schedule
    print("✓ Stream 3: Hourly Summary (Available-Now for scheduled runs)")
    print("   Use Case: Generate hourly reports on demand")
    
    # STREAM 4: Sensor health monitoring - Custom adaptive trigger
    sensor_health = iot_stream \
        .groupBy("sensor_id") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("reading_count"),
            (max("timestamp").cast("long") - min("timestamp").cast("long")).alias("time_span"),
            stddev("temperature").alias("temp_variance")
        ) \
        .withColumn("health_status",
                   when(col("reading_count") < 5, "INACTIVE")
                   .when(col("temp_variance") > 10, "UNSTABLE")
                   .otherwise("HEALTHY"))
    
    query_health = sensor_health.writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .trigger(processingTime="15 seconds")  # Less frequent monitoring \
        .queryName("IoT_Sensor_Health") \
        .start()
    
    print("✓ Stream 4: Sensor Health (15-second micro-batch)")
    print("   Monitors: Sensor activity and stability")
    
    # Let all streams run
    print("\n⏳ Running all streams for 25 seconds...")
    time.sleep(25)
    
    # Display some results from memory sinks
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("SAMPLE RESULTS FROM MEMORY SINKS:")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    print("\n📊 Real-time Statistics Sample:")
    spark.sql("SELECT * FROM IoT_Realtime_Stats ORDER BY window.start DESC LIMIT 5").show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n🏥 Sensor Health Status:")
    spark.sql("SELECT * FROM IoT_Sensor_Health ORDER BY reading_count DESC").show(truncate=False)
    
    # Stop all queries
    query_alerts.stop()
    query_realtime.stop()
    query_health.stop()
    
    print("\n✓ Comprehensive example completed")
    return True

def advanced_trigger_patterns():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("ADVANCED TRIGGER PATTERNS & BEST PRACTICES")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create sample stream
    stream_df = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 30) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("value", (rand() * 100).cast("double"))
    
    # PATTERN 1: Dynamic trigger adjustment based on lag
    print("\n✓ Pattern 1: Monitoring and Adaptive Triggers")
    print("   Monitor query progress and adjust triggers dynamically")
    
    query_monitored = stream_df.writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="3 seconds") \
        .queryName("Monitored_Query") \
        .start()
    
    # Monitor query metrics
    time.sleep(5)
    progress = query_monitored.lastProgress
    if progress:
        print(f"   Batch ID: {progress['batchId']}")
        print(f"   Input Rows: {progress['numInputRows']}")
        print(f"   Processing Time: {progress.get('processedRowsPerSecond', 'N/A')}")
    
    query_monitored.stop()
    
    # PATTERN 2: Checkpoint management for fault tolerance
    print("\n✓ Pattern 2: Checkpoint Management")
    print("   Enable fault tolerance with checkpointing")
    
    checkpoint_path = "/tmp/spark_checkpoints/trigger_patterns"
    
    query_checkpoint = stream_df \
        .groupBy(window(col("timestamp"), "10 seconds")) \
        .agg(count("*").alias("count")) \
        .writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint_path) \
        .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
        .queryName("Checkpoint_Query") \
        .start()
    
    print(f"   Checkpoint location: {checkpoint_path}")
    print("   Enables: Exactly-once semantics, failure recovery")
    
    time.sleep(10)
    query_checkpoint.stop()
    
    # PATTERN 3: Multiple output sinks with different triggers
    print("\n✓ Pattern 3: Multi-Sink Architecture")
    print("   Same stream, different sinks with different triggers")
    
    # Fast sink for real-time dashboard
    query_fast = stream_df.writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="2 seconds") \
        .queryName("Fast_Sink") \
        .start()
    
    # Slow sink for data warehouse
    query_slow = stream_df \
        .groupBy(window(col("timestamp"), "30 seconds")) \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value")
        ) \
        .writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \
        .queryName("Slow_Sink") \
        .start()
    
    print("   Fast Sink: 2-second trigger (real-time dashboard)")
    print("   Slow Sink: 30-second trigger (data warehouse)")
    
    time.sleep(15)
    query_fast.stop()
    query_slow.stop()
    
    print("\n✓ Advanced patterns completed")
    return True

def print_trigger_comparison():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("TRIGGER PATTERN COMPARISON & RECOMMENDATIONS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    comparison_data = [
        ("Micro-Batch", "Fixed Intervals", "Seconds", "Medium", "High", "Most Operations", "General Purpose"),
        ("Continuous", "Milliseconds", "Milliseconds", "Low", "Medium", "Limited Ops", "Ultra-Low Latency"),
        ("Once", "Single Run", "N/A", "N/A", "High", "All Operations", "Testing/Migration"),
        ("Available-Now", "Multi-Batch", "N/A", "N/A", "High", "All Operations", "Backlog Processing"),
        ("Custom", "Variable", "Variable", "Variable", "Variable", "All Operations", "Complex Requirements")
    ]
    
    print("\n{:<15} {:<15} {:<15} {:<10} {:<12} {:<18} {:<25}".format(
        "Trigger Type", "Processing", "Latency", "CPU", "Throughput", "Supported Ops", "Best For"
    ))
    print("-" * 120)
    
    for row in comparison_data:
        print("{:<15} {:<15} {:<15} {:<10} {:<12} {:<18} {:<25}".format(*row))
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("RECOMMENDATIONS BY USE CASE:")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    recommendations = {
        "Real-time Analytics": "Micro-Batch (1-5 seconds)",
        "IoT Monitoring": "Micro-Batch (2-10 seconds) + Custom for alerts",
        "Financial Trading": "Continuous (sub-second latency)",
        "Batch ETL": "Once or Available-Now",
        "Log Processing": "Micro-Batch (10-30 seconds)",
        "Fraud Detection": "Continuous or Micro-Batch (1-2 seconds)",
        "Data Lake Ingestion": "Micro-Batch (30-60 seconds)",
        "Machine Learning": "Micro-Batch (5-15 seconds)",
        "Catch-up Processing": "Available-Now",
        "Testing Pipelines": "Once"
    }
    
    for use_case, recommendation in recommendations.items():
        print(f"✓ {use_case:<25}: {recommendation}")
    
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("BEST PRACTICES:")
    print("=" * 80)
    print("""
1. CHOOSE THE RIGHT TRIGGER:
   - Start with micro-batch for most use cases
   - Use continuous only when millisecond latency is required
   - Use once/available-now for batch scenarios

2. PERFORMANCE TUNING:
   - Balance latency vs throughput
   - Monitor processing time vs trigger interval
   - Adjust batch intervals based on data volume

3. FAULT TOLERANCE:
   - Always use checkpointing in production
   - Test recovery scenarios
   - Monitor checkpoint size growth

4. RESOURCE MANAGEMENT:
   - Longer intervals = higher throughput, higher latency
   - Shorter intervals = lower latency, more overhead
   - Scale executors based on data volume

5. MONITORING:
   - Track input rate, processing rate, batch duration
   - Monitor watermark delays
   - Set up alerts for processing lag

6. TESTING:
   - Use 'once' trigger for testing pipelines
   - Validate with different data volumes
   - Test failure recovery scenarios
    """)

def monitor_query_progress(query, duration=10):
    """
    Monitor and display query progress metrics
    
    Args:
        query: StreamingQuery object
        duration: How long to monitor (seconds)
    """
    print(f"\n📊 Monitoring query '{query.name}' for {duration} seconds...")
    
    start_time = time.time()
    while time.time() - start_time < duration:
        if query.isActive:
            progress = query.lastProgress
            if progress:
                print(f"\n   Batch {progress['batchId']}:")
                print(f"   - Input Rows: {progress['numInputRows']}")
                print(f"   - Processed Rows/sec: {progress.get('processedRowsPerSecond', 'N/A')}")
                print(f"   - Batch Duration: {progress.get('batchDuration', 'N/A')} ms")
        time.sleep(2)
    
    print(f"\n✓ Monitoring completed for query '{query.name}'")


def create_sample_data_generator(output_path, rows_per_second=100, duration=60):
    """
    Create a sample data generator for testing trigger patterns
    
    Args:
        output_path: Path to write sample data
        rows_per_second: Rate of data generation
        duration: How long to generate data (seconds)
    """
    print(f"\n📝 Generating sample data at {output_path}...")
    
    sample_df = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", rows_per_second) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("sensor_id", (col("value") % 20).cast("string")) \
        .withColumn("temperature", 20 + (rand() * 15)) \
        .withColumn("humidity", 40 + (rand() * 40)) \
        .withColumn("status", 
                   when(rand() < 0.1, "ERROR")
                   .when(rand() < 0.3, "WARNING")
                   .otherwise("NORMAL"))
    
    query = sample_df.writeStream \
        .format("json") \
        .option("path", output_path) \
        .option("checkpointLocation", f"{output_path}/_checkpoint") \
        .trigger(processingTime="1 second") \
        .start()
    
    time.sleep(duration)
    query.stop()
    
    print(f"✓ Sample data generated at {output_path}")
    return output_path


def demonstrate_trigger_with_metrics(trigger_type, trigger_config, stream_df, duration=15):
    """
    Demonstrate a trigger pattern with detailed metrics
    
    Args:
        trigger_type: Name of the trigger type
        trigger_config: Trigger configuration dict
        stream_df: Streaming DataFrame
        duration: How long to run the demonstration
    """
    print(f"\n{'=' * 80}")
    print(f"DEMONSTRATING: {trigger_type}")
    print(f"{'=' * 80}")
    
    query = stream_df.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(**trigger_config) \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .option("numRows", 5) \
        .queryName(f"Demo_{trigger_type}") \
        .start()
    
    print(f"\n⏱️  Running for {duration} seconds...")
    
    # Collect metrics
    metrics = []
    start_time = time.time()
    
    while time.time() - start_time < duration and query.isActive:
        progress = query.lastProgress
        if progress:
            metrics.append({
                'batch_id': progress['batchId'],
                'input_rows': progress['numInputRows'],
                'duration_ms': progress.get('batchDuration', 0)
            })
        time.sleep(2)
    
    query.stop()
    
    # Display metrics summary
    if metrics:
        print(f"\n📊 METRICS SUMMARY for {trigger_type}:")
        print(f"   Total Batches: {len(metrics)}")
        print(f"   Total Input Rows: {sum(m['input_rows'] for m in metrics)}")
        avg_duration = sum(m['duration_ms'] for m in metrics) / len(metrics)
        print(f"   Average Batch Duration: {avg_duration:.2f} ms")
    
    print(f"\n✓ {trigger_type} demonstration completed")

# EXAMPLE CONFIGURATIONS FOR DIFFERENT SCENARIOS

class TriggerConfigurations:
    """
    Pre-defined trigger configurations for common scenarios
    """
    
    # Real-time dashboard (low latency)
    REALTIME_DASHBOARD = {
        "processingTime": "1 second"
    }
    
    # Standard ETL (balanced)
    STANDARD_ETL = {
        "processingTime": "30 seconds"
    }
    
    # Batch processing (high throughput)
    BATCH_PROCESSING = {
        "processingTime": "5 minutes"
    }
    
    # Critical alerts (very low latency)
    CRITICAL_ALERTS = {
        "processingTime": "500 milliseconds"
    }
    
    # One-time migration
    ONE_TIME_MIGRATION = {
        "once": True
    }
    
    # Backlog catch-up
    BACKLOG_CATCHUP = {
        "availableNow": True
    }
    
    # Ultra-low latency (continuous)
    ULTRA_LOW_LATENCY = {
        "continuous": "1 second"
    }
    
    @staticmethod
    def get_config(scenario):
        """Get trigger configuration for a specific scenario"""
        configs = {
            "realtime": TriggerConfigurations.REALTIME_DASHBOARD,
            "etl": TriggerConfigurations.STANDARD_ETL,
            "batch": TriggerConfigurations.BATCH_PROCESSING,
            "alerts": TriggerConfigurations.CRITICAL_ALERTS,
            "migration": TriggerConfigurations.ONE_TIME_MIGRATION,
            "catchup": TriggerConfigurations.BACKLOG_CATCHUP,
            "continuous": TriggerConfigurations.ULTRA_LOW_LATENCY
        }
        return configs.get(scenario, TriggerConfigurations.STANDARD_ETL)

def example_ecommerce_streaming():
    """
    E-commerce real-time analytics with multiple trigger patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PRACTICAL EXAMPLE: E-COMMERCE REAL-TIME ANALYTICS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Simulate e-commerce events
    events = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 50) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("event_type",
                   when(col("value") % 5 == 0, "purchase")
                   .when(col("value") % 5 == 1, "add_to_cart")
                   .when(col("value") % 5 == 2, "view_product")
                   .when(col("value") % 5 == 3, "search")
                   .otherwise("click")) \
        .withColumn("user_id", (col("value") % 1000).cast("string")) \
        .withColumn("product_id", (col("value") % 100).cast("string")) \
        .withColumn("amount", when(col("event_type") == "purchase", 
                                  10 + (rand() * 990)).otherwise(0))
    
    # Stream 1: Real-time revenue tracking (fast)
    revenue_stream = events \
        .filter(col("event_type") == "purchase") \
        .withWatermark("timestamp", "5 seconds") \
        .groupBy(window(col("timestamp"), "10 seconds")) \
        .agg(
            sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
            count("*").alias("purchase_count"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_order_value")
        )
    
    query_revenue = revenue_stream.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="2 seconds") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .queryName("Revenue_Tracking") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ Revenue Tracking: 2-second micro-batch (real-time KPIs)")
    
    # Stream 2: User behavior analysis (medium)
    behavior_stream = events \
        .groupBy("event_type") \
        .agg(count("*").alias("event_count"))
    
    query_behavior = behavior_stream.writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
        .queryName("User_Behavior") \
        .start()
    
    print("✓ User Behavior: 10-second micro-batch (analytics)")
    
    # Stream 3: Product popularity (slow)
    product_stream = events \
        .filter(col("event_type").isin(["view_product", "add_to_cart", "purchase"])) \
        .groupBy("product_id", "event_type") \
        .agg(count("*").alias("interaction_count"))
    
    query_product = product_stream.writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("complete") \
        .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \
        .queryName("Product_Popularity") \
        .start()
    
    print("✓ Product Popularity: 30-second micro-batch (trending analysis)")
    
    # Run for demonstration
    time.sleep(25)
    
    # Show results
    print("\n📊 User Behavior Analysis:")
    spark.sql("SELECT * FROM User_Behavior ORDER BY event_count DESC").show()
    
    print("\n📊 Top Products:")
    spark.sql("""
        SELECT product_id, event_type, interaction_count 
        FROM Product_Popularity 
        ORDER BY interaction_count DESC 
        LIMIT 10
    """).show()
    
    # Cleanup
    query_revenue.stop()
    query_behavior.stop()
    query_product.stop()
    
    print("\n✓ E-commerce example completed")


def example_log_processing():
    """
    Log processing with adaptive trigger patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PRACTICAL EXAMPLE: LOG PROCESSING WITH ADAPTIVE TRIGGERS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Simulate application logs
    logs = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 100) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("log_level",
                   when(col("value") % 10 == 0, "ERROR")
                   .when(col("value") % 10 < 3, "WARN")
                   .when(col("value") % 10 < 5, "INFO")
                   .otherwise("DEBUG")) \
        .withColumn("service", 
                   concat(lit("service_"), ((col("value") % 5) + 1).cast("string"))) \
        .withColumn("message", concat(lit("Log message "), col("value").cast("string")))
    
    # Stream 1: ERROR logs - immediate processing
    error_logs = logs.filter(col("log_level") == "ERROR")
    
    query_errors = error_logs.writeStream \
        .format("console") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="500 milliseconds") \
        .option("truncate", "false") \
        .option("numRows", 3) \
        .queryName("Error_Logs_Fast") \
        .start()
    
    print("\n✓ ERROR Logs: 500ms trigger (immediate alerting)")
    
    # Stream 2: Aggregated statistics - slower processing
    log_stats = logs \
        .withWatermark("timestamp", "1 minute") \
        .groupBy(
            window(col("timestamp"), "1 minute"),
            col("service"),
            col("log_level")
        ) \
        .agg(count("*").alias("log_count"))
    
    query_stats = log_stats.writeStream \
        .format("memory") \
        .outputMode("append") \
        .trigger(processingTime="15 seconds") \
        .queryName("Log_Statistics") \
        .start()
    
    print("✓ Log Statistics: 15-second trigger (aggregated metrics)")
    
    # Run demonstration
    time.sleep(20)
    
    print("\n📊 Log Statistics by Service:")
    spark.sql("""
        SELECT service, log_level, SUM(log_count) as total_logs
        FROM Log_Statistics
        GROUP BY service, log_level
        ORDER BY service, total_logs DESC
    """).show()
    
    # Cleanup
    query_errors.stop()
    query_stats.stop()
    
    print("\n✓ Log processing example completed")

        print("""
        
╔═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                          SUMMARY OF PATTERNS                              ║
╠═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╣
║                                                                           ║
║  ✅ MICRO-BATCH TRIGGER                                                   ║
║     - Most common and versatile pattern                                  ║
║     - Fixed interval processing (e.g., every 5 seconds)                  ║
║     - Use: General-purpose streaming, ETL, analytics                     ║
║                                                                           ║
║  ✅ CONTINUOUS TRIGGER                                                    ║
║     - Experimental low-latency mode                                      ║
║     - Millisecond-level latency                                          ║
║     - Use: Ultra-low latency requirements (trading, gaming)              ║
║                                                                           ║
║  ✅ ONCE TRIGGER                                                          ║
║     - Single execution, then stops                                       ║
║     - Processes all available data once                                  ║
║     - Use: Testing, one-time migrations, scheduled batch jobs            ║
║                                                                           ║
║  ✅ AVAILABLE-NOW TRIGGER                                                 ║
║     - Multi-batch processing of available data                           ║
║     - Stops when current data is processed                               ║
║     - Use: Backlog processing, catch-up scenarios                        ║
║                                                                           ║
║  ✅ CUSTOM TRIGGER                                                        ║
║     - Combines multiple strategies                                       ║
║     - Adaptive and priority-based processing                             ║
║     - Use: Complex business requirements, multi-tier processing          ║
║                                                                           ║
╚═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

        KEY TAKEAWAYS:
        
        1. Choose triggers based on your latency requirements
        2. Micro-batch is the default and most flexible option
        3. Use checkpointing for fault tolerance in production
        4. Monitor query metrics to optimize trigger intervals
        5. Different data streams can use different triggers
        6. Balance latency, throughput, and resource usage
        
        NEXT STEPS:
        
        - Experiment with different trigger intervals
        - Test with your actual data sources
        - Monitor performance metrics in production
        - Implement proper error handling and monitoring
        - Set up alerting for processing delays
        
        """)

        traceback.print_exc()
        
    finally:
        # Final cleanup
        print("\n🧹 Performing final cleanup...")
        
        # Stop all active streaming queries
        active_queries = spark.streams.active
        if active_queries:
            print(f"   Found {len(active_queries)} active queries to stop")
            for query in active_queries:
                try:
                    print(f"   Stopping: {query.name}")
                    query.stop()
                except Exception as e:
                    print(f"   Warning: Could not stop {query.name}: {e}")
        else:
            print("   No active queries to stop")
        
        # Stop Spark session
        print("\n   Stopping Spark session...")
        spark.stop()
        
        print("\n✅ Cleanup completed successfully")

def save_trigger_pattern_examples():
    """
    Save example configurations to file for reference
    """
    examples = """
# ============================================================================
# TRIGGER PATTERN QUICK REFERENCE
# ============================================================================

## 1. MICRO-BATCH TRIGGER (Most Common)

# Fast processing (1-2 seconds) - Real-time dashboards
query = df.writeStream \\
    .format("console") \\
    .trigger(processingTime="1 second") \\
    .start()

# Standard processing (5-10 seconds) - General analytics
query = df.writeStream \\
    .format("parquet") \\
    .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \\
    .option("path", "/output/path") \\
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/checkpoint/path") \\
    .start()

# Batch processing (30-60 seconds) - High throughput ETL
query = df.writeStream \\
    .format("delta") \\
    .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \\
    .option("path", "/delta/path") \\
    .start()

## 2. CONTINUOUS TRIGGER (Experimental)

# Ultra-low latency (milliseconds)
query = df.writeStream \\
    .format("console") \\
    .trigger(continuous="1 second") \\
    .start()

## 3. ONCE TRIGGER

# One-time processing
query = df.writeStream \\
    .format("parquet") \\
    .trigger(once=True) \\
    .option("path", "/output/path") \\
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/checkpoint/path") \\
    .start()

# Wait for completion
query.awaitTermination()

## 4. AVAILABLE-NOW TRIGGER

# Process all available data in batches
query = df.writeStream \\
    .format("delta") \\
    .trigger(availableNow=True) \\
    .option("path", "/delta/path") \\
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/checkpoint/path") \\
    .start()

query.awaitTermination()

## 5. CUSTOM TRIGGER PATTERNS

# Priority-based processing
critical_query = critical_df.writeStream \\
    .trigger(processingTime="1 second") \\
    .start()

normal_query = normal_df.writeStream \\
    .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \\
    .start()

# ============================================================================
# COMMON CONFIGURATIONS
# ============================================================================

# Real-time monitoring
.trigger(processingTime="500 milliseconds")

# Standard analytics
.trigger(processingTime="5 seconds")

# Data warehouse loading
.trigger(processingTime="5 minutes")

# Testing
.trigger(once=True)

# Backlog processing
.trigger(availableNow=True)

# ============================================================================
# BEST PRACTICES
# ============================================================================

1. Always use checkpointing in production:
   .option("checkpointLocation", "/path/to/checkpoint")

2. Monitor query progress:
   progress = query.lastProgress
   print(progress)

3. Handle failures gracefully:
   try:
       query.awaitTermination()
   except Exception as e:
       print(f"Query failed: {e}")
       query.stop()

4. Set appropriate watermarks for event-time processing:
   df.withWatermark("timestamp", "10 minutes")

5. Use output modes correctly:
   - append: Only new rows (most common)
   - complete: Full result table (aggregations)
   - update: Updated rows only

"""
    
    with open("/tmp/trigger_pattern_reference.txt", "w") as f:
        f.write(examples)
    
    print("✅ Trigger pattern reference saved to /tmp/trigger_pattern_reference.txt")


def create_monitoring_dashboard_data():
    """
    Create sample monitoring data for trigger pattern analysis
    """
    print("\n📊 Creating monitoring dashboard data...")
    
    # Simulated metrics for different trigger patterns
    monitoring_data = [
        ("Micro-Batch-1s", 1000, 950, 1.2, 0.8, 95),
        ("Micro-Batch-5s", 5000, 4800, 4.5, 0.5, 96),
        ("Micro-Batch-10s", 10000, 9500, 8.0, 0.2, 95),
        ("Continuous-1s", 1000, 980, 0.1, 0.9, 98),
        ("Once", 100000, 100000, 120.0, 0.0, 100),
        ("Available-Now", 50000, 49500, 60.0, 0.1, 99),
    ]
    
    monitoring_df = spark.createDataFrame(
        monitoring_data,
        ["trigger_type", "input_rows", "processed_rows", "avg_latency_ms", 
         "processing_lag_sec", "success_rate_pct"]
    )
    
    print("\n📈 Trigger Pattern Performance Metrics:")
    monitoring_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n💡 Performance Analysis:")
    monitoring_df.createOrReplaceTempView("metrics")
    
    spark.sql("""
        SELECT 
            trigger_type,
            ROUND(processed_rows / input_rows * 100, 2) as processing_efficiency_pct,
            avg_latency_ms,
            CASE 
                WHEN avg_latency_ms < 1 THEN 'Excellent'
                WHEN avg_latency_ms < 5 THEN 'Good'
                WHEN avg_latency_ms < 10 THEN 'Acceptable'
                ELSE 'Needs Optimization'
            END as latency_rating
        FROM metrics
        ORDER BY avg_latency_ms
    """).show(truncate=False)
    
    return monitoring_df


def generate_trigger_selection_guide():
    """
    Generate an interactive guide for selecting the right trigger
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("TRIGGER SELECTION GUIDE")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    decision_tree = """
    
    START HERE: What is your primary requirement?
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │                    TRIGGER SELECTION DECISION TREE                  │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    1. What is your latency requirement?
       
       ├─ Milliseconds (< 100ms)
       │  └─> Use: CONTINUOUS TRIGGER
       │      - Best for: Trading, gaming, real-time bidding
       │      - Limitations: Limited operations, experimental
       │      - Example: .trigger(continuous="1 second")
       
       ├─ Seconds (1-10s)
       │  └─> Use: MICRO-BATCH TRIGGER (Fast)
       │      - Best for: Real-time dashboards, monitoring
       │      - Example: .trigger(processingTime="2 seconds")
       
       ├─ Tens of seconds (10-60s)
       │  └─> Use: MICRO-BATCH TRIGGER (Standard)
       │      - Best for: Analytics, ETL
       │      - Example: .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds")
       
       └─ Minutes or batch
          └─> Use: MICRO-BATCH TRIGGER (Slow) or ONCE
              - Best for: Data warehouse, reports
              - Example: .trigger(processingTime="5 minutes")
    
    2. Is this a one-time operation?
       
       ├─ Yes, process once and stop
       │  ├─ Small dataset
       │  │  └─> Use: ONCE TRIGGER
       │  │      - Example: .trigger(once=True)
       │  │
       │  └─ Large dataset (better resource management)
       │     └─> Use: AVAILABLE-NOW TRIGGER
       │         - Example: .trigger(availableNow=True)
       │
       └─ No, continuous processing
          └─> Use: MICRO-BATCH or CONTINUOUS
    
    3. Do you have varying priority levels?
       
       └─ Yes
          └─> Use: CUSTOM TRIGGER PATTERN
              - Multiple queries with different triggers
              - Priority-based processing
              - Example: Critical data every 1s, normal data every 10s
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │                         QUICK SELECTION TABLE                       │
    ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ Use Case                  │ Recommended Trigger                     │
    ├───────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────┤
    │ Real-time Dashboard       │ Micro-Batch (1-2s)                      │
    │ IoT Monitoring            │ Micro-Batch (2-5s)                      │
    │ Financial Trading         │ Continuous (< 1s)                       │
    │ Log Processing            │ Micro-Batch (10-30s)                    │
    │ ETL Pipeline              │ Micro-Batch (30-60s)                    │
    │ Data Migration            │ Once or Available-Now                   │
    │ Testing                   │ Once                                    │
    │ Fraud Detection           │ Micro-Batch (1-2s) or Continuous        │
    │ Recommendation Engine     │ Micro-Batch (5-10s)                     │
    │ Batch Reports             │ Once (scheduled)                        │
    └───────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    """
    
    print(decision_tree)

def benchmark_trigger_patterns():
    """
    Benchmark different trigger patterns for performance comparison
    """
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("BENCHMARKING TRIGGER PATTERNS")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # Create test stream
    test_stream = spark.readStream \
        .format("rate") \
        .option("rowsPerSecond", 1000) \
        .load() \
        .withColumn("value", (rand() * 100).cast("double"))
    
    triggers_to_test = [
        ("1_second", {"processingTime": "1 second"}),
        ("5_seconds", {"processingTime": "5 seconds"}),
        ("10_seconds", {"processingTime": "10 seconds"}),
    ]
    
    results = []
    
    for name, trigger_config in triggers_to_test:
        print(f"\n🔬 Testing: {name}")
        
        query = test_stream.writeStream \
            .format("memory") \
            .outputMode("append") \
            .trigger(**trigger_config) \
            .queryName(f"Benchmark_{name}") \
            .start()
        
        # Collect metrics
        time.sleep(15)
        
        progress = query.lastProgress
        if progress:
            results.append({
                'trigger': name,
                'input_rows': progress['numInputRows'],
                'batch_duration': progress.get('batchDuration', 0),
                'processing_rate': progress.get('processedRowsPerSecond', 0)
            })
        
        query.stop()
    
    # Display results
    if results:
        print("\n📊 BENCHMARK RESULTS:")
        results_df = spark.createDataFrame(results)
        results_df.show(truncate=False)
    
    print("\n✅ Benchmark completed")

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

spark = SparkSession.builder \\

# Base stream

        "monitoring_config.py": """
# Production Template: Monitoring and Metrics
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
import time
import json

spark = SparkSession.builder \\
    .appName("StreamingWithMonitoring") \\
    .getOrCreate()

# Your streaming query
query = df.writeStream \\
    .format("delta") \\
    .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \\
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/checkpoints/main") \\
    .start()

# Monitoring loop
def monitor_query(query, interval=30):
    while query.isActive:
        progress = query.lastProgress
        
        if progress:
            metrics = {
                "batch_id": progress["batchId"],
                "timestamp": progress["timestamp"],
                "input_rows": progress["numInputRows"],
                "processing_rate": progress.get("processedRowsPerSecond", 0),
                "batch_duration_ms": progress.get("batchDuration", 0),
                "input_rate": progress.get("inputRowsPerSecond", 0)
            }
            
            # Log metrics
            print(f"Metrics: {json.dumps(metrics, indent=2)}")
            
            # Check for issues
            if metrics["processing_rate"] < metrics["input_rate"]:
                print("⚠️  WARNING: Processing falling behind input rate!")
            
            if metrics["batch_duration_ms"] > 5000:  # 5 seconds
                print("⚠️  WARNING: Batch duration exceeding trigger interval!")
        
        time.sleep(interval)

# Start monitoring in background or separate thread
monitor_query(query)

        "error_handling.py": """
# Production Template: Error Handling and Recovery
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
import logging

# Setup logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

spark = SparkSession.builder \\
    .appName("StreamingWithErrorHandling") \\
    .config("spark.sql.streaming.stopTimeout", "30s") \\
    .getOrCreate()

def create_streaming_query():
    try:
        df = spark.readStream \\
            .format("kafka") \\
            .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \\
            .option("subscribe", "input_topic") \\

def run_with_retry(max_retries=3):
    retry_count = 0
    
    while retry_count < max_retries:
        try:
            logger.info(f"Starting streaming query (attempt {retry_count + 1})")
            query = create_streaming_query()
            
            # Monitor query
            while query.isActive:
                if query.exception():
                    raise query.exception()
                time.sleep(10)

            retry_count += 1
            logger.error(f"Query failed: {e}")
            
            if retry_count < max_retries:
                wait_time = 2 ** retry_count  # Exponential backoff
                logger.info(f"Retrying in {wait_time} seconds...")
                time.sleep(wait_time)
            else:
                logger.error("Max retries reached. Exiting.")
                raise

# Run with automatic retry

1. INTRODUCTION TO TRIGGER PATTERNS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Trigger patterns control when Spark Structured Streaming processes data.
The choice of trigger pattern directly impacts:
- Latency (how quickly data is processed)
- Throughput (how much data can be processed)
- Resource utilization (CPU, memory, network)
- Cost (compute resources)

Key Concepts:
- Micro-batch: Default mode, processes data in small batches
- Trigger interval: How often to check for new data
- Processing time: Actual time to process a batch
- Watermark: Handling late-arriving data
- Checkpoint: Fault tolerance mechanism

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

2. MICRO-BATCH TRIGGER PATTERN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

DESCRIPTION:
Processes data in small batches at fixed intervals. This is the default
and most commonly used trigger pattern.

SYNTAX:
    .trigger(processingTime="<interval>")
    
    Where interval can be:
    - "500 milliseconds" or "500 ms"
    - "5 seconds" or "5 s"
    - "1 minute" or "1 min"
    - "0 seconds" (process as fast as possible)

CHARACTERISTICS:
✓ Predictable latency
✓ Good balance between latency and throughput
✓ Supports all operations (aggregations, joins, windows)
✓ Easy to tune and monitor
✓ Production-ready and stable

USE CASES:
- Real-time dashboards (1-5 seconds)
- ETL pipelines (30-60 seconds)
- Analytics (5-30 seconds)
- General-purpose streaming

EXAMPLE:
    query = df.writeStream \\
        .format("delta") \\
        .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \\
        .option("checkpointLocation", "/checkpoints/path") \\
        .start()

PERFORMANCE TUNING:
- Shorter intervals = lower latency, higher overhead
- Longer intervals = higher throughput, higher latency
- Monitor: processing time vs trigger interval
- Adjust based on data volume and requirements

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

3. CONTINUOUS TRIGGER PATTERN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

DESCRIPTION:
Experimental low-latency mode that provides millisecond-level latency
by using a continuous processing engine instead of micro-batches.

SYNTAX:
    .trigger(continuous="<checkpoint interval>")

CHARACTERISTICS:
✓ Ultra-low latency (< 100ms)
✓ Continuous processing (not batched)
⚠ Experimental feature
⚠ Limited operation support
⚠ Only map-like operations (select, filter, map)
✗ No aggregations or joins

USE CASES:
- High-frequency trading
- Real-time bidding
- Gaming applications
- Ultra-low latency requirements

EXAMPLE:
    query = df.writeStream \\
        .format("kafka") \\
        .trigger(continuous="1 second") \\
        .start()

LIMITATIONS:
- Cannot use aggregations
- Cannot use joins
- Cannot use deduplication
- Limited sink support
- Still experimental

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

4. ONCE TRIGGER PATTERN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

DESCRIPTION:
Processes all available data in a single batch and then stops.
Useful for one-time processing and testing.

SYNTAX:
    .trigger(once=True)

CHARACTERISTICS:
✓ Processes all available data
✓ Stops automatically when complete
✓ Supports all operations
✓ Exactly-once semantics
✓ Ideal for testing

USE CASES:
- One-time data migration
- Testing streaming pipelines
- Scheduled batch jobs
- Backfill operations

EXAMPLE:
    query = df.writeStream \\
        .format("parquet") \\
        .trigger(once=True) \\
        .option("checkpointLocation", "/checkpoints/path") \\
        .start()
    
    query.awaitTermination()  # Wait for completion

BEST PRACTICES:
- Always wait for termination
- Use with checkpointing for fault tolerance
- Monitor completion status
- Handle failures appropriately

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

5. AVAILABLE-NOW TRIGGER PATTERN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

DESCRIPTION:
Processes all currently available data in multiple micro-batches,
then stops. Better resource management than 'once' for large datasets.

SYNTAX:
    .trigger(availableNow=True)

CHARACTERISTICS:
✓ Processes in multiple batches
✓ Better memory management than 'once'
✓ Stops when current data is processed
✓ Good for large backlogs
✓ Supports all operations
USE CASES:
- Backlog processing
- Catch-up scenarios
- Large-scale data migration
- Periodic batch processing
- Recovery from downtime

EXAMPLE:
    query = df.writeStream \\
        .format("delta") \\
        .trigger(availableNow=True) \\
        .option("checkpointLocation", "/checkpoints/path") \\
        .start()
    
    query.awaitTermination()  # Wait for all batches to complete

COMPARISON WITH ONCE:
- Once: Single large batch
- Available-Now: Multiple smaller batches
- Available-Now: Better for large datasets
- Available-Now: Better resource utilization

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

6. CUSTOM TRIGGER PATTERN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

DESCRIPTION:
Combines multiple trigger strategies to handle complex requirements.
Implements priority-based, adaptive, or multi-tier processing.

APPROACHES:
1. Priority-based: Different triggers for different data priorities
2. Adaptive: Adjust triggers based on data volume or lag
3. Multi-tier: Separate streams with different SLAs
4. Hybrid: Combine multiple patterns

CHARACTERISTICS:
✓ Flexible and customizable
✓ Handles complex business logic
✓ Optimizes resource usage
✓ Supports multiple SLAs
⚠ More complex to maintain

USE CASES:
- Multi-priority data processing
- Complex SLA requirements
- Resource optimization
- Adaptive processing

EXAMPLE - PRIORITY-BASED:
    # Critical data - fast processing
    critical_query = critical_df.writeStream \\
        .trigger(processingTime="1 second") \\
        .start()
    
    # Normal data - standard processing
    normal_query = normal_df.writeStream \\
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \\
        .start()
    
    # Archive data - slow processing
    archive_query = archive_df.writeStream \\
        .trigger(processingTime="5 minutes") \\
        .start()

EXAMPLE - ADAPTIVE:
    def get_trigger_interval(lag_seconds):
        if lag_seconds > 60:
            return "1 second"  # Speed up when lagging
        elif lag_seconds > 30:
            return "5 seconds"
        else:
            return "10 seconds"  # Normal processing
    
    # Adjust trigger based on monitoring

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

7. PERFORMANCE TUNING GUIDE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

KEY METRICS TO MONITOR:
1. Input Rate (rows/second)
2. Processing Rate (rows/second)
3. Batch Duration (milliseconds)
4. Trigger Interval (seconds)
5. Processing Lag (seconds)
6. Watermark Delay (seconds)

GOLDEN RULES:
1. Processing Rate >= Input Rate (avoid backlog)
2. Batch Duration < Trigger Interval (avoid queuing)
3. Monitor watermark delays for late data
4. Balance latency vs throughput
5. Consider resource costs

TUNING STEPS:

Step 1: Baseline Measurement
    - Run with default trigger (0 seconds)
    - Measure maximum throughput
    - Identify bottlenecks

Step 2: Set Initial Trigger
    - Start with 5-10 seconds for most use cases
    - Adjust based on latency requirements

Step 3: Monitor and Adjust
    progress = query.lastProgress
    
    if progress:
        input_rate = progress["inputRowsPerSecond"]
        processing_rate = progress["processedRowsPerSecond"]
        batch_duration = progress["batchDuration"]
        
        # Check if falling behind
        if processing_rate < input_rate:
            # Increase resources or trigger interval

Step 4: Optimize Resources
    - Increase executor cores
    - Increase executor memory
    - Adjust shuffle partitions
    - Enable adaptive query execution

CONFIGURATION RECOMMENDATIONS:

For Low Latency (< 1 second):
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "10")
    spark.conf.set("spark.streaming.backpressure.enabled", "true")
    .trigger(processingTime="500 milliseconds")

For High Throughput:
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
    spark.conf.set("spark.streaming.backpressure.enabled", "true")
    .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds")

For Balanced:
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "50")
    spark.conf.set("spark.streaming.backpressure.enabled", "true")
    .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds")

1. ALWAYS USE CHECKPOINTING
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/reliable/storage/path")

        logger.info("Shutting down gracefully...")
        for query in spark.streams.active:

        spark.stop()
    
    signal.signal(signal.SIGTERM, shutdown_handler)

9. TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

PROBLEM: Processing falling behind input rate

SYMPTOMS:
- Processing rate < Input rate
- Increasing lag
- Growing backlog

SOLUTIONS:
1. Increase trigger interval (more throughput)
2. Add more executors
3. Optimize transformations
4. Reduce shuffle operations
5. Increase parallelism

CHECK:
    progress = query.lastProgress
    if progress["processedRowsPerSecond"] < progress["inputRowsPerSecond"]:
        print("Falling behind!")

---

PROBLEM: High batch duration

SYMPTOMS:
- Batch duration > Trigger interval
- Queries queuing up
- Inconsistent processing

SOLUTIONS:
1. Increase trigger interval
2. Optimize query logic
3. Reduce data volume per batch
4. Add more resources
5. Use caching for repeated operations

CHECK:
    if progress["batchDuration"] > 5000:  # 5 seconds
        print("Batch taking too long!")

---

PROBLEM: Out of memory errors

SYMPTOMS:
- Executor OOM errors
- Frequent task failures
- Slow performance

SOLUTIONS:
1. Increase executor memory
2. Reduce batch size (longer trigger interval)
3. Optimize window operations
4. Clear old state data
5. Reduce shuffle partition size

CONFIGURATION:
    spark.conf.set("spark.executor.memory", "8g")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "100")

---

PROBLEM: Checkpoint corruption

SYMPTOMS:
- Cannot restart query
- State recovery fails
- Checkpoint errors

SOLUTIONS:
1. Use reliable storage (HDFS, S3)
2. Enable checkpoint backups
3. Monitor checkpoint size
4. Clean old checkpoints periodically

RECOVERY:
    # If checkpoint is corrupted, may need to start fresh
    # WARNING: This loses state!
    .option("checkpointLocation", "/new/checkpoint/path")

---

PROBLEM: Watermark delays

SYMPTOMS:
- Late data being dropped
- Windows not closing
- State growing indefinitely

SOLUTIONS:
1. Adjust watermark duration
2. Check event-time correctness
3. Monitor late data metrics
4. Consider allowing more delay

CONFIGURATION:
    df.withWatermark("timestamp", "30 minutes")  # Increase delay

EXAMPLE 1: E-COMMERCE REAL-TIME ANALYTICS
------------------------------------------

Requirement: Process customer events with different SLAs
- Purchase events: < 1 second (critical)
- Browse events: < 10 seconds (standard)
- Analytics: < 1 minute (batch)

Implementation:
    # Critical: Purchase events
    purchases = events.filter(col("type") == "purchase")
    purchase_query = purchases.writeStream \\
        .format("kafka") \\
        .trigger(processingTime="1 second") \\
        .option("topic", "purchases") \\
        .start()
    
    # Standard: Browse events
    browse = events.filter(col("type") == "browse")
    browse_query = browse.writeStream \\
        .format("delta") \\
        .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \\
        .start()
    
    # Batch: Analytics
    analytics = events \\
        .withWatermark("timestamp", "1 hour") \\
        .groupBy(window("timestamp", "1 hour"), "category") \\
        .agg(count("*").alias("count"))
    
    analytics_query = analytics.writeStream \\
        .format("delta") \\
        .trigger(processingTime="1 minute") \\
        .start()

EXAMPLE 2: IOT SENSOR MONITORING
---------------------------------

Requirement: Monitor 10,000 sensors with anomaly detection
- Anomalies: Immediate alerting
- Metrics: 5-second updates
- Historical: 1-minute batches

    # Detect anomalies
    anomalies = sensors.filter(
        (col("temperature") > 80) | (col("pressure") < 900)
    )
    
    alert_query = anomalies.writeStream \\
        .foreach(send_alert_function) \\
        .trigger(processingTime="500 milliseconds") \\
        .start()
